To understand: Mirissa is a relatively small town to the east of Weligama on the coast of the island, located compactly on the shores of Weligama Bay. Strange as it may sound, international tourism, including beach tourism, "came" to Mirissa only 30 years ago - before this settlement was well known only to tuna, kefali, oilfish and other ocean tasties as the largest fishing port on the south coast of the island. Now all-knowing tourist avenues will gladly inform you that in Mirissa traveloman awaits two exclusive threads - the beach here and blue whales!!! As for the latter: savvy Mirissants in the high season (December–April). by boat take thirsty "Panem et circenses!" tourists to the vastness of the Indian Ocean, where they promise the unforgettable must see in the form of whales (usually - blue, sperm whales and minke whales Bride). We seemed to be getting into this seasonal "fork" - we were in March - but I already had the experience of a similar tourist breeder behind me, when I, while vacationing in the Dominican Republic, decided to fly on the "corn corn" to Samana (peninsula such as this) - there were also promised whales, only humpbacks (Megaptera novaeangliae). There it ended up being a minus four hundred bucks and a phonic killed by a sea wave. So they decided not to mess with Mirissa's blue whales and went to the beach here. First impression: a more “chambered” and definitely more cozy version of the beach “sand village” (Veligama’s syrah). And it's sort of "three-bay": it consists of three lagoons, separated by a rocky block of Parrot Rock (we were in the eastern part). I'm not a beachphile, but Miriss beach really poked: a wide beach line, many fewer people, surfers - count on your fingers, sand, unlike the great, more golden shade with a slight blur of black (I reminded myself of Playa Fañabe beach in Costa Adeje), a "soft" gradual descent to the depths (but be careful with the wave - it's quite treacherous here), the purest water of the turquoise-malachite collier, the greenery of the broad-leafed palms surrounding the beach. Along the beach stretches a number of café-restique-bars, which have sunbeds, WC and showers. After leaving the "other half" to catch Zen and vitamin D, he took a walk in the direction of Turtle beach - he read that there can be seen large Chelonia Mydas (green sea turtles). Alas, like Megaptera novaeangliae in Dominican Samaná, the miracle Green Turtles proved to be a fantasy of tourist avenues. In general, Mirissa, especially her beach, we loved it. I recommend it!!!

Mirissa Beach Review Mirissa Beach, located on Sri Lanka’s southern coast, is a tropical paradise known for its golden sands, turquoise waters, and vibrant beachside atmosphere. It is one of the most popular beaches in Sri Lanka, attracting both locals and international travelers. Pros: ✅ Stunning Scenery – The beach offers breathtaking views with palm trees lining the shore and clear blue waters. ✅ Great for Swimming & Surfing – The waters are generally calm, making it perfect for swimming, while the nearby surf breaks attract surfers of all levels. ✅ Whale Watching – Mirissa is one of the best places in the world for whale watching, especially from November to April. ✅ Beachside Restaurants & Nightlife – There are plenty of beach bars and seafood restaurants offering fresh catches and tropical drinks. ✅ Relaxed & Less Crowded – Compared to Unawatuna or Hikkaduwa, Mirissa offers a more laid-back vibe without overcrowding. Cons: ❌ Can Get Busy in Peak Season – During December to April, it can get quite crowded. ❌ Limited Shade – There are not many natural shaded areas, so bringing sunscreen is a must. ❌ Some Areas Have Strong Waves – While the main beach is swimmable, some parts can have strong currents. Verdict: 🌟 Mirissa Beach is perfect for travelers looking for a mix of relaxation, adventure, and vibrant nightlife. Whether you want to sunbathe, surf, or go on a whale-watching tour, it’s a must-visit destination in Sri Lanka.

Mirissa, a charming coastal town in southern Sri Lanka, is best visited between November and April when the weather is sunny and dry, making it ideal for enjoying its stunning beaches and vibrant marine life. The town experiences a tropical climate with warm temperatures year-round, but from May to October, the monsoon brings significant rainfall. Just returned from Sri lanka, where we stayed for 3 nights in Mirissa beach. We had stayed in Unawatuna on a previous visit, so wanted to try a different beach this time. Having spent 7 days on the east coast, which was off season, Mirissa was nearing the end of peak season and much livilier. We wanted a place on the beach side of the road, so choose Sea World hotel, which had fantastic views and excellent breakfast. We didnt book evening meals, because the daily blackouts meant that we had to choose places with a generator. The blackouts during the day didnt bother us, as we spent most of this time travelling around to different beaches and places. Cold beers and food was always available somewhere. The beach bars and restaurants on Mirissa beach were mostly all open day and evening, and even when the blackouts came there were plenty of candles making it even more romantic. I had heard the road along Mirissa beach was very busy and no footpaths and I would have to say it was really dangerous when we were there, especially at night when there was no street lighting. It really was a challenge to avoid speeding tuk tuks and buses. If I was to compare Mirissa to Unawatuna I would say that Unawatuna is at the end of a small road far from the main road, so much safer to walk around the main street and go in and out of bars shops etc

My husband and I have just spent four days at the northern end of Marisa Beach in a hotel called Number One Marisa. (See my review RE this hotel.) The surf has been constant during our stay here and my husband has averaged two surfs a day, early morning and early evening. There is a main road of simple shops; a supermarket, atm, wine store and a few handicraft shops. Along the beach are several restaurants, and of an evening the beach comes to life with seafood restaurants. Boats and carts stacked with ice and displaying today’s catch ...prawns, lobsters, fish, calamari etc. Just select what you want to eat and they cook it for you. Most of them offer happy hour beverages. At the south end of the bay is an island that is accessible at low tide... challenging but a great vantage point. Tips: Rock shoes for the coral bottom when surfing. Be patient with the language - Sri Lankan’s are very happy people and try hard to please. Tip$$$ ....as their wages are quite minimal and hours of work long.

We had a trip of 3days to cover downsouth. First stop was Mirissa Beach & Parrot Rock. You can easily access to the Mirissa beach from the main road and the Parrot rock is visible from miles. Through the beach you can reach Parrot rock. It is a small island separated from the main land and you can have a mesmerizing 360° view of the sea when you climb up. You can swim in the Mirissa Main beach as well as the best place I found is the small beach situated on the right side of the Parrot rock. there the water is shallow for a long distance. But when you go further there will be rocks under water and you have to be careful of it.  Waves are not very tide. Can enjoy a good evening swim there. Children also can enjoy a good swim there. There are some local restaurants by the beach. We did not go there so not sure about the food & beverages they have and the prices. The beach will be lightly crowded in the evening. But the best time to visit also is the evening, around 3-4. After a 1-2hr bath we went to have a hot tea and to eat something. We found this small place called "Spice Rotti shop" by the main road. It is on google map. the food was amazing and prices also very affordable. They have a variety of sri lankan foods and in there we met some foreign travellers also. They customize your food up to your taste. If you are around Mirissa prefer to try this place. Don't choose the rainy season to visit Mirissa, as the waves will be rough. Mirissa beach is a Must visit if you are a beach lover.

What a beautiful place! Can’t describe it. Tropical views. Postcard! Enjoy the warm water and all the good food and drinks you find on the beach. Good accommodations and beach restaurants. Excellent surfing. Watch out for the reef, rocks and sea urchins!

Tragically on Mon 15 Apr at 2:40pm there was a drowning incident at this beach. The waves were extremely strong, further compromising the normal conditions which feature a strong tidal rip. Assisting with the rescue were two doctors, a nurse, a paramedic and a firefighter. All foreigners. It took ten minutes for local lifesavers to arrive on scene even though they were less than 200m down the beach. Once there the lifesavers stood back and observed without relieving tiring people whom were performing CPR or offering any direction or reassurance that further assistance was on the way. The CPR balloon and defibrillator on site did not function. After we loaded the individual in the ambulance it took a further three minutes for the driver to turn the vehicle around and get it moving towards the hospital. After the ambulance had departed witnesses sought out lifeguards to give a statement; they seemed surprised at this and there was no template for an incident report or recording our details. During discussion one of the lifeguards indicated “today was a bad day to go in the water” but shrugged when asked why people were not being discouraged. I would strongly caution against young children or inexperienced swimmers entering the water here. I hope the individual and his family are okay and I offer my thanks and respect to those people that did what they could to assist.

If you want to swim with big turtles search the small beach named Coconut bay just under the Coconut Tree Hill also named Coconut Garden. We rented flippers from him for around 200 LKR/ person as we had snorkeling masks. He will show you the best place to search and swim with the turtles. We went two times there. This side is the nosiest (closest to the road) and is the best for party bars. In summary - it’s not expensive to eat and drink from breakfast to dinner, it’s safe for kids and pensioners, it’s clean, it’s not overcrowded, the sand is very soft.... what more could you ask for!
Not bad, if you are looking for the experience with lots of umbrellas and cabanas, and people.  It was enjoyable watching the kids play on the beach.

There are several points of interest like and accessible island, a beach where sea turtles swim, you can actually swim with them. Go scuba diving, surfing whale watching. So much to choose from...I’m sad that I’m leaving soon...
One of the most famous beaches in Mirissa. Great place to have a taste of the high waves. Good quality sea food available.
We visited the beach on the way back from whale watching. It's a pretty beach near the south coast which kind of reminded me of the beaches in North Goa.

The beach is beautiful and pretty clean. The waves are really fun for jumping through - especially at high tide. There are some great places to eat and drink along the beach. You can also see the turtles making their journey from hatching at the sanctuary to the sea.

The beach is very nice and clean, the water was very warm (around 28 degrees) and also clean and there were some nice big waves sometimes (that's if you are into big waves). But be aware that it can get very crowded sometimes. We were in February 2019 and until 10 am you had to occupy a sun bed, otherwise they was nothing free anymore until around 4 pm (or you had to be lucky). One thing which i didn't like: all the restaurants (to whom the sunbeds belonged) were telling you at around 4:30 pm-5 pm to get off the sunbeds, because they were replacing them with tables for dinners. I found that they did this much too early ! It was exactly the time when the sun wasn't that strong anymore and it was really nice to lie in the sun and you had to go. I know that it gets dark really fast there, but still , I wish they had begun with this at 6 pm or later. The area around the beach is not nice though. There is a LOT of garbage lying around  everywhere and stinking (especially in the small river, yuck), there is a lot of dust and a lot of noise from the traffic on the main street and also no sidewalk, so you had to pay a lot of attention to the cars coming from both sides. So not really a place to walk relaxed in the evening. The service on the beach is terrible (with a few exceptions). Very slow waiters, you had to wait a lot for everything (menu, drinks, food, even the bill), they forget a lot from the orders and for some of them there is 10% percent service charge already included ( a service which is as I said terrible). But the service and the food is generally much better on the main street than on the beach (we found some places with really amazing food and very good service). So 4 stars for the beach itself, which is very beautiful, but not for the area surrounding the beach or the service on the beach.

Nice beach for goofing around with kids, enjoying the waves. We climb the Parrot rock to enjoy good views and looking on number of crabs. It’s nice but as with all sand beaches with high waves, at the end of day sand is everywhere 😁

The beach is nice, also lots of restaurant options available. The Mirissa area near the beach was not that nice though. Streets were dirty compared to other areas I've seen in Sri Lanka, trash everywhere and when it rained, the streets got pretty smelly.It was not that pleasant to move around. Unawatuna and Bentota areas were cleaner.

Came to Mirissa to see whales (which was amazing) and enjoy relaxing beach time. We knew that the tourism had been developing in Mirissa but didn't expect it to be this crowded. There is still natural beauty left but all beach parties during night (we had to change accommodation away from Mirissa centre to get some sleep), trash and unfinished construction sites and crazy traffic along the beach are not helping the experience.
We enjoyed the swimming, the waves are not too strong, and the people watching during happy hour. Probably a young persons place!
This beach is very clean and well maintained. We highly recommend coming here but just don't expect to have this beach to yourself. Very busy for a good reason.
Such our favorite beach in Sri Lanka . Very nice to see sunset at Coconuts hill. Discovery Secret beach.

Mirissa beach could be beautiful. The water is lovely, the scenery is beautiful, a few great restaurants to hang out in, but... Unfortunately it has a pack of street dogs and some owned dogs treating it as their toilet. The dogs are aggressive and need removing. Some locals bring their dogs to the beach and they are equally unpleasant. Also be careful when the jet skis are out on the water if you are swimming. Nobody is paying attention to swimmers.

Unfortunately we had booked for two weeks here. It became a little too much by the end. If you are young with a beautiful body and want to strut your stuff this is the place for you. Lots of places to eat on the beach, some very good. Jet ski hire, body board hire, wake boarding and plenty of people wanting you to go whale watching or snorkling. The sea can get quite rough with big waves. Not a beach I would say for children unless they are confident in the water . Either side of the beach people are surfing. Unfortunately our hotel was very close to the beach and there was loud music until the early hours. So again if you are young (or old) and that is what you want, then go for it. There was hardly anywhere to souvenir shop only a few tiny shops which did not want to barter, fixed price. To buy alcohol you had to visit the store opposite the Cargills supermarket. You can not go in but have to jostle with the queue and stand at the barred windows and ask for what you want.
The beach is clean, and you can rent sunbeds at the local places. The sea is quite rough. You can order a whale-watching tour from the local vendors.

This was a fantastic beach full of tourists, sun loungers and parasols. Plenty of bars and restaurants. Also surfing for beginners and an added break for experienced surfers at the eastern end. Sadly, this is not the beach for us. Jet Skis in the sea and a seriously busy road that runs the length of the beach. Far too much noise! The restaurants and bars were characterless too. We much preferred the amenities at Weligama Beach but both were eclypsed by Polhena. At Polhena, you're away from the road, it's a reef so there's no jet skis, you can swim with turtles and just down the road is Madiha; proper surf! My advice is to stay in Polhena and take a day trip to Mirissa.

The beach is clean and the sea very warm (didn’t risk the big waves but lovely when calm). Hardly any sunbeds but you can pay them...we prefer to find a nice shack, chill and eat & drink there all day but here you have to pay for food and drinks up front rather that waiting until the end of the day...no trust maybe?!?! The staff already have a 10% service charge so no effort is put in to make you feel welcome or valued. I know we shouldn’t compare but going to South Goa (Agonda) was a 10/10  experience for food, service and friendliness. We don’t travel all that way to eat western food like chips, burgers, pizza, or bland noodles. We won’t be back
Super beach to chill out.. food prices at a moderate charge evenings at the beach are super if you find the best restaurant.
I loved this beach! I had a very relaxing time there. One advice, if you go there from 12-15h better you find a place in the shade, the sun is very strong!

Nice beach close to the city that at times gets a bit crowded. it is dotted with bars and cafes. I enjoyed frolicking among the waves during the day and sipping beer in the evening while watching the sunset...

Unlike other beaches, this one was relatively clean. Also, there is a spot by the coast guard station where there are trees you can hang out under full shade. I spent many days stretching out on the hammock that I brought with me to Sri Lanka. Not to mention it was a beautiful beach well trodden by international hotties.

Mirissa Beach strikes the balance nicely between having plenty of options for eating on the beach, but yet it isn’t too commercialised so retains its beauty. It’s a beautiful beach and the perfect place to head for dinner and drinks when the sun goes down and the candles all get lit at the tables at the various eateries along the beach. There are still a lot of open beach spaces so it’s not packed with tables and loungers, just the right balance. We based ourselves in mirissa for our 3 days on the south coast so we could eat and enjoy the evening life in mirissa and then just caught tuktuk to weligama for the day to surf. The waves can be pretty rough here at Mirissa Beach so not the best for swimming, surfers seem to prefer other bays also.

Really nice beach. Sand is soft under foot, clean and the sea is fantastic. Waves are  can be a little rough so maybe not one for kids but lots of nice restaurants. Ps. Love the comment below from the person complaining the beach is “too sandy” and took 4 showers to remove. It’s a beach, there is sand.....! Thought it was the best all rounder beach i had been to in a while

If you like sand, waves and surfing, is the perfect place to spend your holiday. The beach is breathtaking at sunrise or at sunset(perfect for romantic couples) and it has tones of restaurants and coffeshops to offer. At night(after 5.00pm) you have restaurants with tables with fresh fish, where you can choose the fish that you want and they cook it for you and serve it right away.

Mirissa is fantastic because you will find everything there from wonderful soft sand, bars, clear blue warm ocean, amazing good to swimming along with fish and turtles. We’ve been here with my family twice in a year, and we will be going back again soon.

The beach is really beautiful specially at night time. During day time you can stay in one of the places that offers sunbeds and enjoy the see. I will say the see is rough all the time and it is a great spot for surfing. You can rent surfing board and also you can take surfing lessons. In the evening time you can enjoy all the restaurants on the beach. Great beach.

Not being a beach person myself I have to say even I enjoyed Mirissa beach. There's decent surfing at either end of the beach, a small island to walk up and enjoy the view, clean white sand, decent shallows for young children to paddle safely and great restaurants and bars. Not too commercial and nicely laid back. A good balance.
Nice waves and the view from parrtot rock is breathtaking. Probably the best beach in Sri Lanka (my opinion as a local)

Beautiful clean beaches, with miles of golden sands. Mirissa was not as crowded,noisy or garish as we had anticipated. Lots of food & drink places directly on the beach.  Prices are reasonable and the “happy hour” stretches from 1-11pm in some places. Several shops in the back streets and food generally cheaper there. Lovely rock to climb for lovely views

I really loved Mirissa beach. Nice white sand, beautiful clear water and lots of options for places to eat and drink. The seafood is fresh and the restaurants are open from breakfast until after dark. A great spot, I didn't see any rubbish anywhere.

I am a good swimmer, I usually love the beach, but I could not enjoy Mirissa Beach.  I would usually swim for 3 hours when I go to a beach.  But here I stayed less than an hour.  My fiancée can’t swim very well, so she stayed out of the water.  The waves are unpredictable and can be very high and rough.  I got tossed around like a child by a couple and even got slammed onto the sand by one and my shoulder is still sore days later.  My biggest warning is not about the waves/surf though... after my short time swimming and even going back out to the open water to rub/brush off excess sand from myself, I found that sand had gotten everywhere and it was quite difficult to remove.  I took 3 showers that night and still had sand all over.  When I woke up the next morning, there was sand all over my bedsheets and pillow.  After my 4th shower since my swim, I finally managed to rid myself of the feeling, but I don’t like the feeling of having sand everywhere.  For surfers, you will love the beach, for non surfers (especially those who can’t swim strongly), I would recommend going elsewhere.

The only place i would come back in Sri Lanka ! I loved Mirissa the most. A lot of beach bars, clean sand, international tourists. You can easily rent surfing boards, paddle boards and so on. This place is really prepared for foreign guests
Lots of people there. Plus many restaurants and small cafes. There are 2 volleyball fields to play. Waves make it fun for surfing
big bay with good beach big crashing waves coming  in rock to climb on at one end gives a good view nice places to eat

The beach is nice, with clear water, but the problem are business that are located around it. They are very western-like targeting western customer so there is not much of local Sri Lankan spirit that one can feel while enjoying sun there.
After an intensive trip around the mountaina and the tea field.. Mirissa beach is the right place to chill out and enjoy the sea, fun and beach. Highly recommended 😊
Mirissa beach is one of the best we've seen in Sri Lanka. It was not too crowded and it looked pretty nice. The ocean water was swimmable in January.

The waves were quite big in the main part of the beach and I’m more of a calm water gal. Beautiful stretch of beach with clean, clear water and golden sand. Lots of moderate and budget hotels and restaurants along the beachfront.
Clean and clear water. Beautiful place to just relax and enjoy the water. Many diving center's around incase you plan to take a scuba diving trip.

This beach, lined with restaurants all along it's stretch is one of the most happening places on Sri Lanka. Good food, lots of alcohol, surfing, snorkeling, water sports. U name it and they have it. During the day it's lined by bright umbrellas and sun bathers.. and at night it completely transforms. Trees and restaurants lit by fairy lights.. every restaurant has tables and chairs on the beach with candle light. Fresh catch displayed at every 50 m with a lot of options. It's brilliant! Must visit!!

We're in Mirissa for the final week of our trip and I've been stressing for ages about finding turtles and what beach you can see them near here. Google searches suggested we needed to go near Galle to see them, which was disappointing. But then we were recommended by our villa's manager to check out Polhena beach. We did a little research. Its 6 or 7 min tuk tuk ride towards Matara. We hired Nirosh as our guide after reading some good reviews. It was phenomenal!! Within 10 min we were hanging with turtles. The bay is shallow because of the coral and the waves are far calmer than Mirissa. Nirosh is absolutely sound guy and made the whole thing seem so easy. If you're in the area, its a definite must! You can find him at the Polhena Bay Resort or call him on 077 5481252. Peter

After coming from the east coast where we were the only people on the beach it was a bit of a shock arriving here.  It is busy but no where near as busy as European beach resort.  The sea and beach is fantastic and there is room to find a quiet spot. Great bus connects to Galle
Beach it clean and beautiful, but too many people. For us it looks like Mallorca. Nothing more to say.
Very nice beach with a lit of restaurants! The beach is very clean with a lit of activities to do...
Clean beach with soft white sand. Large enough to accommodate the crowds. Plenty of options to dine on the beach with the waves lapping away at your feet.

Great Holiday Beach nice clean water with a decent wave for body surfing, can be a bit of a powerful shore dump so a bit of caution is recommended. Plenty of lunch options after a swim as well with a few cleansing ales. 👍
Must visit, serene beach... go for lovely beach side experience. Have time to explore around the area..

Lovely fine sand and clear warm water secure its place as probably the finest on the traveller trail around SL. Easy to hire surf or body boards we spent most of our time at the Bay Moon which we felt was the nicer side of the beach.
Simply beautiful beach. Enjoed the relaxing walk on the side. Specifically good in the evening when restaurants put the tables out almost in the water.

Mirissa if fabulous everything you want from beautiful soft sand, clear blue warm sea, bars, nightlife, amazing food to swimming with turtles. We have been twice in a year & will be going back again. There are no 5star hotels just clean, comfortable basic hotels & at silly cheap prices. Best relaxing holiday ever.

Based on all reviews and hype I was expecting a lot more from Mirissa. The main road cutting through the town ruins the beach side feel, although that seems common here in Sri Lanka. Too many people meant it was difficult to enjoy the beautiful beaches. Obviously the main draw is the whale watching but after reviewing we decided against due to sheer number of people boats, not my idea of fun I'd suggest bypassing Mirissa in search for queiter beach destinations.

Spend two nights here and do not regret it! The beach was really good and sandy. At night time you can find loads of bars and restaurants by the beach and with outside sitting. Mirissa beach is a must!
Quite warm water, clean soft sand, nice restaurants around so this is a perfect place for vacations or learning to surf or going to party because there are many young people here. I loved this place.

Unfortunately we did not like Mirissa beach. It probably depends on what you are looking for but we found it over-developed and very close to the noisy road. The beach itself is nice and sandy, lined with lots of restaurants but when we walked along at night it felt like an average european resort rather than magical Sri Lanka :-(

At first I can't decide whether to choose Mirissa or Unawatuna. These 2 beaches is just nearby and u can just go to one place to another by bus. Personally I like Unawatuna more than Mirissa. Mirissa is very popular with Whale Watching. You can ask the price around and I can say most of the boat companies / agents selling the ticket for LKR3000 (discounted price). The difference is only, which agent can give you opportunity to sit at the top deck and also at the front row. I bought a whale watching ticket from Panorama Guesthouse Mirissa with a tagline "money back guarantee" if you don't see a whale. Unfortunately I can't even see a whale on that day and didn't get my refund. So, my advice..don't worry much about the seating places on the boat, there is no promises when u dealing with nature, animals, etc. If you have a short time in Mirissa, just enjoy the beach and skip whale watching.

I was told Marissa was touristy and maybe it is!! It’s a good kind of touristy with backpackers and cool bars with plenty of entertainment! My advice would be to stay 15 mins away which is quieter and cheaper plus you get to do the night time tuk tuk my fav thing!!!
Beautifull beach, amazing sunsets, really cool ambient, good food and drinks, relaxing place for fun. You shouldn't miss this beach!!!

Nice beach but difficult to swim in as the waves are rough. Short enough for a nice walk. Rock area to climb up to see the views. Lots of bars and restaurants with a nice vibe. Lots of happy hours to keep the prices down.
This is a time for indian ocean for whale watiching,surf and many more with sun,sea and aps9 sand.you can get there best experience.

Before we set of for our adventure in Sri Lanka I was torn between staying in Unawatuna or Mirissa so we decided to stay a couple of days in each. Me and my partner visited Mirissa for 3 days and was slightly disappointed. We found that the beach was busy and didn’t look anything like the pictures advertised. The beach is big and wide but I prefer smaller beach with more of a tropical feel to it. Don’t get me wrong if your into surfing it’s great but not so great for a relaxing swim. We also found that the main Road was busy, dusty, smelly with lots of litter. If your looking for somewhere that’s calmer and cleaner I would look elsewhere on the south coast. We did do the whale watching in Mirissa which was great! This was with the whale watching club who I would highly recommend. We also stayed in Unawatuna prior to Mirissa. Unawatuna Beach was just ok but a 5 minute tuk tuk away was Wijaya Beach which was heavenly!  Long and narrow and lined with palm trees. It was also very clean! You can also watch a beautiful sunset here.
Swimming, dinner and drinks. Can’t go too far wrong at Mirissa beach. Service seems incredibly slow for cocktails and most places however.
Beautiful nice beach but too crowded but it was nice at the evening . So many restaurants and great food, good for surfing ❤ So try it you will love it
You will love it... Great place to rest... Good restaurants around... Lot's of good Sri Lankan food places...

Mirissa Beach has got a certain vibe at night with all the cafes and restaurants on the Beach, reminds us s bit if Kuta. But during the day, you see a lot if garbage, some parts are not really swimmable.  Stray dogs roam and there is a lot of construction and broken buildings still happening.  It can get very crowded.
My one month trip really enjoyed place in mirissa beach..nice and beautiful ...I like come again this beach..

This is a lovely beach which is kept clean.  There are many tourist activities available here but I don't recommend the whale watching as it is not very kind to the whales and dolphins.  The beach is great for swimming and the water wonderfully warm.  The surfers at one end provided us with hours of entertainment.
Such a nice place to visit in Southern Coast of the Sri Lanka. Good food in many restaurants in this area.

We went to Fresh Wave 2 times so far and definitely not the last time. The food is amazing and the chef as well as the staff care so much about you being happy with everything. Especially Ruan was the best waiter ever. He offered us the best fish and gave the best advise. We got food, drinks, shisha and amazing company at this place for a very affordable price. The place is at the beach and super cosy including good music. We’ll for sure come back!

this place was a party zone and everybody wants to build a hotel here - its dirty noisy and very polluted - rubbish everywhere. It sucked. Marissa was obviously a nice place in the past but rampant development and pollution is killing it fast - if you want to go the beach find somewhere quieter.
This is awesome beach with great space of sand, and waves are great. Downside is this beach could be maintained better by local authorities as it’s filled with plastic & garbages.

Absolutely loved Mirissa beach, it is gorgeous and stunning. Palm trees and eateries with sand sloping down to the surf. The surf is rough here though, very powerful waves with many crossing over and the steepness of the beach means waves form heading back out to sea as well. Nothing to be worried about but don't be complacent. Lifeguards on duty. Absolutely perfect for bodyboarding with the long waves bringing you right in to shore. Beautiful place.
Unique stretch of beach with eateries right on the beach so that you can watch the ocean, sunset, waves and stick your feet in the sand.
Very nice beach, you can go to not crowded beaches very near and you  have also lots of restaurants and bars, the beach is clean and not too much waves, is possible to swin
Don't miss Mirissa when you are in Sri Lanka. You can walk all the from the other side of the Mirissa to the other side - Palm Tree hill. Beautiful.

Loved the lesser known sleepy town of Mirissa and more so it’s beaches..  :) It’s beautiful, clean and full of activities you can take up or just lie by the hammock and enjoy! Love the soft sand and the shacks by the beaches.. Great for families as well as friends/solo!
Nice sandy beach, could easily swim in the sea, as the waves were not big, sea water felt nice and warm, also good place for surfing
Great in the mornings to bring little children for a walk when the sun is not too hot. A couple of restaurants right on the beach once the sun sets for a great dinner.
Sea is very sandy and there are dogs everywhere. Otherwise its really clean and there are no annoying sellers or touts here. Recommend coming
Nice tropical style beach with lots of places to relax by the sea. Sunbeds, umbrellas and bars. Great way to spend a day or two if that's what you're looking for.

The beach is nice even if not very large. You can reach the water imediately, and there are a few bars that offers sunbeds - you just have to buy something from them. The prices are similar, however, you have to be there early to find any sunbed available. There are moments with big waves and if you don't know how to handle it, the experience it's very unpleasant. The sand is very fine and it's easily carried by the waves - it will be very difficult to get it out of your hair.
Family friendly beach with lot´s of restaurants for snacks, lunch, dinner and sunset drinks. Easy reached from inner town guesthouses and hotels.

I think we had been spoiled as we travelled around central Sri Lanka before getting to the South coast and were treated by fairly untouched natural beauty but Mirissa seems to have been developed for a foreign crowd which made it similar to many other nice beaches in countries around the world. By this I mean the beach has a lot of bars serving overpriced, average food and drinks and has chairs/sunloungers scattered across it. There is still plenty of sand to make your own and the water is lovely. It is very wavy which is fun to play in but if you have kids I would keep a close eye on them and make sure they are capable before letting them loose. If you are in Mirissa then definitely visit the beach, if you were heading there for the beach and prefer something a bit quieter or untouched then maybe look at some other lesser known places along the coast.

The azure blue waters of Marissa beach is a spot not to be missed. The long stretch of immaculately clean powdery sand is flanked by many different eateries, bars and cafes to seek shelter from the sun for a bite to eat. The warm waters of the main beach is quite safe for young and old swimmers alike. To each end of the beach there are two reefs ideal for beginner / intermediate surfers looking to improve their skills but at times these can be very busy so be respectful of more advanced surfers. Know you level and limits, respect the surf line up and stay chilled. There are also a number of surf schools renting boards, selling scuba trips, snorkeling trips, whale watching expeditions and jet ski trips. Overall a beautiful beach but during the on season and even the off season it can be very, very, very busy.

Well, the sea itself is great, maybe a bit dangerous if you are not paying attention to the waves. What I would change? I would clean the beach! A lot of plastic, garbage, coconut shells and cigarette butts.
The beach was clean in December 2018 when we visited, the sea was also clean and only a few jet skis. This is real paradise and lots of great bars and restaurants.

Nearing the end of our trip, we took a bus trip to Mirissa Beach, admiring the scenery of  the coastal route as our driver manoeuvred  the lanes between tuk tuks, elephant transporters and  school buses... it was beautiful but nothing prepared us for the beach in Mirissa. Truly a surfers paradise but for us evening - tripers we simply kicked off our shoes and strolled along the golden sandy beach, enjoyed the quick flowing and ebbing tide and drank the fresh air, watched the sun set whilst sipping exotic cocktails at one of the beach side cafes. Truly delightful.
The beach is amazing. Sand is very clean, so as the water. But be careful with the waves. It is a surf area, so the waves are prety big

Loved it here, surfing and drinks and food all good. Defiantly worth a few days on your trip! There are fish easily seen and titles of you venture in the water with a snorkel and the beach bars can serve some decent drinks!

It’s a very busy beach we just arrived from a lovely quiet village with only 1-2 bars We stayed here last year and enjoyed the choice of bars and restaurants most are very reasonably priced It’s great if you have been off the beaten track which we have for us 3 days and nights is enough here for us It’s great to be a tourists here and loads of choices, after the 3 nights we will be ready to find somewhere a little quieter though Well worth a visit
beautiful beach with coconut plantations so nice  to see. we dive and get a unforgettable experience in the Beach
Mirissa is a perfect beach for relaxing. The sand is the softest I have ever felt and the whole beach is very clean. It’s a good swimming beach and there are lots of restaurants for lunch or dinner.

Great place for surfers but not for children. Bones-breaking waves :) It is very nice place with many restaurants, sun beds... you can rent snorkeling equipment. The beach is pretty long so you dont meet many other turists there (out of main season) Great views.
The beach itself was not that great. Really crowded however the nightlife is amazing.  New Years was fun. There is not much town to speak of.

To say that I hold Mirissa with active dislike, would be an understatement. A half built, rancid, huddle of half built homes, crowded around the A2 main road, reaking of diesel fumes from the thundering, unforgiving buses, lorries and tuk tuks. Get here, watch the Wales, stay as far away from the main road as is feasibly possible and then bugger off to Unawatuna, Iraq, Mars, or back to the cold drudgery of London. Anywhere but here. Do not think you could spend a quiet two weeker here away from it all, unless 'it all' is a war zone or Slough.
Loved it. Kids loved it. Some great restaurants. Definitely an up and coming place. We will be back.

Good luck getting a spot to sit - it is packed, reminded us of Kuta in Bali or the Costa del Sol. Mirissa is a nice place but too many tourists and the beach is geared towards the masses. Sea is quite rough with dumping waves likely to pull you under. Best place to eat is No 1 Dewimni roti hut - amazing.

We loved this beach! Even though our hotel was facing a beach we rented a scooter to get to Mirissa beach every day. The sea is great to swim and just enjoy the rolling waves. Doesn’t have surfers (at least in our 5 days we didn’t see any). The sea is quiet enough to swim but also has some nice waves to make it fun. It has lots of restaurants and shops around.

I even went to Unawatuna and Hikkaduwa on scooter tours, but still I think that Mirissa beach is the most interesting. Go to cliff just of the beach for spectacular sunsets. Right side of Mirissa beach is a party area and a bit of a tourist trap with wild overprices. Go left instead or continue to Turtle Beach. Much cheaper, more tranquil and at least as spectacular views. You can even watch turtles diving for algae near the beach and people, who snorkel with the turtles
If you could combine Unawatuna village and Marissa beach Sri Lanka will have an outstanding destination
Wonderful place to relax good food and great Ocean n fabulous beach ideal place for a holiday and water sports and toatal relaxation

Lovely beach to go and relax for the day. There are plenty of restaurants on the beach that offer free chairs and umbrellas and reasonably priced drinks, especially during happy hour when you can chill and watch the sunset.

It's a nice beach to party animals.one can enjoy variety of seafoods along with drinks, sitting in a beach facing restaurant with loud music till midnight. Normals shops get closed around 8:30 pm. Lively atmosphere around the beach
One of The most beautiful beach in The Ceylon! Perfect for stay on longer time. There are a lot of restaurants And activities.

We arrived on 15. dec. in Mirissa and came by chance to the opening party of the new Restaurant and Hotel „Fresh Wave“ in the middle of the beach from Mirissa. This singhalese food was so delicious that we came on next day again and again. We have been in many other Restaurants but for us this was the best food in Mirissa. The interior design is the best on the beach with an open kitchen it looks luxury and very beautiful. Top Standard! The stuff is very friendly and everything is clean. Super toiletts!! Also the rooms are beautiful and next time we will book here. It was a big surprise for us and it is a real good place to recommend. Super! Super! Super „Fresh Wave“!

The marissa beach is quite scenic but very crowded and with a lot of restaurants who have their tables at the beach so its more some place for seating and drinking than to relax. Alternatively there are two smaller beaches which are called secret beach and and another, which is accesible by the harbour road. These are much more calm and also quite scenic (especially at sunset)

Beautiful beach having a lot of cafes and restaurants offering sunbeds and great food. A lot of companies offering water activities like diving and wale watching  also have small connection booth's on the beach for advertisement and booking etc. The waves are good for surfing if you're brave enough - they tend to be huge and fierce. Be prepared to have sand all over if you try to go for a swim!

So far the cleanest beach I have seen in Sri Lanka! A bit of rocks (with see oursins) on each end, surfers to look at (if you are not one of them) plenty of nice locations to eat, drink and listen to music. Large clean sandy beach to dip in at any time. Very few locals, it is a very touristy, but still nice and relaxing. We loved it!

This beach is a mix of travelers, local cafes along the beach and road side restaurants  with very friendly staff. Just be careful as sometimes the waves can be too strong for swimming; best for surfing.

Sometimes the waves were too big for me so swimming was hard but I loved the whole beach. No sand fliess (unlikely to Weligama beach), some shade under the palm trees, great for walking and watching the sunset. Not too overcrowded and rather quiet. Well, it has a quiet part and also the other one more crowded and noisy so you can choose what fits you better.

Very vibey. Loads of restaurants to choose from. Not a beach for beginner surfers yet beginners can take a 5 - 10 min tuk tuk ride to Weligama where there are plenty of surf school schools and a sandy beach. Prices are on the higher spectrum here. Beautiful beach and if you enjoy the beach with things to keep you busy, this is a must stop for a few days.
Good surf environment with plenty of schools around. The instructors are really nice people that love their jobs.

We stayed here for 3 days in our Sri lanken journey and it was very cool! We were lucky with the sun and temperatures, as we got 30 degrees C and cloudy weather so not too much sunburn. There are a lot of waives so surfers are the happiest. I enjoyed the very warm water and fine sandy beaches

Located closer to the Southern tip of the Island, this crescent shaped beach is one of the perfect places to get away from the busy city. It provides some picturesque views, as well as plenty of restaurants and South coast's signature ROTI joints that sells some range mouth-watering foods. This tropical beach boasts some stunning sunsets and sunrises.
Nice waves for body boarding or learning to surf as you can go out some way and stand in water which is under 1.5m. Beach needs to be cleaned more often.

We visited a few beaches but this one by far had the best chilled atmosphere. Best coffee shops and cafes. Music on the beach at night in the restaurants. Great atmosphere. Clear water. Don’t waste your time at Hikkaduwa go here instead. Unawatuna is also a good place but Mirissa was by far my favourite.
Clean and very nice place to swim, take sun bathes and have fun. Not many people, specially now(maybe because season started not so long ago)

This beach is not too bad. Big powerful waves. The water is refreshing on a warm day. At night time its beautifully lit up. It appears to be cleaner thensome of the earlier posts I have read. In the evening with the restaurants & bars, the place reminds me of Goa. A nice little buzz to it.

Beautiful clean beach, great for swimming and surfing, many restaurants on the beach with great food and very long happy hours. At night it looks wonderfull with all the candles lit on the the tables.
go at sunset and enjoy the cafés along water. there are surfers, bathers and its probably the only safe beach diving spot i. mirissa
Lovely blue waters. Good surfing and diving. Excellent beachfront restaurants. A small main street but all you need.
Great atmosfere and big waves, great music and locals go swimming there as well! Would recommend definetely☺️

Mirissa Beach is a beautiful beach, you can walk gthe length of it, it is not a long beach. The sunsets are amazing, and swimming is fun in the waves. Restaurants open for "Happy Hour" at Sunset and dining on the beach is very beautiful in the evening.

Beautiful sandy beach at Mirissa, quite shallow for some way out so good for paddling.  Plenty of loungers available at the restaurants which are generally free to use if u have a drink.  No hawkers so hassle free, what’s not to like.  Enjoy a cold Lion beer and watch the sunset!
Nice surf point with nice view.Nice relax place in Mirissa. Some parties on their. We love this place for look sunset
It was a great trip to Sri Lanka special Mirissa beach is the Best beach ever We had a good time with my friends And the weather was great

Firstly - surprised it doesn't have a separate entry on Trip Advisor - walk down the beach to visit the Coconut Tree Hill; really picturesque spot. Mirissa Beach itself is one of, if not the best beach I've visited. Super clean, beautiful soft sand, with palm trees overhanging - paradise. Great bay with decent-sized waves coming in - lots of opportunities for fun things like bodyboarding :) Plenty of secluded spots, but also bars, restaurants and sunbeds, but none so busy that it feels crowded. Stunning sunsets too. Amazing place :)

Our top spot for the south west of Sri Lanka. The beach was nice to walk along and while there are lots of bars and restaurants (a couple of touts) it remains ver relaxed and chilled out. A great place to spend a few days.
Mirissa is a beautiful and clean beach! There are a lot of small properties on the beach - either restaurants or shacks with accommodation at some of them. Sunsets on the beach were stunning!

Love, love, love this beach.  It is a beautiful small bay with gorgeous soft white sand and clear water.  The surf was great. From morning till night we just swan, lazed around, ate, drank and did some nice walks along the beach and in the area. The restaurants and bars on the beach are awesome offering great fresh food (including seafood caught fresh that day) and very good (cheap) prices for food and drinks. It's a very casual, friendly and happy place. Staying at a hotel on the beach is a must. Be sure to include Mirissa in your itinerary!
This is nice beach to relax and surf. Nice view and get more freedom on this place.  Actually we loved this place.
Very nice beach with lots of nice bars and restaurants, which becomes very romantic and cosy by night!
We went this place this November This place has nice view. Their has a small rock this is the nice place to see 360 degrees Mirissa.

Slightly crowded beach as compared to other beaches in Sri Lanka. Dint enjoy the beach much as it is quite dirty. Mirissa harbour is famous for its whale watching tours which you might want to try. You might also want to try the parrot Rock bridge , which is the most worthwhile thing to do while you visit this place.

This place is a must visit for beach lovers, lovers, photographers and many more. provides fresh indian ocean water with nice place to rest and take sun bath. Come here with relaxed mind and stay for minimum one week.

Visited here today and its like a bombsite. We were orignally meant to stay here this week but after reading reviews about the destruction of the beach by the Government,we decided to stay in Unawatuna and what a choice we made. Unawatuna area and the beach is amazing. Mirissa is just a dirty horrible beach. A beach if you can call it that, as its about 15 foot wide before the waves hit you. The buildings are almost all demolished and it just looks dirty and unwelcome. It's as if the Government and local people are just willing to let it rot away. Below are pics of whats left of the bars o n the beach, a side alley next to Zephyr bar and a comparison of the beach and Unawatuna beach. Avoid Mirissa!!!

I was in Mirissa on 15,16 May 18. While sitting at the cafe by the beach we could see a crocodile swiming behind the breakers less than 10 metres from the shore. It was there for the full afternoon and then it was seen again the next day in the same area swimming back and forth behind the breakers. Locals told me this was the first time they had ever seen a croc at Mirissa and government officials had been notified. The Coast Guard HQ is down the road and one would hope they would be monitoring the situation. The crocodile was a large adult possibly saltwater croc measuring up to 3 metres. I didnt realise that crocodiles live in the area and did some research. It turns out this is crocodile country. They have croc tours in a river system nearby. Coming from Australia this set off alarms bells and I couldnt bring myself to enter far into the water. In Australia where crocodiles live the messaging is strong that no water way is safe. Is it dangerous? I am not sure. People swim there every day and I didnt find any reports of attacks at Mirissa. It was perhaps a rare once off that the animal had ventured from its usual territory due to flood waters. It had rained alot in that period. However, I think it is important to note and be aware that this is a habitat of crocodiles.So you can make your own decision on whether to swim or not. There is no signage at all to announce that it is a possible danger. When I was there the lifeguard never mentioned this or even stopped people from swimming. It was other tourists that alerted swimmers. I am not trying to scare anyone from swimming at Mirissa I simply want to make people aware of this possible danger because there is no signage at the beach or messaging in tourist information.

To be honest  on this whole trip I (a 25 year old Bristol girl), this was the first time I felt genuinely uncomfortable and on edge by the many young men standing around and leering. My husband and I have been travelling around Sri Lanka, and after hearing several rave reviews about Mirissa Beach, Meligama Bay, Unawatuna Beach, Hikkaduwa etc. we decided to hit the coast. We are not fussy, high-budget travellers however Mirissa Beach is the biggest disappointment I’ve had in terms of any beach I’ve ever visited. The photos you can find online seem to portray what the old Mirissa Beach looked like, before the Marriott Hotel was even built. Since then, it’s been completely destroyed. Rubbish is everywhere - plastic bottles, beer cans, cigarette butts and everything that stinks of careless Western tourist can be seen floating here in the sea and all over the beach (I’ve also seen locals throwing rubbish from tuk tuks - something I never even witnessed in the North of Sri Lanka so I find this particularly shocking). Hotels along the beach cater mostly for backpackers and therefore tacky repetitive Malia music can be heard all. day. long. The sea is very foamy due to pollution and it is less than ideal for swimming as it’s too rough and rubbish like wooden palletts get washed about the shore when the tide comes in. I’m past the age of drinking and partying on a low budget with the exact people I came on holiday to get away from. If you want peace and beautiful looked-after scenery then avoid this beach and the others mentioned above which have all gone the same way!!

You can chose which fish and how you like it to be prepared. We even saw baby turtles hatching two times as there are quite a lot of turtles egg nests buried on the beach (highlighted by the coast guard). Beach is observed by the coast guard) safety). We enjoyed our time here very much.
Lots of bars and restaurants - plenty of shade under the palms. Sea is spectacular with mighty waves - hence all the surfers. A lovely place to relax and unwind.
Beautiful beach but very overcrowded with tourists, day beds and expensive restaurants. Beware of sea urchins and rocks!

busy beach but very pretty. we spent the afternoon here, there are lots of bars and restaurants along the beach front, we went to papa mango which we wouldn't recommend but there are many other options
The beach is nice but full of tourists. If you like to have Company and a wview beers on the beach, this is the place to go. It is quite clean and nice to hang out there

Great place to relax! Clean fine sand, not so wild waves in the middle, nice bars and restaurants, not crowded. And what the beautiful sunsets you can look at while sipping a cocktail few meters away from the ocean!

A fantastic beach in the shape of a cove almost. The sand is golden and the water is clear. As previously mentioned by many the waves are quite big on the left side so if you are not a strong swimmer stick to the right side of the beach where the water is a lot calmer. Lots of beach bars to grab a drink or some food.

Very nice beach: yellow sand, some shadow places for relax, nice waves, many good restaurants. We stayed in Mirissa for 4 nights and after visiting Unavatuna we decided to back to Mirissa to stay 6 night more, because we liked this beach so much.
Long clean beach with a few little restaurants beside it.  Very few people seem to use it I think because the currents can be a bit strong at times?
Mirissa beach is a gem. We went there during shoulder season and it was not overcrowded at all. There is a small stretch of mangrove trees in the middle where you can chill for free in the shade.
Mirissa beach is very nice. There are many bars restaurant and accommodation. We stay there on March. Beach was quite. Only few turists.  Recommend

Mirissa Beach is loaded with restaurants, tour groups, ocean activities and people. It is a great way to spend a day at the beach or at night. I went with my family to have lunch after diving, and spent several hours hanging out and boogie boarding. We came again a separate night and had dinner on the beach with fresh catch of the day. It was honestly some of the best fish I have ever had.

One of the few clean beautiful beaches I've been to. The local businessmen make sure the area is clean and nobody bothers you when you are relaxing on the beach. Caught the sunset and the nightlife is simply splendid. We were lucky enough to dine at a Wednesday special restaurant joint who had fireworks and a bonfire going on that night. Perfect place for a getaway.
Nice beach with a lot of resturants. Big wawes and plenty of room for everyone. Be careful with small kids due to the streams and wawes.
OK beach with a number of bars/restaurants. Great for whale watching and backpackers. Otherwise not exceptional

Beach restaurant Nishan Sri Lanka looks Nice but completely uninterested staff ! They do not care at all! Food was cold , when I Said This at the end , the waiter said oh? And walked away. Much nicer and better beach restaurants nearby!

Spent a day and a half at Marissa. The beach is beautiful, one of the best I’ve been on. Plenty of places to eat. It not in your face. No sellers, free to walk along beach undisturbed. Sand really soft. Activities available. Only downside is there are a couple of areas where there is rubbish, those are set back from main beach but still there.

Brilliant beech during the day to sun bath & people watch. Brilliant beech for a multitude of restaurants serving fresh sea food all severd al- fresco. what else do you want for your money. Gets my vote.

Beach in Mirissa is so nice. Beautiful view and clean. You can find there a lot of bars and restaurants, where during the evenings (sometimes even days!) you can join to nice party. The minus for me is fact that beach is not too big, so very crowded during the seasons. It's difficult to find quite place to chill.

Nice, clean beach where a lot of tourists are.  Very pretty at night too. There's a little cliff where you can climb and see the whole area. A lot of restaurants by the beach side. Nice beach to swim and surf.

This is a really good family beach, lovely sand, generally calm waters but can pick up a bit late afternoon. There are plenty of bars and restaurants lining it but not too many and of course central and a sunset to boot.
Can't say a bad word. First time I thought there will be a hundreds of tourist but it was fine. Water is clear, great waves, it's fun. Will be missed.
Mirissa beach is one of my top favourite beaches in SL. A perfect weekend getaway after a stressful week!

Watch anything when swimming,- it’s OCEAN! But if you want to splash with little children then there is place at the left side of the beach  behind the headland. There some beach boys sitting nearby usually so you can find it with ease. Watch your steps - there are big underwater rocks. And there is a small local cafe near with relatively chip prices. Enjoy. if you are not a snob, it's just fine.

We had read great things about Mirissa and were looking forward to having some quality beach time for the final week of our 3 week trip around Sri Lanka. What a mistake. Mirissa is a dirty dump. The beach that everyone raves about, is covered in plastic chairs from ramshackle bars, which offer no charm. We saw a cockroach in one.The vibe was Benidorm not beautiful. I wouldn’t have been surprised to see egg and chips on the menu and yesterday’s Daily Mail being read by overweight, leathery chested Brits abroad. Most accommodation is behind the beach and seems to have been thrown up without a thought. Rubbish is being burnt in the streets and the rivers are full of litter. It is the WORST place we stayed in Sri Lanka. Do yourselves a favour and go to Tangalle or Talalla. We didn’t go to Unawatuna or Weligama, as we had been put off by stories of overcrowded beaches, but driving past in a tuk tuk on our way to Galle, they looked like paradise compared to Mirissa. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. MIRISSA IS A TOILET

We enjoyed walking along the beach front  and were able to walk along through 2 smaller bays into the larger beach. Never seemed overcrowded. The sea has potential to give you a bit of a battering my daughters loved it however Turtle Bay has much calmer waters.
Lovely beach stretching out in a bay. Quieter at each end. Good to swim play and snorkel.  Nice relaxing eateries.
Nice atmosphere, restaurants along the beach with tables almost in the ocean, many different hotels to choose between. Best restaurants SALT and TYPHON.
It's a nice beach with plenty of food and drink options not to far from the shore line. It's a great place for family, friends or couples to hang out.

Let the mass lie on the beach in Merissa, no more than 5 minutes from Merissa you will find the secret beach. What's interesting about it is that everyone talks about it, but nobody goes there. This beach is for pure relaxation no surfing just a resturant and a wonderful place to just be on. Here it's great to snorkel Do not pay more than 200 with tuk tuk to come here. Walk home to Mirissa in 25 minutes. Then You are ready for a lovely dinner at the beach in Merissa.
Nice beach but taken over by hordes of foreigners and businesses catering for them
With all the fantastic beaches that the southern coast of Sri Lanka had to offer, this one just dossen't cut it. Too many people. Too much turists.
Beautiful beach, not much of a party place. Great vibes, food and all the Sri Lanka people smiling around.
Nice beach to chill out on or go swimming. Not the best for beginner surfers as the waves are short and dumpy. There is a reef break but only go surfing there if you are experienced.

Mirissa is a coastal town bisected by the busy east/west link road. Of interest is the busy fishing port with its jumble of colourful fishing boats. Apart from the whale watching, which seems to be its other main attraction, there really isn’t much to do here. There is an attractive and clean beach, which by day is a centre for surfers and sun lovers. There are lots of young families here too. In the evenings the tables and chairs come out onto the beach in front of hotels, along with fresh fish sellers who offer a nice fresh fish for supper. Quite expensive at about 1500-2000 rp. My mistake was in coming here I wanted to be lulled to sleep at night by the swoosh of the surf. No... at 10.30, music started from a nearby hotel or bar. A deep thumping base that punctuated the minutes throughout the night until 5.30am when at last it stopped. After 2 sleepless nights I am so glad to be moving on. I wouldn’t recommend Mirissa for tranquility. It’s a shame. The people of Mirissa should be careful what they wish for.
Great place to chill very clean and sandy beach large selection of eateries but don’t go to Barracuda over priced but nothing big about it

Very nice beach, long stretch of soft white sand with turquoise clear waters. Able to swim. Lots of wonderful restaurants that serve delicious seafood and all have good beer and cocktail happy hours. Beach party at 1 restaurant every night- fun if that's what you want to do and didn't notice a disturbance from it if not attending. Would recommend Mirissa over unawatuna. Lots of sun loungers along beach you can use for free or purchase of drink.

Not as busy or touristy as the guide books make out. Lots of space for sunbathing and also restaurants etc. The sea was warm but quite rough so be careful if you go in. If you want a quieter part of the beach, then head to the north side near Papa Mangos.
A great strip, super clean and not so busy. Recommended to see after having seen some other like delawalla and Tangalle.
Beautiful beach and amazing sunsets. Go to the big rock to have a view of the whole beach which is stunning.

It is a nice beach and water is clean. There are big waves for surfing. Though there are many resturant which people can have dinner on the beach, we found the beach is very clean. Also a good spot to watch sunset. We stayed days in Mirissa beach and should have stayed longer.

We visited Mirissa on 10th February and spent 3 days on the beach. The beach is great for swimming , surfing or simply enjoying tha sand sun and the sea. The little island just adds to the beauty of the beach. And watching sunset from that island is an experience to savour.

A great beach for swimming and chilling. A long beach with not too many people, not very crrowded, well enough room for everyone to feel comfortable. Swimming conditions are great and the sand is nice and soft.

If you like crowded, noisy beaches with European   prices and attractions, food that would be considered "acceptable" at best in Europe, full of people from your home town, BUT available during European winter, when very similar beaches in Spain or Italy are too chilly, this place is for you. Otherwise, I would recommend more peaceful places, for example around Tangalle.

We stopped here for a couple of days as we wanted to go whale watching. The beach itself is quite nice but can get very busy, looking around you feel you have missed the boat and now it's just full of expensive restaurants preying on tourists. Come the evening the beach is filled with dining tables and chairs. We stayed to have a drink on the beach and had to wait half an hour for 2 beers to arrive, there are better places to eat away from the beach. It's worth a visit for a day or two but there are nicer beaches on the south coast.

Mirissa isn’t pristine and has some litter. There are lots of good breaks for surfers but we suggest you go further south or on the east ,less populated side of the island. Paradise has been lost here! Russians love it here!

We have had a few beautiful meals but each time upon paying they tell us we cant use our credit card depite a sign being 10 feet away that we can. We love the view, the locals working there and the food but not so much the response we get from the Irish woman as the head honco. Dont let us order 3 bottles of wine and tell us to find a  atm.  You let the see sri lankans down

Mirissa is a nice beach with clear water and many activities around. The beach is not that crowded and is isolated from the busy road by restaurants and bars. Make sure to come early enough to get a sundbed and an umbrella. They are for free provided that you have some drinks at the bar. The bars start to take away the umbrellas and sunbeds quite early - around 4:30pm - to prepare tables and chairs for the dinner time. This is kind of annoying as a guy is standing behind your back waiting for you to stand up and leave the sunbed. However, after sunset the beach turns into a romantic place to have dinner with many candles, lovely food and even fireworks. There are some surfing schools on the beach but I would prefer Weligama for surfing.

The sunset views are magnificent, but that's the only thing I really liked about Mirissa beach. Anyway, it's worth it to visit it if you've come to Mirissa for whale watching. It was quite crowded there, but everyone got enough space, so I wouldn't say it was packed. There's plenty of bars along the beach, we were staying at the guest house just across the road from the beach and our sleep was disturbed by the loud music being played at those bars all night long. Btw, all the restaurants serve pretty much the same food, they sell it for the same prices, and the food was OK, nothing to remember and nothing to complain about. The beach itself is clean but the entrance to it wasn't, there were some storks that couldn't resist a garbage dump feast. I'd better opt for Tangalle.
It’s a picturesque place. Great restaurants along the beach. It’s a great one for not more than a week. However, you have a few more options around- turtles, elephants, temples not far away.
even though touristy -this beach is amazing and crystal clear. Not huge waves for anyone that is not confident of swimming. Also a lot of cafes and bars!
Very busy with tourists in the main beach area. Beat to stay in the east end. Good surf break though when working

Rough but warm sea, enough room for everyone, many restaurants and cafes and sound of crashing waves- sounds and is like a dream. ..until the horrible and way too loud technowhatever music starts in the evening in one of the restaurant/cafes and ruins it all. No more peace, just thumping music. So if you are planningto stay in a hotel on the beach, think twice!

We walked down to the beach on our first night in Mirissa. The main strip is a mixture of restaurants and bars with seating on the beach. Get off the road and onto the beach as soon as possible. You can walk through most the beachfront restaurants and it’s much prettier, quieter and safer (especially at night) than the main road!! There are about 20 or so venues along the beach. Most offering fresh fish and happy hours which seen to last all day!! The food seemed much of a muchness but the atmosphere was great. When lite up at night the beach looks really nice with twinkling lights from the restaurants reflecting in the ebbing tide. There are couple of venues with disco lights and music which seems to ruin the relaxed vide some what but if that’s not your thing you can easily escape this by going a little further down the beach, the sound of the waves quickly drowns out the neighbouring noise. Although probably not the idyllic undiscovered place it once was of old it is a must even if just for a stroll along the beach to soak up the atmosphere or for a quick drink whilst listening to the waves and feeling the sand under your feet.

Top tip, beach boys are banned from here so you can relax in peace... unless you lose concentration whilst swimming and get nailed by massive waves... which is great to watch! Beach bars are excellent as well

Was here for a few days and spent a lot of time down here under the trees, be careful of the strong waves coming in though it can be fun to watch others get slammed. You will see a lot of turtle nests at the top of the beach and if you come at night you may be lucky enough to see the turtles hatching in the wild.

Mirissa Beach is great, very nice atmosphere, you can relax during the day and go party in the night time if you're in the mood. Besides the beach is super beautiful, I loved it there. Nice waves to play around 😀

I visited here in September which is low season and rainy season for this area. I walked across it and tbh it was nothing special, it's not huge but wasn't the cleanest either. I don't know if it's a lot better when the weather is better. It's not worth visiting Mirissa just for this.

The beach itself is pretty and good for swimming and watching the sunset. However, we found the town and the area you have to walk to to get to the beach not so nice- there is a stinky sewer and quite a lot of rubbish in general. I would recommend mirissa beach as a day trip if you are in the area, but not staying in mirissa for a few days. Mirissa seems like the sort of place that would have been a chilled beach spot  five years ago but sadly mass tourism has changed it for the worse.
In just a few years this beautiful beach has been spoilt by too many restaurants with plastic chairs, rubbish and jet skis. It's still fun for swimming.

We were initially disappointed with Mirissa as it felt dirtier on the streets than other places we visited. It turned out that we really enjoyed the beach which had ample bars and restaurants. The beach itself is clean but the entrance to it wasn't. Great waves but do watch yourself as they break on what is a very shallow depth - no end of people getting slammed into the seabed and we did see one guy sadly dislocate his shoulder. Watch your kids as they go in, but with a bit of cautiousness, you can really enjoy the sea. There seems to always be one bar at night which opens late and generally you can see where the party is happening because they set the fireworks off at about 9:30 pm.
Amazing beach with a variety of great restaurants!! Clean and spacious...If your are lucky you even may see a turtle laying eggs or little ones hatching.  Magical place.
It's very nice beach for family,  really good for children also there are many beach restaurant to have food at the beach. Also we have gone for weals watching was really good experience

Great clear water, waves and no undertow. This is a sandy beach with lots of restaurants that offer beach lounges, food and drink to wile away your day swimming and sunning. The vibe is laid back and the water is truly wonderful. Great also for families with small children.

Our second visit to Mirissa & the beach is still great. Lovely to have a beer or cocktail & watch the sunset. We don’t tend to eat on the beach as it’s overpriced and we’ve found better food away from the beach/hoards of tourists. The beach is clean but the waves are rough. If you walk along the beach, past Mirissa rock for five mins you’ll come to a bar called Papa mango. Great food & sun loungers plus it’s in a little bay where the water is calmer, perfect for swimming.

Loved this beach! Yes it is getting more touristy but the water is just so beautiful and clean. I would highly recommend a stay here. There is some rubbish they should clean near the roads but the actual beach is very clean.
Perfect beach. Best of both worlds: sand and places to crash & nice small restaurants and bars. Both within walking distance of eachother.
Everything is nice here. The view, the send and waves are not too big for kids. Big ocean line so you can find a good place for you

Mirissa is still somehow romantic. Some touristic bad karma will come, but probably for 1-2 years one can still enjoy the nature and the atmosphere of chill, cool and unwind place. I got to surf 🏄‍♀️ for the first time, I did yoga on a beautiful spot up on a hill, had great food still at affordable prices. Super experience!
This is the best beach for relax . best for whales & dolphin watching. paradise beach club is the best restaurant . North side of The beach There is nice rock called giragalla to climbing. best

We dropped by for a day around four years ago, fell in love with the place, and determined to come back some day for a week. It didn't disappoint. Lovely sandy beach to wander up and down on, loads of beach bars and restaurants, and a very relaxed atmosphere throughout. A little slice of holiday paradise.
We went to this beach for breakfast after a whale tour in Mirissa. It’s smallish but not crowded. Mainly young crowd. Lovely water for swimming without the waves further along the coast.

I first visited this beach in 2006,it only had a few places to stay at the the right hand side looking at ocean,can't believe the change since then this is by far the most touristy beach I've seen in Sri Lanka,it is lovely but unfortunately it's still a place where turtles come to lay there eggs,this happened last night one came onto the beach with all the tourists,bars and lights full power plus music,and tried to lay it's eggs but this was never going to happen,even if it did how would the eggs survive!I've been to a few beach's around the world late at night and watched these amazing creatures struggle up the beach,and lay there egg,with a warden there to safeguard there incubation,happy knowing that another generation off turtles will be reproduced, unfortunately last night watching that green turtle struggling to get back into the ocean without laying a single egg I felt really really sad that yet again tourism takes over from nature once again

Great for versatile beach stroll - the little island, walking track by the beach, swimming and other water activities, cozy seafood restaurants for dinner. Compared to some other beaches there were no hotels blocking at the beach and that made it more open nice space for everyone.

Mirissa beach is a beautiful cove beach with lovely sand and possibly not as dangerous as some other beaches for taking a dip. It would be the perfect beach but it has been taken over by bar after bar competing with each other for numbers of sunbeds and volume of music.  We found a little oasis of quiet and calm at paradise beach club that for 500 rupees you can use their beds and pool.

I honestly mean this when I say this is one of the nicest beaches I have been to in a long time. I have walked pretty much the full stretch of it and although the sea is rougher to the far right, it is much more picturesque and the waves are perfect for surfing. It's pretty clean as well which I was very happy to see. I actually saw workers in the morning collecting rubbish off the beach. Bravo Mirissa!!
Nice beach road behind can be a bit scary lots going on food drink surfers don't bother you if you don't bother them

Change is good, they say. When speaking about Mirissa beach, that's true. When we first came here six years ago, there was just two big hotels and a few shacks/restaurants by the beach. Well... Things were quite different this time. But better in a way. More choice of restaurants. Some really good, offering a bigger range of food. Some just for a drink. And of course, each one will find its perfect spot to relax, sunbathe, unwinded and dip in the sea. Nevertheless, at daylight Mirissa beach offers different atmospheres. Facing the sea, the last third left side is bordered by the main road. More noisy and dirty then. The middle part is the sunniest. Lots of sunbeds and umbrellas. Our favourite one was at the far right. A shady spot by a rocky creek probably best known as the surfers corner as it is the entry point to catch the waves. There's a lovely restaurant and sunbeds.

I read a lot of travel blogs before our trip and just over 2 years ago Mirissa was quiet and unfound by tourists. Well.... Not anymore. Unfortunately so. In the daytime all is absolutely fine. A beautiful, quite small beach with great waves. Not too crowded. Sure maybe too many restaurants, but that is not a big problem. At least you can have lunch at a different place every day. When the sun goes down, it seems to be partytime every night. There is a proper beach party at some reastaurant every night with lights and fire works...... Most of the places has the music nightclub level even though they're places for dining. This is really tragic. Not the Sri Lankan bliss I was looking forward to. The third night was the most we could take and moved on to Galle. Only two quiet restaurants on Mirissa Beach, Kama and Zephyr, but they had their own problems.

At night it's all pit up with amny shacks to eat and drink. It's very clean and the ambience is mind blowing. At night there will be a beach party which is a must to attend if you like to enjoy. The beach is not for surfing but good to dip in. The view from parrot island is amazing.
Have spent 3 days resting on this beach,its was absolute peace, clear waters ,no much crowd, this beach and surrounding beaches  are good for surfing...
