If you go to to srilanka you should see here.You must absolutely eat seafood in the restaurants on the beach in the evening.
The beach is very clean and beautiful. The water is so very transparent that we can see the fishes from the top. The atmosphere at the beach is very vibrant. A very good place to unwind yourself.
Very clean beach with many restaurants to suite your taste. Visit the parrot island as well! It’s just on the beach/at the end of it.
If ur young and want to party probably great but if your like me and over 60 Do Not Take a Place on the Beach. Dumpy Dump music starts at 10and goes on until 5am. You cannot get away from it. Awful

This is a decent sandy beach with lots of restaurants. We went there two days after the full moon day and the sea was rough. Still we went for a bath. This beach was packed with people. Some were water skating. There is a little island close to the beach and it is worth trying to reach it. Try not to do this when the sea is rough.

It was nearly 40-45 minutes journey from our hotel. we stayed at koggala. early in the morning we have visited this site specifically to watch dolphins. after reaching here, different boat riders has approached to us..for dolphin ride.. its better to visit early in the morning. we found boat riders having good skill. kids can enjoy also.
This beach is gorgeous loads of beach bars and at night they all put tables and chairs on the sand which is nice. The sea is lovely and warm the sand so soft

I visited this beach with my son and walked along with him. While as an experience it was good I could not say very good so have rated it average. The sand and cleanliness I am used to in West Australia frankly is a lot better. Having said that the water was very pleasant and there was surf. There were also many very reasonable priced surf schools were you could get lessons form under $20/hr share and hire a board for a ridiculously cheap just over $2 an hour Aust. There are also plenty of cheap food and drink options All in all worth going to, but falls short compared to home- which of course is purely my opinion.

Clean and empty beach. We stayed at the Sri Sharavi Beach Villas & SPA hotel, and the beach in front is basically a private area. Within 5 days we saw only one fisherman and a few tourists walking by. The waves are quite high, however still not that big for surfing. Beach area is very clean.
Absolutely amazing combination of laid back atmosphere while still having enough restaurants and beach bars. Great waves as well.
The beach is beautiful and calm and perfect for families if you avoid the main beach hotel, The Paragon, which is sleezy to say the least.

Read the other reviews that cover most points to note. We were there for just 2 nights. The road through "town" is very noisy and very busy  - quite a scruffy place. Thankfully we stayed in a wonderful little place just 1km away from the beach road so it was nice and peaceful and lots of wildlife yet could still get into the beach area with ease. Our host also took us to Secret Beach which is a little out of town but really nice. I suppose it depends on what you are looking for... We're probably too old now to appreciate what is mostly on offer here. Youngsters will probably enjoy it more.

Beach is very safe, minimal invasion from hawkers selling their wares (when compared to other beaches in SL). You can wade a considerable distance into the ocean without fear. Food options aplenty, however note that some restaurants refuse to cater to locals which is a little dissapointing.

Loud music, a lot of booze, party hard till the early morning in front of a lovely beach. If this is what you are after go to Mirissa beach. A cheaper Ibiza 2.0 with no locals. I think it’s fun for a night or two but Sri Lanka is not here. Just a lot of tourists who do not care about the country’s culture or the excellent food you can enjoy here. A pizza with the Long Island Ice tea will do. Very sorry for the staff who have to endure all of this with a smile on their faces. Very glad it was only a day trip for us and we left to much nicer places

We spent two afternoons on Mirissa beach and enjoyed the atmosphere. There were all ages, families, young travellers, older travellers and couples of all ages. The beach is fairly clean as is the sea. It is busy compared to Tangalle but not too crowded. The sea is safe and fun to swim in.
Nice place to eat something. Also to drink Lion beer :) Nice wave and sand. A lot of people form Europe.
Lovely beach with ample place to eat and drink, ideal for surfing, sea is fairly rough but at the left hand side of the beach it's more sheltered more suitable for swimming.

A lovely relaxed holiday atmosphere on the beach.  The road through the town is horribly busy and not easy if you have children.  Lots of great bars and restaurants on the beach with a range of prices and menus.

The beach is very clean, calm enough for families but also have a couple of small waves for older people to catch shories. The amopsphere of bars & restuarents are appropriate for families and young people. Would highly recommend Mirissa liked this place more then Matara & Polhena Beach

I visited Mirissa Beach in mid-January 2018 with my wife and two, late-teenaged sons. The beach is quite long and very attractive and there are many eating establishments right the way along the length of the beach. However they all offer much the same menu with very little in the way of Sri Lankan food. Not only that but they're all priced much the same and the prices are excessive - not only for the quality, but the quantities. I'm the first to acknowledge that you pay more for food and beverages in sort-after locations, however when the food is as expensive as a Sydney cafe, and not anywhere near the quality, then I'm forced to question the value, and hence write this review. In addition, the wait staff, in general, are slow and disinterested. We've had three meals and five drinks-only experiences on the beach, and I've had one good service experience. On two dining occassions, we've waited so long for the bill, it was tempting just to leave! And furthermore, if we had, I'm pretty certain it wouldn't have been noticed! I'm not a huge fan of Bali these days but my last visit was in 2011 and it was a much more sophisticated dining experience in terms of the finessed food and service. And the prices are comparable. To me there's a laziness about Mirissa - hundreds of tourists on any given day, prepared to enjoy themselves, and spend whatever the menu dictates, regardless of food quality, finesse or service level. I cannot recommend Mirissa Beach - certainly not in peak season at least.
Beach which has something for everybody from areas where families can play with your kids. There are also places which rent out snorkels and surfing equipment

This is an extremely popular beach with its long stretches of golden sand and good surfing waves. It is a great place to walk, jog, swim or surf. There are countless restaurants along the beach-side road and plenty of places to sit and enjoy looking at life and the Indian Ocean. For young people who like disco music this beach must be a haven, but if you don't like loud music that goes on well into the early hours of the morning I would not stay in a hotel on the beach side. Many hotels and bars have dining tables on the sand and loud speakers blare out disco-style noise.

We spend some days at Mirissa beach and it was calm in daytime. Unfortunatly, there were a lot of music ALL NIGHT! Very disturbing if you're not a party human. High waves! You can find a small beach for your kids in the end of the beach. Many restaurant at the beach.

Lovely beach of Mirissa although feels very much like tourists have taken over. All the beach bars and restaurants come alive at night too with candle lit dinners on the beach and some blaring out their tunes. Good fun seeing the great displays of fresh fish outside the restaurants at night.
This is an excellent beach which is free to use, there are a lot of activities to do and the restaurants are excellent on the beach.
A beautiful beach but shame that it seems Sri Lankan's are discriminated against in many places
Excellant and a must visit if you are in Mirissa Good sea food and services safe beach . Ample choices  of food and restaurants.

The beach is not crowded, really suitable for families with children to go there. The best time to go is the morning time as the waves become very strong in the afternoon. The beach is very clean with nice sand. Many people surf or snorkel there.
Like the title says! Enough places in the shade, lot of beach restaurants. Big place to swim with some waves, which are nice. Crouded surf spot, be careful for sea urchins!

it's our second time we stayed at Dulcy and Damith and it was true pleasure and relaxation that we needed. Beautiful garden and the most kind and the nicest family to stay at.  Beach is 5 minutes away, shop very close to the house and everything thing else you need you can manage.mwe stayed at apartment, cooked meals every day, tea whenever we wished for, toast in the morning ( there is also fridge with small freezer ) and what was the beast- we enjoyed our meals at very private garden behind the house, watching monkeys in the morning moving to another lot, often saw peacock just passing the garden, squerls playing at the trees...  IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR THAT KIND OF EXPERIENCE IS A MUST TO STAY AT BANDHUSENA HOUSE.

Looking for a quick getaway or long stay? Mirissa is exactly what you need it to be... Quiet Busy Peaceful Surfing Parties It’s all here and it’s a great place! A beach is a beach but the local people make Mirissa very special!
Its a lovely beach, but if you stay nearby there is too much party house at night.    Bring earplugs to sleep.

Mirissa is not as fast paced as either Galle or Welligama. Services are limited however the beaches are quite nice and not as crowded with some pleasant beaches and overnight guest houses for the whale watching. The best operators we found were Raja and the Whales and Paradise Beach Club. Food wise its hard to go past the No 1 Roti Shop which is some of the best food we had.
Lovely sand, warm waters , yoga, surfing, scuba diving, gorgeous restaurants. What more do you need!

Myself and my husband were in Mirissa last week for one night in order to do Whale Watching the following day. I had previously been to Mirissa on an Asia trip 5 years ago and was amazed (not in a good way) at the change since then. Mirissa is still beautiful however it has transitioned from being a stunning, relaxed beach with some scattered bars and restaurants to an overcrowded beach packed with western tourists and lined with bars/restaurants, cafes and strobe lights. This is ofcourse some people’s scene and if beach night life is what you are after then Mirissa is worth a visit. We are on our honeymoon and more keen for quieter, more romantic, less tourist packed spots. Therefore Mirissa was a big disappointment (and shock to me!) I am not one for leaving negative reviews and I absolutely stand by Mirissa being some people’s cup of tea but just wanted to leave a review for like minded travellers to maybe consider the beaches east of Tangalle and the likes of Bentota etc!

Water was a great temperature, it was a lot busier during the peak season over New Years but less touristy than other beaches I’ve visited at that time. Amount of people of the beach seems to drop off from the 8 Jan. There’s lots of restaurants with sun beds and the view is spectacular 👌

Beautiful beach, with plenty of bars & restaurants and occasional concerts on the beach. Be aware of big waves, especially in the Monsoon season. Surf available in walking distance (primarily for the medium + skilled). Recommended!
Nice beach but for us looking for a relaxing time it was a bit crowded and a party feeling. Lots of restaurants having ok food.

Great beach with nice and soft sand! Great for swimming with waves and amazing view. There are small beach bars all along the beach, lots of turists, but still have a good local feeling compares to unawatuna. Really recommend to visit for a nice beach afternoon!
If you are in Mirissa you must come to the beach.  This is a pretty beach with lots of activities that you can chose to participate in.  The water is warm and inviting.

'Wow', that's the word. This is with out an argument One of the best and spectacular beach in Sri Lanka. Most popular among the tourists both foreign and local, this beach is so unspoiled and beautiful. Mostly popular for its Whale and dolphin watching excursions this is a iconic pin in the world map. As some of you may know that Sri Lanka is residence for the world's largest Blue whale population it is a favourite location for researchers and marine wildlife photography enthusiasts. You may hitch a boat and go to the sea for this amazing safari or you could enjoy a dip in the sea and relax with a cold beer, Your choice. Oh.. I must say that the seafood is amazing at any of the beach side restaurants. But I would say the prices are not very expensive, yet reasonably bit to the high side comparing to other similar locations in the island. It's just a heads up and an as example would be, cost of a Chicken Fried Rice would be about Rs.800/=. Overall a unspoilt beach with plenty of action and good restaurants. Oh my god almost forgot, the Night life. One must always check out its nightlife as it is with plenty of action. So I would highly recommend for you'll to check the place out. I'm sure it will be a amazing experience that you'll will never forget.
Excellent whaleswatching. Saw 5Whales and Dolphins, Sea turtle .Staff at the cruise were friendly and served many refreshments including B fast.Excellent service during 5 hrs Jurney. Very good tour.
Loved the setup of the shacks / hotels on the beach. Beach is good for surfing. You can also go to a small island up and across the beach.
Many people...but still very nice! Good restaurants, fresh fish, not always enough sunbeds, especially in peak season.

Crowded beach. Hot sandy beaches. Plenty of hotels and not friendly towards Sri Lankans. If you are going with your Sri Lankan friends probably not the good place to be. Even when your skin isn’t white. Whale watching is the best thing you could do in mirissa. Try to do it with Sri Lankan Navy. They have better boats and professional service. Could try Surfing in Weligama Bay Area and spicy food. Great place to be if your skin is white..
Is ideal place for Christmas and December holidays to watch Whale and Dolphin by venturing into deep seas.
Lovely beach.  Not as busy as some of the others.   We saw every type of traveler.  Perfect for a relaxing tropical beach escape.
Good but not good as Unwatuna. Crowded. But still beautiful. Suggest Unwatuna over mirissa 😦😦😦😦😦
This beach was our favourite, it has variety of coffeeshops and restaurants and is also great for sunbathing.

Mirissa is one of the best beaches in SL for surfing and whales watching. It's long golden sandy beaches will make you fall in love with the place. Lots of accommodation options and dining options are available for any kind of budget.

Beautiful beautiful beautiful! Great weather, sheltered bay from the wind, plenty of good restaurants and bars (check out Zephyrs, Our World WiFi cafe, Rocket Burgers, Kama Mirissa do a cracking selection of cocktails!)

Mirissa beach is beautiful but it struggles with the crowds that it attracts. It was the only place we saw in Sri Lanka that had litter, the restaurants -but Zephyr- were disappointing and the main road was a nightmare! Saying that our hotel was great, the beach is stunning and you can swim safely!

Mirissa is a beautifull bay surrounded by coconut palm and Mangrovie. Despite the main road is very close, you feel really relax. It is also one of the few places in Sri Lanka were you can bath safely for all year round.
This beach is fantastic, not too busy and good for swimming. Also eating and drinking on the sand is possible at one of many places along the beach.
A great beach, wonderful sunset and waves, only just a bit crowded. Lots of places to have a drink/eat but not the easiest to find a free table during dinner time.

The beach is very clean and the ocean is fresh. Along the beach are several restaurants located if you want to eat at the beach. The beach itself is fairly long and quite good to take walks on. However if you're looking for a beach that you can play soccer or beachtennis on for example, it might not work because the beach is quite narrow, mostly giving space to sunbeds and restaurants.
it's very smooth and dry, no halmufll animal for body, you can lay down whole day, morning to evening
Good for swimming,body boarding it's clean and lots of bars restaurant and entertainment nice 💦 water and the sea is very warm

We went to Mirissa in December 2017 during Christmas break and given the holiday season, there were tonnes of tourists here. Although people were mostly well spread out and weren't getting in each other's way. There is a small town/beach called Weligama bay where you can go by cycle/bike which are easy to rent in Mirissa. Weligama seemed popular with surfers. There's no dearth of guest houses/home stays etc to stay in Mirissa. It is accessible by bus.  Whale watching is a popular activity here and all the home stays and guest houses will offer you a package to go whale watching though we avoided it as it seemed far too cliched a thing to do.
Amazing beach: nice sand, great waves, and no rocks under water. Only pity is that there are no trash cans, which results in people throwing their stuff right at the border of the beach.
The very busy beach. But very best for a holiday.there steamy many hotels stemware it. Untouched are not inform swimming don't jump to the water
Lovely for newbie surfers, not too deep and nice clean beach. Lots of food spots around. Quite nice to walk
The sea was warm and clean with waves that were fun and not too rough in December. The beach had lots of clean sand. We loved it.
A great place to surf and to bask under the sun. Could enjoy local sea food and drinks in the evenings.
The beach looks OK, the hotels are better, the main street interesting, and the harbour good. Not somewhere for a beach holiday.
Beautiful beach with great sand stretches - unlike a few beaches where the waves wash up till the parapet itself! Clear waters and high waves for surfing.

Nice area but way too touristy for our liking. Felt like Benidorm where all caters to drinking and eating on the beach for quite expensive prices. Not much space on the beach if you dont want to rent a chair or sit for a drink. Much prefer the quiet, secluded beaches near Tangalle!

Mirissa is a nice and beautiful beach where you can relax. There are a lot of good restaurants on the beach and no hustling. There are waves and it's a bit deep for small children but you may find a more calm sea at the east side next to the small peninsula.
Wasn’t impressed with the beach. Its too narrow, crowded and dirty. The chairs from the hotels flooded the beaches with not much space for other people.

So disappointed  road is so busy and noisy. Dangerous walking around the road with very scary fast drivers honking; food is way over priced. Beach too narrow. No where to walk much along the noisy beach. Really disliked this over tourist narrow stretch. Horrid place. Got to be more serene and reasonable places left on srilanka

You feel to be free ! Evening dinner in the sand with the sea water waving, simple, long beach to walk, It is a casual place and you feel well if you find your spot on the beach and a good cleaned room.

I was very disappointed on the general state of the beach. People are dirty (locals but also foreigners), maybe because there is not a single trash bin in the entire beach!!!! How is this even possible? Sri Lanka is a beautiful island but too much plastic and waste from tourism 😣
Mirissa beach is nice place to get relax. Mainly you can see blue whales and dolphin there. You can do swim there
We had a great day on the beach after we went whale watching. The scenery is perfect adn the waters very warm.
Its a nice clean beach good for surfing. There are plenty of restaurants that provide good food. The waves are big but there are lots of people swimming comfortably in the water.
Number one beautiful beach in sri lanka. best local food ,good friendly local people. beautiful whales in hear
Amazing beach, beautiful. Great vibe with awesome beach restaurants and accommodation. Would definitely recommend this spot in Sri Lanka
Beach itself has good waves and vibe for surfing activities, but a bit overcrowded with tourists so you need to look for a good spot to relax and enjoy the waves.
Clean, easily accessible beach, public beach. Various restaurants and vendors nearby in case you need food or beverages.

Whats good The quaint beach is beautiful at sunrise and buzzing at sunset. Small but self sufficient, the beach attracts a lot of foreigners. Whats not good The beach is little inaccessible given it is somewhat in between the two major towns of Galle and Matara. What to do Enjoy the morning with a jog. Enjoy the evening with the party. The night life is equally good. Whale watching and surfing at nearby Weligama is promising idea.

Mirissa Beach is where you will be most of time during your stay at Mirissa! Beautiful scenery gently sloping as you walk along the bay. The beach has numerous bars and restaurants all offering competitive prices! Having a swim is relatively safe during the day however, waves and the currents do strengthen as the evening pulls in. We managed to have a few naps on the beach which reinforces the serenity of Mirissa Beach! The ocean is quite shallow towards the shore allowing children to enjoy it as well.
great beach very shallow and sandy so good fro swimming especially with children. Plenty of choices for food and drink

Visited for 2 nights and found the beach to be clean and good to swim off. Occasionally the waves got a little rough but that is dependant on the tides and even then as long as you find the right distance from the beach you can avoid them breaking over you. Lots of choice for food and drink and body surfing boards can be hired cheaply. One end of the bay has small breakers and offers surfing lessons suitable for children.

The beach at Mirissa is a lovely clean one with clear seas and clean sand to lay down on. The main damper with regards to it is the number of mange infected dogs which are left to roam. Being dog lovers my girlfriend and I bought dog treats and ended up with our own little gang of stray dogs. It was sad to see such beautiful animals completely uncared for. The other negative is the number of people trying to flog you terrible weed. Literally everyone who owns a restaurant there would start offering food, then drinks, then weed. It did get pretty tiresome.
Beautiful beach, there many pub you can stay in relax or to made sport. A good place for family, young people or couple.
Mirissa is a quite and secluded beach around 25 kms away from Unawantuna Beach.. Calm water and lot of travel options for whale watching..

This is one of Sri Lanka's most visited beaches. There are a lot of Westerners visiting this beach. This beach is at the South tip of Sri Lanka. At night, good seafood will be set up by different shops along the beach. There are also small amount of surfers who like to go along with with the minor waves in the sea.
Wheale watching. .diving. .snorkling. .fishing tour..fun tour with speed boat and big trimaran..

We headed out in the morning (around 7.30) to avoid the 10 am heat and get a few hours of swimming. Go towards the left side for swimming, waves are gentle, the sea and beach is clean, and it fekt like I had the ocean all to myself. Definitely among the cleanest, best beaches I've had the pleasure of hanging out at.
Well it was the first beach we visited during our trip to srilanka. Sand was soft and the waves not rough. Very close to where we stayed. Easily accessible and certainly spending a few hours.
Nice beach, not as big as Unawatuna, but still very good. Few beach clubs/restaurants and free sunbeds.

Absolutely stunning beach, looks in real life thousands times more beautiful than on the photos. Lots of sea side restaurants which in the evening transfers to romantic atmosphere along the whole beach.

We came back to Mirissa beach after being disappointed with the pollution at Weligama beach. The centre part is not a safe swim zone, BUT it is lifeguarded. If you want to body surf, do it in front of the life guard hut. A safer swim zone is to the left of the beach, in front of a reef. Don't learn to surf here, go to Weligama. If you want a more Western experience come to Mirissa!

This beach could be gorgeous although sadly it seems a little overdeveloped now. Still worth a visit, many bars and restaurants (of variable quality!). Nice for a walk along the shore in the day or evening. Sunset looks great and all the bars have extended ‘happy hours’ for drinks whilst you watch.
Здесь у вас есть уникальный шанс поплавать с гигантскими морскими черепахами. You'll get a unique chance to swim with giant sea turtles
Excellent beach! Many great restaurants! The natives are very friendly here. I've been here 2 times already and can't wait to come back next winter))
Watch the huge blue whale, through a tour on Mirissa beach. A beach that is also very good for some dives

Mirissa is well and truly on the beaten track now. I went to Sri Lanka with an older guidebook which described it as quiet - it is anything but quiet! The entire beach is filled with restaurants, happy hour, sun loungers, burnt tourists - if this is your scene, then Mirissa is perfect. The beach and sea are still beautiful, but the rapidly exploding tourism is really having an impact. When I was there I could literally see the sand erosion happening.
Even if your driving past, stop and check this beach out. Its super quaint with restaurants and bars right on the beach front. Water is beautiful and blue, and the surf is good. Highly recommend.
The beach is nice and less touristy than hikkaduwa but still has a lot of people and is touristy meaning prices can be inflated. There are some good happy hour deals and it is still beautiful

I LOVE MIRISSA. THE beach is fantastic. Very beautiful. No junk on the beach. Ive been coming here 10years. Surfing. Body boards. And nice beach restaurants. And beach bars..what more do you need?? For a great day out. Mjh.u.k
The nicest beach I visited in Sri Lanka, not overcrowded and had a tropical feel with the jungle surrounding it.
Was here 4 years ago. Much busier now & many more young Europeans but not crowded YET!  Still best beach in the area.

Beach is nice enought but...many tourist, less free space and more noise. If you wanna try serfing and drink some coctails than it would be a good choise. If you want romantic beach than should be better look for some other beaches like Talalla.
Mirissa is one of the most beautiful beaches in Sri Lanka. From ancient times it was popular for its unique location on the map o Sri lanka. Now there are lot of Marine life at Mirissa.

The beach is pretty, but it’s really crowded so I guess it really depends on what you are looking for. Lots of old sun beds right next to each other. If you want to relax in a secluded beach this is not it. There are so many other quite beaches just as beautiful around.
The beach is lined with restaurants and eating places. At one end a peninsula sticks out that can be accessed in low tide. It makes for good photographs.
If you are from SAARC countries , you are not allowed in beach parties after 10 pm .... I think Sri Lanka government should look into it immediately.
It is really nice beach with huge waves, very good accomodation posibilities and more or lessclean compared to others.

Highlight of our trip! Spectacular beach and the food along the beach is great. We spent out days sunbathing and stayed until late at night having sea food along the beach. Have all the roti's and cocktail!!
Sea was a little choppy when we went so swimming was a little challenging buy my friend and I had a good time bobbing about and seeing how far the waves could take us. It was a lot of fun.

We absolutely loved Sri Lanka! We Honeymooned in Sri Lanka at the beginning of November, at first we were worried about the weather as the forecast said it was rainy during our dates but take no notice of the forecasts because when it says rainy it means it may rain for an hour or two during the day/night, November is the end of the rainy season and we have great weather but be careful of the sun as it's much more powerful in that part of the world! GET A GOOD DRIVER/TOUR GUIDE, it can save you lots of money! - Even though we booked two weeks away we only initially booked a hotel for a couple of nights in Colombo (Galle Face Hotel was stunning by the way) as we were told it was easy to find a good driver at a good rate once we got there and that was absolutely true. We got a taxi from the airport and we were very lucky as we were picked up by just the best tour guide/driver we could have asked for. Ashan (details below) was the kindest and most relaxed young man, he had great knowledge of everything and offered us options of what we would like to do and achieve, he tailored our trip around us and he was at our beck and call for the whole two weeks, it's also handy to have someone around to take photos of you intsead of every photo being a selfie! We agreed a really good price of $550 USD for the two weeks but bearing in mind this was just out of season so expect to pay a little more in season and we have him a little extra for being so good, also the cost of running a car had just risen as we were on our trip so you should be looking at paying between $300-350 USD per week for a decent driver/tour guide. Ashan also saved us so much money when we booked our other hotels via him, you'll pay around 30% less (sometimes more) if you book though him as this is the cost of TAX in Sri Lanka which can be avoided booking through your tour guide. Ashan took us to some wonderful places which included Sigiriya where the view from the sacred rock it breathtaking, Kandy which is a busy place but you can do some good shopping there, Ella which again is stunning with some great places to eat, try the Chill Cafe - food and drinks are just unreal! Nuwara Elliya is another place worth checking out, it's a little cooler there which is why the call it little England and of course some of the architecture is very English, beautiful place! We spent our last 5 days in Mirissa which was just paradise, you can see tutles, whales, eat, drink and just relax which was the perfect end to our Honeymoon. I could go on for ever but in a nut shell it's an amazing place, lovely people, great food and breathtaking scenery....what more could you ask! Contact this guy if you want a good, honest driver who will help you no end - just brilliant! ASHAN - +94 71 77 63 762 / +94 77 54 19 700
Beautiful Clean beach with Clear Waters, Waves to enjoy, best location with Bars Restaurant. At night you can dine on the shore. Recommended visit for beach lovers.

Lovely beach filled with bars and restaurants - big waves, beautiful location. In the evening, the deckchairs and parasols disappear and tables and chairs replace them, with fresh fish on display at each restaurant. Chilled vibe, relaxed atmosphere - highly recommended!

Mirissa beach is best of both worlds.. it has beautiful soft stretches of sand and has a fun night life without it being tacky! Totally in love with this place! More lively and beautiful than Unawatuna beach.
Still my favourite beach in Sri Lanka. This sandy tropical beach boasts some of Sri Lanka’s best and most stunning sunsets and sunrises.
Restaurants, fresh fish, cocktails, cold beer, big waves...and fireworks...you got it all.  We visited 3 nights...because we only had 3 nights.
I can really recommend you this nice place. You can do a lot of things at the beach. Very friendly people.

Mirissa beach is truly beautiful - the sand is perfect and the numerous palm trees ensure you can sit in the shade. The waves are pretty strong and you need to take care to not get dragged about. Loads of bars and restaurants along the beach to suit everyone

Beautiful beach and amazing restaurants with the freshest fish. Great for tanning, relaxing and surfing. There are also great bars and the beach has a good night life, especially during the festive season. Beware of beach gangs and trouble makers. We were attacked by about ten of them with sticks and bottles. They took our money and cellphones. If you are out late, stick together. Girls should be careful of walking around alone, especially after dark. I will not return because of the safety issues.
Beautiful beach to start surfing, or just chill out on the beach. Lot of options to eat and have drinks. Nice sunset! At night there's party everyday!

I loved the walks on the beach. we could not swim in the sea as there were big waves at the time of our visit. But ocean is beautiful, p-perfect blue and the water is warm. Also, lots of restaurants and bars along your walk. It is a very crowded place, but it is part of the fun. If you are looking for quiet, try to stay somewhere between Mirissa and Unawatuna, or go to Tangalle (further to the south east) and you will have amazing long beaches.
Nice ,clean,small beach with golden sand.C water Restaurants not that clean but food always served with a smile!

A long curved beach with patroled and non-patrolled sections. Clean sand and crystal clear water. Early November was a good time to be here. A number of spas close by, offer good quality  ayuverdic trestments. There are nice cafes at the back of the beach offering good food and relaxed dining atmosphere. By comparison, Jungle Beach and White Jungle Beach are exceptionally poor cousins; the beaches are littered with plastics and other rubbish and the water is not clear. Don't waste time on these beaches.

Great beach, bars and places to surf. There is a lot to do in and around Mirissa. You can go to the nice restaurants at the beach or if you like surfing you can go to Weligama where there are great waves to catch. Rent a scooter en explore the area!!

There are some fantastic beach bars along this stretch of beach - lovely location for an evening meal with the sea lapping at your feet - do be careful in the water - lots of tips and dangerous currents
Nice beach especially compared to the ones we saw nearby. Good for swimming, partying and eating fresh fish.

Nice clean beach with some bars, restaurants and hotels We can in November and the beach was not particularly busy so gave a lovely laid back atmosphere The beach is very narrow and even more so when the tide is in Would recommend the small walk up the small headland (need to be careful as steps have eroded so the path is very near with a drop either side) great view of both beaches
Small cosy beach with a few restaurants. Quite high waves when we were there, but that was ok as it is not that deep. Possibility to rent body boards that was great fun!
The most beautiful beach I've ever seen with great food along the shore. Amazing place to relax and sunbathe in the Sri Lankan sun!

It’s a very layback town with many surfers and easy going vive 1. Beach: Very clean beach. High waves, really good for surfing but it also a good spot to lay on the beach and enjoy a pretty relaxed atmosphere. 2. Food: There are plenty of restaurants on the beach offering seafood and western plates.  You can go to the main streets and find good restaurants for a cheaper price with local food. 3. Lodging:  There are many homestays and hotels.  If you go on low season or before peak time you can go to the beach front hotels and negotiate a good rate so you can stay at the beach.  Homestays sometimes have the same prices and are not beach front. All places include breakfast. 4. Transportation: You can walk everywhere or take a tuc tuc - ALWAYS NEGOTIATE the price. 5. Check your change: ALWAYS check your change back - people tend to scam you all the time if you are a foreigner 6. Party scene:  There are plenty of bars on the beach with happy hour from 5 - 7/8 pm or you can go to downtown or secret beach for a longer party night
A nice beach, but not that long, which can be also very nice. Not really good for surfing. A lot of bars/restaurants are right at the beach, some of them very touristic.

A great place to relax. Whether you want sun, drinks, food, swimming, surfing or just a lie down, this beach is perfect. Be aware that the sea has some strong currents/riptides that can quickly pull you down the shore or out to sea. They're quite manageable providing you stay aware.

The water is reasonably clean and at an inviting temperature. There is a gutter in close which has a current at times which would only effect small children. The sandbar breaks the bigger waves well behind. A small surf break towards the Hedland and you can also hire boogie boards for the kids to surf into the beach on small waves coming over the sandbar. Snorkelling tours with turtles are advertised at the Ox Cart. Apparently a money back promise if you do not see one sounds positive!

Pictures don't reflect the beauty of this place. Nice, clean beach with a pleasant view. 30 to 45 minutes distance from Unawatuna by tuktuk. Saw people snorkeling on their own, so apparently seemed safe too!

I arrived at my hotel and went for a wonder on the beach, I saw a man doing some great work, cleaning the rubbish of the beach, which I thought would be great for future swimmers there. I enjoyed the walk. and around the roads and areas

We stayed in Mirissa Beach , Sri Lanka 🇱🇰 for 10 days. It was an amazing time even though i didn't really swim a lot in beach but i still feel in love with this place. There are some pub in the beach and at night they transform the place into a open seafood feast! A lot of seafood fresh! You can have your food prepared fresh while enjoying the atmosphere! Just wonderful! In the morning we always walk in the beach before having our breakfast then after we always make sure to enjoy the amazing sunset 🌅! What i miss is the sunrise for sure it will be amazing as well! The place is pack of tourists since its a tourists zone so its very safe but expensive place as well, we are budget travelers we still manage , you will still find cheap stores, restaurants , trips and accommodations. I wish to visit the place again someday.

Beautiful beach - rather a lot of plastic on it which would take little effort to clear up.  Spectacularly beautiful - just like in the movies.  You can hire a body board for an hour and have fun messing about in the water.
We loved our stay at Mirissa, great location numerous good restaurants,  friendly people who are always smiling,  beach is clean and the water refreshing,  easy bus ride from Galle.
very relaxing and no over populated with tourism they have kept it clean and quiet, nice bars by the beach and fresh fish.

I don't know who is charge of the beach because the waves are set far too big.. you go in the sea and you get thrown around by the waves, someone needs to turn the machine down or something. Not good oh and it was cloudy too

I loved this beach, it's a good stretch with plenty to do. Rented out some body boards had a great day. Good waves for body boarding. Lots of places to eat and drink, some good some not so pick wisely. Very clean water, they look after this beach, overall a must see for all ages who just want to be big kids for the day. 2 sections to the beach, parking and tuk tuk available with a nice spa up the road, which is worth a visit to rescue sun kissed skin.
Superb beach with so many surfing training schools. Took my 9 year old to sea and she really enjoyed.
We really enjoyed the beach in Mirissa- we loved the waves. It was not to crowded and you have some really nice bars and restaurants- in the evening you can join one of the party’s.

After a nice long week of sight seeing, we spent the second week of our trip relaxing on the beach in Mirissa. Watch the sunset on top of Parrot Rock and then take a walk down the beach to browse the restaurants daily catch, where you point to your fish and the BBQ right on the sand for you. Hard to beat having candlelit dinner in the sand with the water washing over your feet. Check out some surf boards or morning yoga on the sand.
Very small and lovely beach. There is very small island you can go by walk. Good beach to enjoy. Beach bars and fresh seafood is very nice.
If you are in down south, don't miss this place to visit. It's nice beach and lot of beach bars on the beach LOVELY !!!!!!

If this is the best beach in Sri Lanka then goodness me there are some terrible ones.  Yes, the sand was clean - that being the sand that hasn't been built over by the greedy bar and hotel owners that is.  The water isn't all that clean, the streets are narrow and hot, the food is generally so-so and there isn't really a town here.  There's no coral, few fish but there are a few turtles that graze on the almost bald rock shelf at the eastern end (don't get sucked into the "snorkel with the turtles" thing either BTW - it's really pretty awful).  The "cocktails" are actually safe to give to children as they are almost alcohol free.  I suppose this place would have a real party vibe around XMAS but the rest of the time it is really rather skippable.  Bob Marley by the bucketful in all bars.  You get the picture.
The beach is great for swimming in the summer Best restaurant in the beach i loved this place, the waves, the view and the weather

We were told Mirissa was a must-visit in Sri Lanka. We were not impressed. The beaches are not very good, with huge rocks in the ocean and almost no where you can swim. The beaches are very small and right next to the road.

Around the corner from Palm Villa is the huge surf Beach, the main Mirissa beach which has prefect surfing waves, while being too rough in September for much swimming. The smaller bay is much better for swimming.
Sri Lanka is blessed with many beautiful and generally unspoiled beaches - this is another one we only stopped for a few hours on route to Galle had a nice lunch and moved on.
Lovely place for a spot of swimming. Plenty of turtles in the right season. Lots of places off the beach for a coffee and a Sri Lankan curry

The beach is great for swimming in the summer season , not too strong waves, and the beach is pristine and clean. Has a overall lovely wibe with many restaurants lining the beach. There is a small hill here where you can climb upto when you get bored of just lazing at the beach.
The beach is lovely but a lot of tourists. The water very rough this time of year. One of the cleaner beaches I've seen in Sri Lanka

Amazing fine almost white sand, laid back vibe yet a developed infrastructure, great food and drinks available wherever you go: Welcome to Mirissa Beach. It's probably one of m favorite beaches in the world and I keep coming back here. Great vibe!

i loved this place, the waves, the view and the weather when we visited were all just perfect. In July this place is way better than any other beach you can visit in sri lanka. you have many restaurants to eat and drink in the sun; the food around is good and people are friendly.

fabulous beaches lovely waves .. cheap food and drink .. go during season if you are a local... if not ....any time if your not from SL is fine cause i went off season and it was still fab....the place is perfect relax unwind cool off in the beaches party at the clubs on the beach... drink be merry enjoy the local cuisines you can do it all....stay on the beach stretch if you can ... please make note there are 2 beaches that show up on the maps you need to be at the one with W & D and Central etc on it it you want to be with all the happenings of mirissa .. if you want a more quiet location stay on the next stretch where you will find Madara resort, Marriott etc
Don't miss this place if you are coming here!! Such a gorgeous stretch of beach with everything from food, drinks, parties or just relaxing.
Worth a visit but not a beach for swimming as waves are quite big and strong. More of a surfers beach. Lots of food and drink choices all along the beach too which is great!
The beach itself is nice and clean and there is small mound which can be climbed and gives good views of the beach and the sea as such.

So. This beach is in all the tour guides. We therefore duly added it to our itinerary. What a waste of time. With the clear but ambivalent expectation of being shot down by the twenty-something hippie/Essex travellers, this place is a dump.  *Full of the tattooed English. If you are used to/ expect clean beaches and a relaxing, taverna style character/ tranquil beach, this place is NOT for you. It's essentially a busy diesel fuelled main road right next to a narrow strip of sand upon which the various hotels and copious beach bars lie. You cannot therefore escape the M42 noise and fumes. The beach is not for swimming (or seemingly, in sept, even surfing) as the waves are too high. The beach bar Rotti was also underwhelming. Sigh. We hot-footed it straight outta here to Galle. Which, if you're in your 30s/40s and NOT from *Essex or Manchester, is far better. *No offence intended to those from Essex/Manchester, you understand.

Mirissa Beach was fantastic, it has several different parts to it so you never get  bored.  We loved all the beach restaurants along the way, everyone was so friendly and the food and cocktails were amazing.  Turtle Bay was great for snorkelling and spotting turtles.  at the other end of the beach was crystal clear water.  Please be aware that the sea can be very rough and dangerous so listen to the locals as to where is safe to swim.

Mirissa beach is very beautiful & it's also lovely & clean!  We loved swimming in the ocean here & also going for walks in the evenings.  We were lucky enough to see the fisherman perched on the poles in the ocean which was a real treat!

I am very fussy about my beaches but I loved this one.  Just pick a lounger and chill.  Because the beach is quite narrow, I could sit on a lounger while my 12 year old played in the sea all day just feet away.  The view in both directions is beautiful, with a rocky little island one way and a palm covered headland the other.  The sand is golden and thick grained (I hate those dusty fine sand beaches!) without any nasty critters on the sand or in the sea.  The sea was very rough further out when we went but we had a lot of fun splashing around in the waves in the shallow part.

Mirissa beach is probably the best in Sri Lanka. we went there from Trincomalee and we found the beach much cleaner and nicer. It's good to spend a couple of days there. the town itself doesnt have much to offer. there is only one good supermarket there and for buying food you need to go to Matara.

When deciding where to spend our last few days in SL we were deciding between what is usually suggested Hikkaduwa, Unawatuna and Mirrisa....we are glad we chose Mirrisa. It is wonderful, not crowded (even though we were there at the peak of the season), great waves all the time, water is warm, enough bars to choose where to drink you cocktails and eat your dinner. We did go to Unawatuna one day for a swim but we preferred Mirrisa.

Not a surfing beach in August but fantastic beach for holiday. You can swim in off peak but it can get rough. About a dozen or more beach cafes in hot competition. Food is god. Beers cold. You can try almost all shacks and not be disappointed. Plenty of shade. You can use the beach huts facilities. Cold beers around. Can rent shares and umbrellas cheap. Some are free if eating at the bar. Favourite bars are Zypher, WaterCreatures Restaurant and Bar and Sunshine Beach inn. Best beach on the coast. For non surfing relaxation, better than Weligama and Unawatuna.

This was a lovely beach. August is not great for snorkeling but we gave it ago. My son did manage to swim with turtles in turtle bay, just walk south along the beach. We stayed in Giragala village guest house. It must be the best location on the beach; right on the point with the small island. 'Why not getaway' tours booked all our accommodation and this hotel was better than we expected. We stayed an extra night in Mirissa as the location was perfect.

Even this time of the year swimming was possible. The beach itself was quite flooded so there was just a small strip of sand surrounded by the many happy hour bars and restaurants. Nothing for people seeking lonely places (for those the Tangalle area is much better).

This is a beautiful beach. It is popular with both tourists and locals. The sea is calm so great to swim in. The sand is pretty clean and there are some good views, especially the little island that signals the end of one side of the shore. The beach is also popular at night with several good bars perched on the sand. Many offer happy hours all day and some bars even have some little puppies in them! The only downfall of Mirissa is the busy road that runs right next to it. It is dangerous, especially at night, and there is a lot of litter on the side. Mirissa is naturally beautiful, shame about the road.

personally I like Mirissa beach on other beaches near by cause it is small and the shore line is very clean . also the restaurants there are very close to water which made the setting perfect  . I liked the small island across the corner of the beach and you can reach by passing on couple rocks or swimming but it's not that much easy .

Another good beach to rest. Wonderful beach with good people. In mirissa beach, Don't forget to go to see whales. Is a wonderful journey. If you are lucky, you can see huge whales & you can collect some remarkable  memories to your life. Romantic Beach with more leisure.
Went to Mirrissa for two days last week. Lovely beach, nice atmosphere.cannot fault it. would have liked to have stayed for longer.

A lovely beach near Galle, to party and to relax. There are a lot of shacks to just chill with your loved ones, and have the local seafood and a drink. We enjoyed the whale watching a lot too, that happens nearby. A must visit in your Sri Lanka trip
Wonderful beach, amazing experience, be aware of big waves, restaurants are very good. It was worth to come here, perfect place to rest.
we went whale watching and went there and had fun in the secret beach after  we went whale watching   so we collected sea shells
Mirissa beach is nice calm and lovely place to spend a day few nice restaurants around beach and wave is actually high in august now but still enjoyed swimming
Clear waters.Enjoyable to walk from one end to the other.Small island in front of the beach, but not accessible easily.Water currents are too strong.Good place for kids.Lots of nearby restaurants.

The sand is white and soft, the waves gentle. You can enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of surfers on the beach or on the water. The main street features neat little stands where you can purchase neat T-shirts, Buddha pants and tops. If you walk a little further, you'll spot private islands and fishing boats. This is the place where you can pay fishermen to take their pictures as they pretend to fish on the traditional stilts. Great photos for an activity that no longer takes place, but really, you might be helping the local economy, so why not?
Kids had a blast paying here..the depth can be quiet deceiving at a few places. So watch out for those waves.

clean, peaceful, amazing, breathless beach! pubs were all over the place. however we visited the place during off season thats y the beach is somehow rough. we only stayed and played in d shores due to big waves.
Stunning beach with warm seas. great food available, fresh seafoods ,local curries and plenty of fresh fruits either to drink or eat. A beautiful part of Sri Lanka.

This is one of the most picturesque little spots I have seen in the whole of Sri Lanka after 12 weeks. So nice in fact that I came back a second time! The beach itself has a healthy number of beach bars without feeling too overcrowded. The scenery is beautiful with golden sand and palm trees. The sea remains shallow for a fair distance meaning wave jumping is fun. Body boards are freely on offer in the bars for 250-300LKR per hour. However, it is VERY important to note that the undercurrents are extremely strong in parts of the beach and it is very easy to get overwhelmed by the combination of large waves and strong currents if going too far. Locals are regularly swept away from beaches throughout Sri Lanka - so tourists unfamiliar with the water should take extra care when swimming.
Definitely this is not the best beach or most beautiful beach of Sri Lanka, lot of waste, not so much space to sunbathe.
Very nice beach with many variant of pubs. I prefar local pub with name Our world Wi-Fi Cafe. Good place for relaxing out of season.

One of the best beaches we've ever come across! Amazing water and sand, and lots of cafes/ restaurant along the way. Not too overcrowded, just amazing. Can rent body boards here which is the best fun. Also lots of free chairs for sunbathing and relaxing.

This beach is beautiful and so much fun. The waves have a pattern I have never seen before.  They crash in both directions causing a large crashing effect that towers high and powerful. Its so much fun.  Another plus is the body surfing.  I have never body surfed before.   We enjoyed it for hours and with cheap board rentals and delicious food offered at multiple places. It kept us there for hours.

Had read much blurb about Mirissa before visiting and expected great things.  But we were quite underwhelmed.  If the waves are why you are visiting then maybe it's worth it.  As a family we had fun body boarding but the beach itself has a very narrow strip of sand which I was told is always the case.  So no room to spread out on the sand. The top is lined with a strip of bars for a bite and a drink all pretty similar. The main road through Mirissa has nothing of interest and is quite busy with buses hurtling through here and there were piles of dumped rotting rubbish at the side of the street.  Welligama looked a bit nicer although still with the tide coming in quite high.  Have to say our experience of east coast beaches were nicer.  If I were doing this trip again this coastline would still be on the agenda but I would not stay for long. If it was a paradise at one time it isn't now. Just a tad grubby.  Although if you want to stay somewhere which is just off the main drag with nice tasteful rooms and a Sri Lankan chef who at the time of writing serves the best Sri Lankan food we ate whilst here, check out the Spice House.
Gorgeous bay with a long stretch and golden sand.  In the evening the restaurants put out candles making it magical.

Great beach, nice and sheltered, lots of options for eating and drinking all along the beach. Not cheap but tourist prices however most of the places do very long happy hours! Expect to pay about Rs.300 for a large beer.
Very nice beach, fun sized waves to play in. Lively without being overcrowded and a great place to watch the sun go down.Easy to find good food or other things to do if you tire of sand and sea.

Mirissa beach ... Not the kind of beach if your after pristine,clean coastline and wide open spaces.Nope Mirissa is all hustle,bustle ,dark skinned over tanned Europeans with sour faces or Brit holiday makers travelling in packs( safety in numbers perhaps?)Do not get me wrong.. It's a fun place and the locals are super friendly- which makes up for the filthy massive amount of rubbish and the ugly face of tourism everywhere

This would be an ideal place for you if you are in seek of whale and dolphin watching expeditions, breathtaking views, recreation including SCUBA diving, lovely beach-side restaurants, year round parties and activities, budget accommodation options etc.

This beach is lined with restaurants, lots of fresh seafood but all options available. You can book your whale watching tour which was amazing! We saw about 8 blue whales. We took our 18 month old, he did great! See my insta for more pics @loewenlife
Great beach and lots of shops, cafes around, good for swimming, not surfing. There are beach parties almost everyday

So glad we chose this beach to go to. It is a beautiful place, a narrow beach with beach beds and palm trees. Many restaurants right at the beach. In the evening the beach beds make room for tables and chairs for dinner. The sea is so close, you can often feel the water at your feet when you're having dinner. I went here in July and then the sea was pretty rough. It was not possible to swim, but standing in the waves is a lot of fun too!

The Mirissa bay is a fun place for the kids to play on the beach or go body boarding and for experienced surfers to enjoy surfing. One could hire a board on the beach for a small amount and go body boarding there.There are many places on the beach where one can have a good meal as well.
Such a beautiful beach. Its one of the cleanest with lots of little cafes all the way along. No one bothers you here it really is a chill out beach. The sea is very clear and a bit calmer here.
We went to Unawatuna and Mirissa and found Mirissa much better. The beach is more beautiful and no one will bother you while you are on the beach.
Sometides if this devided beach ia sand , some are gravel..just make sure u hit the one after banana garden hotel towards gale. Its sandy and full of bars and small restaurants

Amazing nice sunset on the parrot rock in mirissa. Whale watching is really amazing in here. Restaurant and clubs are opened until mid night. Cheap places and expensive places are every where on here. Wish to come on this upcoming December with my mom

Mirissa Beach is ideal location for beach holidays. Its excellent for surfing, scuba diving and deep sea fishing. There are also many restaurants and hotels nearby. Its high tide when we got there so we weren't able to swim.

Top beach in the south of sri lanka. Rather rough waters at end of june 2017, do be sure to enter the water only if you are a good swimmer (the big waves are much fun!). Some spots ok for kids, but never let your little ones alone at the beach.

This place ' Marissa ' on of the weal watching destination in sri Lanka , most of visitors visit and do yoga and mediation in Ashram Sri Lanka / katuwana / Tangle (1.30 mints) from this place , all most all recommended this beach is one of the best in sri Lanka
We stayed in Paradise beach club. The area of the beach nearby was beautiful but dangerous to swim in. There were few cafes and many stray dogs. We didn't try any of the cafes.

There is a big rock a little inside the waters with a narrow strip of land connecting it to the beach. Make sure you climb up the rock and see the sunset from there. You will love it. This is a very clean and lovely beach. The waves are mellow and nice and you can take a swim in the water. It's a beautiful experience.

Such a great beach for having some nice days. There are a lot of small beach bars, where you can sit just a few meters away from the water. In the evening, there are also some small Partys in some of these bars. Great place in Sri Lanka!!

The water is crystal clear with the right amount of waves. Beach is not over run with tourists & has a lot of options for restaurants & drinks. Ideal setting for a relaxing evening by the beach. It also

This was one of the better beaches we saw on this side of Sri Lanka, however powder white sand it is not and the waves can get a bit dangerous. I dont see what the fuss about the town is either I think it is just a better beach resort than some of the others. We were there during the monsoon though.

Mirissa is a great place to spend the day and relax. There are plenty of restaurants along the beach to have a meal or a drink and hang out. My friend and I spent the day going back and forth between the ocean and our table at the Reggae bar. The water in the ocean was a little rough, but once you get past where the waves are breaking it's not so bad and we had a lot of fun. There's a big rock just offshore called Parrot Rock that has stairs. On top of the rock there are paths and benches, and it offers a great view of the beach and coastline.

We visited Mirissa Beach in the month of May. Beach is very clean and curved in shape. Beach have water sports activity and Food shacks. Beach have small Island in the center. You can visit that island as well. Due to the monsoon, Deep swimming was not available. Beautiful Beach
The tide comes in up to the chairs and loungers - beware if you put your bags on the sand! Otherwise lovely!
If You want to take some rest and chill You need to visit Mirissa Beach. It is a really clean and quiet sandy beach. And if You are hungry You can find some good restaurants near to the beach.

One of the best beach in Down South which has much life. The best time is sunset hours. Go for parrot rock to see a sunset. it will be much romantic with less crowd. Becareful your steps when you go up and down to parrot  rock. Good vibe in the evening at all pubs.
I am quiet disappointed by mirissa beach. Lots of dishes, to many resorts. Two good spots: the big rock in the middle and the coconuts island on the far-left side.

Love this beach. Really clean, nice white sand and beautiful water. Lots of cafes and restaurants along the beach but it's not overdone. Having said that, we're here in low season and it's nice and quiet - assume high season might be a different story
What a great way to finish my trip in Sri Lanka. Mirissa beach is chilled and pretty. There are plenty of accommodation and restaurant options to fit everyone's budget.
Mirissa has a small beach with lots of cafes and water sports Also the locally whale watching boats leave locally

Great spacious safe beach with Life Guards In season!Best in the area!Good choice of accommodation Most with restaurants and guest houses attached. We got here after the whale season had ended as well as snorkeling season to swim with the sea turtles!Great vibe from the locals and honest Tuk-Tuk drivers.

This beach and its view is fantastic, but there isn´t a proper public access to the beach. All the beach is occupied by hotels and shops. The waves are quite strong. Don´t swim there and watch your kids.

Nice, but the waves can be quite dangerous if one ventures outside of the breakers. I preferred the beaches in Uppuveli. Coast Guard mans an lifesaving-tower and watches over several nests of turtles, quite amazing when they hatch!
This beach is beautiful, there are many restaurants and the people here have been warm and welcoming.
Nice and calm beach. Beatiful. Great sea. Nice for snorkeling and for suf. Nice beach restaurants and hotels

This beach is so wonderful that you shouldn't miss it :)) Water was great - clean and warm, beautiful sand, many really nice restaurants and bars. You can come here and just chill and relax whole day. Definitely highly recommended.
I liked this place a lot. I am sure to visit again along with family/friends. Whale Watching was an awesome experience.

We accidentally ended up here, we only wanted a coffee. When we saw the beach we were all sold. We ended up staying almost two weeks here. Bodyboarding, surfing, snorkeling, whale watching, body surfing, sunbathing. We also saw the fruitbats (ask Indika, the guy renting sufboards near Suduweli to show you their tree, his number +94718797084[ he also organises whale watching trips, scuba diving, surf lessons, etc, etc at fair prices]), monkey up on the hill, adult turtles laying eggs, baby turtles making their way to the sea. You just sit around and see thing happening around you. Let's not even talk about the amazing cocktails and every day beach parties at different bars. What a lovely place. It's true paradise!
Great beach with many restaurant options.  Catch a beautiful sunset while drinking beers and enjoying the fresh locally caught seafood!
Enjoy a lovely coconut water while watching this cute little beach buzz with activity and dip into the fun waves...

A lot of bars, friendly people and a beautiful beach. Loved it.. you can also. Book tours on the beach..like whale watching or the yala safari tours, but u would recommend you to book them a little bit nearer to the weligama beach ( on the main street) it is much cheeper and friendlier.. + you get more comfortable service.

Myself and the girlfriend stayed here for 9 days over all.  We were originally meant to stay for 3 days and move on.  After moving on to tangalle we realised how much we loved the buzz in Mirissa. So we came backed and stayed in the surf and yoga hotel which we can't recommend High enough. Mirrisa's has a great atmosphere with a great mix of activity that isn't over crowded or too tacky. The main beach is great for water activities like body surfing and the bars are great for a beer or cocktail at sunset.  Also there are protected turtle nests which we were lucky enough to see hatch. The waves can get big with a swell so children do need to be watched at the shoreline. Overall the place gets 5/5 from me and I can't wait to go back!
Beautiful place. Whale watching with raja and the whales highly recommended. Excellent trip with them. Wonderful views and beach.

This is a great place to spend an afternoon and have lunch. It is near the main town and offers a lot of tourist style food options. Do note that the water can be pretty rough here and can come up to the edge of the beach. Overall, a clean beach with decent views.

Very friendly area to visit & if you like seafood you will not beat choosing your own fresh fish,prawns or lobsters straight from the fisherman on the beach at night and having one of the many restaurants cook it for you

We spent two days in Mirissa and the beach is stunning! Definately try to go up the little island next to it because the view ia wonderful. It has a nice sand, plenty if places to eat and have drink, a space to lay dowb if you want to get a tan and nice and clear water.
Nice beach less sauvage than the others, can spend a nice day if u are based around, weligama just next but not really for tourists, for sunset better to go other side like bentota or hikkaduwa

We went earlier in the day (around 10am) and it wasn't too busy.  There are plenty of bars and restaurants around in walking distances. The waves are good for body surfing, but do come crashing down pretty hard. We did go back later in the day, and it was way more crowded. Although we did not get a chance to go, there are other beaches 15 minutes by tuk tuk east that are better for snorkeling and not as crowded.

It's a nice & pristine beach for the people seeking calm & relaxing holidays. Though, snorkeling is not very rewarding, but the turquoise blue water, half-encircled by coconut trees offers a very eye-soothing scenic beauty.
Visit with family was very nice with nice clean beaches and clear blue water. The crowds there are not bad and not too rowdy.  Quite suitable for family.
Clean, and plenty of bars for drinks and food. Rocks present, great for surfing and watching sun rise.

Small bay but very nice and relaxing. The sun loungers we used were free providing we bought some drinks or food which was reasonable. The sea was a bit rough but I believe it's a surfers bay so to be expected.

Mirissa beach has it all happening. Great restaurants on the beach, sun lounges for hire and surfies aplenty. Whale watching is one of the many activities you can do in Mirissa. We saw some Blue Whales but if you are a little bit squeamish, please take sea sickness medication, we had quite a few seasick people on our trip. Having happy hour on the beach, with a spectacular sunset and then a fresh seafood dinner with the waves crashing in, cannot be beaten.
Wonderful little beach - we recommend walking along to Zephyr for an amazing dinner! Make sure to book or get there early though or risk being turned away!

Mirissa Beach and Wiyama Beach are the two most beautiful beaches in the south. They are both white sand beaches and have several cute beach restaurants. Wiyama has calm water due to the reef outside that keeps away the waves

My wife and I loved the beach! Free use of sun chairs/umbrellas at most places if you order something. Lots of tourists, which is to be expected, but very little trash. Obviously, the prices at the beach restaurants are higher than many other places, but the view is great.
Must lay down on The  beach with cold beer.perfect weather to chill and happy to stay all day on the beach ..

This was our first beach experience in Sri Lanka! We loved the vibes (busy but not crazy busy), the restaurant options and the waves. Other beaches along the coast we just incredible but for swimming we found the seas a little treacherous. We ended up coming back to Mirissa because we wanted to surf and enjoy the variety and atmosphere.

The owner/manager/reprobate called Chaminda or "Chami" (short tubby man with long hair and patchy moustache) just chased us from the property with 2 x 1m long machetes threatening to kill us over a discussion over pro rata rental of the snorkel, fins and goggles. They made us pay - via intimidation - the full hourly rental rate for 10mins of use.. Further, the food (and drinks!!) takes incredibly long to arrive and is drastically overpriced. I would recommend visiting the beach - take your own picnic and sit on the beach around the corner, but DO NOT DO ANY BUSINESS WITH THEM!!
Beautiful beach with fun waves although they can be dumpy. There is no shortage of beachfront bars to choose from and you can check out the surfers too.
Lovely beach but a nearby Marriott Hotel is being built which may change that. Fabulous surfing on the waves and warm, warm water and sandy beach all the way out.

A great long sandy beach that was very popular with body boarders as the waves were so good!! Great eating places around as well, especially The Shack, which was good for a snack in day and meal at night! We had loads of fun on this beach.
many restaurants around, nice place for a walk at night or in the morning . only if you stay near the beach, the club would be too loud.
Quick look as we came primarily for the whale watching and to see the fishing area. We were looking for other attractions in the area

Went backpacking in Sri Lanka in January 2016 and spent 4 days in Mirissa -  A small village with the perfect, calm beach. It was a perfect destination for relaxing after Colombo, Kandy and hiking in Sri Pada. The beach was clean and it had enough services (a few cafes and restaurants but nothing more, no big touristic hotels or night clubs). During our stay the only "minus" was the fact that some days the waves were so high it was forbidden to go into the water for a while (although this might be the case in other parts in Sri Lanka, too). We made the mistake and went to Hikkaduwa after Mirissa for 2 days - And found beaches loaded with tourists and tourists only (and sand full of garbage). If we could turn back time, we would spend those 2 days in Mirissa instead! So Mirissa is highly recommended if you're looking a place to calm, relax and enjoy lazy days after hectic cities and climbing :) There is really not much to DO there but that's my point!

This beach has a really lovely easy going vibe and the waves are quite fun. You can suntan on the sunbeds of the restaurants or simple lie on you towel underneath the shady trees. There are no beach vendors intruding and you can even find a decent ice coffee at the coffee house (these are really hard to come by in Sri Lanka).

Loved this beach with some good sized waves. Lots of restaurants to lay in front of and have drinks and food. Sand is very nice. We even got to see baby turtles when they hatched and headed to the ocean. Very special. Very nice at night too.

Mirissa beach is quite small compared to other srilankan beaches I've been to. Small, but lovely. There are couple of restaurants and some bars you can have a party in the evening after swimming in the ocean. There were quite big waves when we went there so I do not recommend entering water with small kids.
Amazing beach with three bays ; the first one with huge  waves , the second is with calm waves and the third which is calked turtle beach is a swimming pool.
I've been to different beaches on Sri but Mirissa beach is the best and the most spectacular. You wouldn't be disappointed.

We saw Blue whales from 20m away and watched turtles hatch on a beach. The beach itself is stunning, great surf and a huge variety of food & drinks on offer. We also swam with turtles and saw Bats at dusk. Outstanding!

One of the best beaches in Sri Lanka, ideal for couples if you prefer a walk of secluded serenity try the beach in the evening hours its less crowded. If you are daring you can also try climbing the "Rock Island"

Had a great time here, although the first 2 times it rained. The beach is big, with very good restaurants, sun beds (which you don't have to pay for). In one side of the beach you can see a few people doing surf (specially in the afternoon). Evenings are very relaxing there, you can see people happily walking around the beach.

mirissa is one of beautiful beach in Sri Lanka, I love staying here and walk around the beach in the morning and have a quality time on the beach.and you can even do a whale watching in mirissa, they say it's a place for them,next time definitely will do..but overall I loved being here..

This is a nice and chilled beach. The water and beach seemed quite clean (hardly rubbish in comparison to other beaches). Lots of Restaurants and Cafes on the beach front for a beer or cocktail. I was lucky enough to see some turtles be released on the beach while I was there. It was unreal.

We read a lot of reviews about Mirissa before deciding to make it a destination during our trip to SL. I'm not sure I can agree with images of swinging in hammocks sipping from coconuts. Our first impression was one of disappointment when we saw the hoards of tourists and bars and restaurants swarming the beach. However the day after our arrival didn't seem to be as bad (we arrived on a Sunday). Never the less it's far from paradise but is fairly decent in it's own right.  Many eateries on the beach but all are overpriced and lack the quality you find elsewhere in SL. We found Zephyr to be an exception to the rule (amazing food and value) and also some places off the beach. Would recommend "Little tuna"for sushi! Too touristy for us but not a complete train smash!
Lovely beach. Big waves. Lots of eateries and bars. Not alot of aunbesda when we went but it was New Year so might change when everything open.

Beach which has something for everybody from areas where families can play with your kids, to areas where surfer dudes can ply their trade to a strip with bars and restaurants catering for different crowds. This is a beach targeting the masses although it did not feel too crowded

Clean and not too rough to swim. Many restaurants. We also saw turtles hatching on the beach. There are also places which rent out snorkels and surfing equipment. Some dogs running around on the beach but they did not seem dangerous.
Lovely sandy beach with fine sand. The waves are quite big though so it's good for surfing and not swimming, the waves just beat you up!
Sandy beach with great sea waves.  Lots of places to eat and drink on the beach, some with the water coming right up to the tables.
Really nice location. Clean. Full of tourists.. Locals dont come here. Nice sand..nice and warm water

The water is very clean and warm but it is hard to find just a place one the sand to put your towels. Everywhere you have companies who wants to rent you  sunbeds. The music in the night is annoying and much too loud. Despite al this trouble we  were delighted to see hatching turtle eggs!

Absolutely beautiful beach lots of little restaurants offer sunbeds with umbrellas to hire for the day..night time the beach comes alive with live music or quite bars lovely food lots of wonderful fresh fish to choose. .
Very beautiful beach with clean water and lifeguards because of the huge waves. I don't like the people who try to sell you fresh fish from the bars-restaurants next to the beach

I haven't been to the west coast but the north doesn't really have beaches and the east coast is disgustingly dirty. The surf beach of Arugam Bay on the east is probably the only other backpacker beach but it is so expensive, smells of rotting fish due to all the fishing boats parked up & mainly rotting away. The beach is full of rubbish and the sand has black on it, it's also 3 times the price of Mirissa. A basic curry & rice is 600 & a beer is 650!!! In comparison Mirissa has lots of cheap places to stay, cheap & delicious food and lots of places on the beach to eat at night & chill out. The waves can be a bit hairy but there are life guards, You can do a day trip to Galle from here and there is just much more of a sociable vibe. If you want beaches then stay at Mirissa, I don't think any of Sri Lankas beaches are a patch on places such as Thailand, but this was the best I saw in the month I was traveling
Went there for whale watching. We saw around 4 whales and quite a few dolphins. Water was blue and changed its colour the deeper we went in. Beech was nice light sandy beech with lots of beech pubs!!

Marissa Beach is one of Lanka's best. The surf is big and exhilarating. But the road through town is busy and polluted. Get a room on the beach, NOT on the road. Eat on the beach, NOT on the road! The beach is everything. The only consideration for beach rooms are the midnight bar parties that feature loud, heavy, pumping noise. Ask around for advice on quiet hotels.
Nice beach one end was very good for surfing.   Lovely restaurants actually along the waters edge for fish etc.

We've just travelled to the hill country and down to Tangalle, and Mirissa is by far the cleanest place we've been to so far on our trip. The beach has a great ambience, particularly at night. There are lots of good and  cheap bars and restaurants. We did a day trip Weligama today and couldn't believe how filthy and smelly the beach was. A good place to stay away from.
Really nice beach but the waves hit you really strong. You can see a beautiful sunset there. Is full of restaurants and bars where you can drink a beer next to the beach

This was my favourite beach (two beaches really) of six I stayed at on my first visit to Sri Lanka. The coral to the east of the island is trashed and the water a bit murky, but I did see a small shark. Beyond this is sheltered swimming but the middle of both beaches gets rough in the afternoon and is suitable for good surfers. Heaven for sundowners and then dining on the beach and the restaurants take it in turns to host the later entertainment.

Nice beach and good sheltered place to swim if you struggle with the bigger waves.  But, at night, the beach comes alive with restaurants and fish displays.  Walk along and select your fish and after a brief haggle about the price, relax and enjoy.  Very rustic and extremely atmospheric, but not classy.  The town behind the beach is average Sri Lankan town.
Not a massive beach but it is very clean and picturesque. As a result it is also very touristy. The waves are strong and there are reefs so be careful not to stray to far from shore.
