The beach is blue and super clean. Mirissa Town is truly a seaside town with many sea-related activities. Whale-watching tours are highly recommended here.
Clean sandy beach with good opportunities for Surfing, Swimming or just hanging on the beach. Some People say that snorkelling could be done here, I gotta say forget it!
what you are looking for. Its quite clean, but many dogs lives there. Waves are too big for swimming, but nothing special fir surfing. Many restaurants, many people....

The beach itself is possibly one of the nicest beaches I have seen. Unfortunately the tourist industry has sprung up to fast around it, giving what appears to be little thought to the beaches natural beauty. Dotted along the beach you will find several restaurants and bars that sadly take away from the beaches charm. Whilst  walk to the beach is littered with rubbish and waste. It would b fair to say that this beach is no longer a hidden gem. If looking for somewhere a bit more private and natural I would keep moving!

What I love about this beach area is that it is still (relatively) undeveloped. The beach is clean, as is the water. Head south of the island which divides the beach and you have a smaller beach (check out Papa Mango) which is less popular but still as lovely. The water breaks closer to the shoreline which means once you get over the initial wave you can float about in the lovely clear sea...and even see the turtles. It's a much narrower beach and the sand is coarser. Then you have the wide, long stretch of beach north of the rock which has all the restaurants and sun beds and whale tour touts. This beach has more space and is much more populated. There are bigger waves but also a good shallow swell for little kids to enjoy. There is also a life guard at the far south of the beach which is reassuring.  This is where all the action is - with cheap restaurants offering great "happy hours" in the evening. My daughters and I loved Mirissa because of the choice of two different beaches.

What's not to like about this beach it's beautiful, it's fringed with palm trees, the sea is clear, the sand is soft and it's clean. Even though Mirrisa is known as a tourist area the beach wasn't over crowded and It wasn't overly commercial which is great as a beach looses its identity if it's too commercial! It was also a great place to sunbathe and take photos. You'll find a rock in the middle of the beach which was a particularly good spot and view point. Moreover, the sea in Sri Lanka can get pretty rough so you'll generally find surfers. For those interested they were on the left hand side of the bay. Finally, Mirrisa is known for its whale watching which we unfortunately didn't do it but there's always next time. xox

Was really excited about ending my Sri Lanka trip in Mirissa Beach. Was happy that I had selected a hotel outside of the main area. Although beach was nice...Was disconcerted by the amount of garbage up the side streets and the bright blue River water emptying into the ocean (what got dumped into this river?). Only gem on this beach was the lovely man selling Beautiful handmade bags, skirts, and other clothing. Also concerned about reading that locals were turned away from frequenting bars and hotels. Hope that was not true.

The beach is very nice, it is all the beach side restaurants that need some work.   A fine place to spend a day, yet unless you are here to bum about or penny-pinch stay on the outskirts of this overpopulated area.
Nature is highly unpredictable in sharing its beauty. Each beach has its own beauty and to a nature lover each place offers a new feast. So is this beach
It's a busy spot with lots of beach front diners to choose from. It's nice to have a stroll up and down. Waves were fun!
Nice beach with bars and clean water! We enjoy it! Nice to visit at the night time and take a bear !!

This is a bit different from Dikwella Beach and places like that as it got a whole lot more going on, much more. Lots of diving, eating, drinking and sunbathing. It a good place to go for a bit of a night life and just to be it in all. No hassle from anyone, just sit, have a beer, go for a swim and watch the world go by.

Not too many hawkers trying to sell you stuff/ in fact the only salesmen were right at the entrance, selling whale watching tours. We didn't have anyone harass us while we were lounging. There are a decent amount of beach chairs, and the one we went to didn't appear to be charging for beds, but most people were buying drinks or some form of food. The water is gorgeous. The waves can get as high as 4 feet. We body surfed (300lkr an hour) had loads of fun. Depending on the day and time, the crowd varies. More people after 3pm. The mornings are usually quiet. Overall loved our time here. We've also spent time on weligama beach, hikkadua beach and unawatuna beach.

I've never seen a beach in Sri Lanka with so many people! Not too many people in the water as the sandy waves were a bit rough.  I would suggest heading to Mirakollita in Tangalle or one of the 5 beaches in the Unawatuna area.  Mirissa beach also has many restaurants to choose from but the service from staff and sometimes the food is poor!
We liked this beach mostly because of our Hotel Number one Mirissa, great food fun whale watching, but the loud music until 4am every night was a real bummer.
The place is so amazing, especially when there are no big waves. Crystal clear water and beautiful sandy beach. I really loved it here!

Mirissa beach is lovely, there is lots of space and plenty of options in terms of restaurants and bars. The waves are quite aggressive so only strong swimmers should venture into the sea. The sand is lovely and fine, no stones or shingles even when walking into the sea. The water is also very clear. I loved my couple of days spent at Mirissa beach!

Marissa beach, although not unpopulated but rather crowded is still beautiful and amazing place to visit. Waves are awesome to surf, food is great and overall everything's compact and easily accessible. Comparing to nearby Unawatuna this one is far better.

A beautiful palm fringed beach with lovely beach front restaurants. We stayed here for a week and could have stayed longer. The sand was soft and the sea was clear and clean. The sea could be a bit rough as you go further out but if you stay near the beach it is shallow and calmer. Great for body boarding and surfing. Hire shacks on the beach offer both. There was a life guard on duty when we were there. Lots of restaurants line the back of the beach and they all offer fresh fish, prawns, squid and lobster. A lovely relaxing beach and I would definitely return.

Pro: + Papa Mango - best place intimen for sun beds and beach + lot of sea food places on the beach + party every night in another bar during high season + surfing destination + diving, surf schools, Whale watchings offerings on the beach + maybe a good place to stay is Palm Villa but definitely not Wadiya Guest House + close to a turtle beach Con: - most sea side sea food restaurants don't have good quality (zephir is an exception for food quality but definitely not for service) - a lot of Beach boys - definitely no secret hideaway anymore - not good if you don't like waves - not a Perfect Sunset place

A good place to stay a few days. Nice and sandy beach. Prefer Unawatuna, but ths is not bad either. Can be current in the waters, so please be careful.Plenty of restaurants and bars along the beach. Enjoy !

The beach is packed we people but you can still have a great time. Water is good and you can surf. Usually at sunrise is the best. Don't forget that there is unfortunately a lack of surfer etiquette in Sri Lanka. I won't point fingers or even suggest a solution as it is quite obvious.(I mean if they managed to get better in Bali. It's possible). Be careful and do your best to lead by example.

This beach had it all...it was clean, had fun waves and soft sand! We were so sad that we had listened to reviews saying there was nothing to do in Mirissa but whale watch as we only booked 1 night here...I would have loved at least 2 or 3 as it was our favourite beach in Sri Lanka!

I researched this 3 month long trip in India and Sri Lanka and all I ever read was how wonderful Mirissa was.  It's not that wonderful.  Its a nice beach, but access to the beach is limited by the very busy road which runs along it and there are VERY FEW reasonably priced hotels actually on the beach.  We are staying at a horribly over priced hotel 8 minute walk from the beach and have to risk our lives every time we want to cross that highway.  In addition, the trash is worse than the trash in the north Goa beaches in India.  We had to find a path through a trash pile from the highway to the beach.  The beach is full of people  - jam packed and not mellow at all.  I would not recommend Mirissa to my friends for a good beach experience unless they stayed in a hotel with a private beach.  Not worth it.  I think the east coast of Sri Lanka is the place for mellow beaches.
Fantastic beach(es) spread out over three or four bays.  Suitable for swimming and surfing - nice combination.
Good swimming, great beach, good body surfing and surfing. Nice restaurants on the beach. Various activities

Mirissa is a very nice and clean beach. Sometimes the waves gets too big so it is hard to swim. Plenty of options for lunch and dinner. There are more young than old people on the beach and in the middle of it they play loud music to late night but it was not especially disturbing.
Nice beach to chill out, quite crowded but for me ok. Good for swimming. The sand is wonderful :) At night is this beach very lively, lot of bars and also party
It is a nice beach with a good sunset, but nothing mind blowing. The waves are very strong! And very sandy. Not much to my liking. The sunset saved the day for me
No harrasment, clean beach and good for snorkeling, cheap prices than hikkaduwa. There is lots of bars and restaurant with hammock on the beach, so u can easyli get food or drinks. I love it.

Fantastic beach, watched turtles come out of the water and lay their eggs. Whale watching is a must but chose wisely. We went with "Raj & the Whales" these guys work with scientists and will not chase whales. They care about wildlife and not money.

Served cold chips with hamburger and waiters were not able to handle the situation, result was a destroyed evening with no food for my friend. Beer size in menue is 500 ml but they serve 300 ml at only slightly lower price. We feel cheated and would not recommend the place at all.

The beach and bay are beautiful but they are badly let down by the local infrastructure. The lack of sewage treatment and rubbish collection means the beach (and the sea) are very dirty. Even after showering the smell of the sea stays on your skin. Access to the beach is difficult and poor, clearly evident that there are no decent planning regulations in place.
It might not look as a great beach, but it was OK. Just for relaxing. Besides the sunrises and sunsets from the rock are wonderful. It's worth to get earlier in the morning. :)
We enjoyed lot at this place and this place is very attractive and better place to rest and restaurants around the beach make it better and awesome.. Everyone who visited LK must to go there..

I didn't have high hopes for Mirissa as so many of Sri Lanka's beaches are dirty and full of rubbish. I was delighted to find that the beach was pretty much litter free even though it is very busy. The sea is clean and the restaurants provide good food at a reasonable price. Mirissa is a shining example to many other beaches in Sri Lanka.
Mirissa beach is a wonderful beach, enough people to make it interesting but not overcrowded. Great lunch and dinner venues along the beach and great surfing.

swimming, snorckling, diving, surfing. Its such an amazing area with alot of tourists from all over. You go to the beach and enjoy sipping a cold beer and a cool chat with people as they are all so friendly

I loved this beach.  The weather was hot but there's a lovely breeze which makes it bearable.  Lots of low key bar/restaurants which shield the beach from road noise.  The sea was lovely but with strong waves which can knock you over - children would need supervision - but great fun and good swimming beyond the waves.

We Visited mirissa beach we stayed in hotel Glamour Mirissa. It's nice place to stay because you have all there. If you want rest you can go to "black beach" and just relax under palms. If you want bars, music and more people you can go to main beach and if you want try surf, watch whales and diving or snorchling it's all there :)

This beach is wonderful! The main beach is full of restaurants and hotels but also have some spots were the palms have been allowed to grow close to the water. We did not think the beach was overcrowded or that is was difficult to find a spot to sunbathe. In the southern part of the beach there is a smaller bay that are somewhat more secluded. The north part of that bay, close to a little private island is calm and good for swimming with children, and have some spots good for snorkling. The south part of the bay has somewhat more waves but also a lot more palms that gives wonderful shade in the middle of the day...

Mirissa is a bay. Excellent beach. Mirissa can be reached by road from Matara on the southern coast of Sri Lanka. There are lot of buses passing through Mirissa since it is on the Colombo - Matara road. The journey from Matara to Mirissa will take about 20 minutes by bus. There are many places you can stay depending on the amount you want to spend. Resorts / hotels with access directly to beach will be a bit more expensive than the ones across the road. You can get a room from 1500 LKR to 15000 LKR.  If you want a budget accommodation there are several available across the road from the beach within short walking distance. there are also restaurants by the beach side where you can enjoy a meal or a drink. If you are a beach lover you will love this place. for food just taste the local food from road side joints. Restaurants I found are more expensive here. I heard this is the best place for Whale / dolphin watching. Check out the prices before you strike a deal for a trip to sea, Nothing else much in this place other than the beach.

I had to take my business friends from china to Mirissa when they visited in August last year and I must say that I absolutely enjoyed the whole tour. We stayed 2 nights and the highlight was whale watching! we saw like 2 or 3 whales and one was so close to our boat...that really was an experience! The beach is so clean and so much relaxing; would recommend to any1.

If you are over the age of 25, enjoy peace and tranquility, and didn't travel all the way to Sri Lanka just to party with other westerners then you probably won't like Mirissa Beach. We severely disliked it. Had dinner at two subpar, packed restaurants.  Rented lounge chairs for $12 one afternoon and left after an hour.  So we have it 3 tries. Sri Lanka is a modest place yet girls donned thong bikinis and got drunk like it was spring break in Cabo. The beach itself is nice enough, but nothing very special (I can think of 50 beaches in the US that are much nicer just off the top of my head). If you are young and here to party instead of here to appreciate culture then I guess this is the beach for you.
The only negative thing is that there's a lot of tourists. Beyond that, the water is warm and clear and the beach is clean.
We headed towards Mirissa beach after the whale watching. It's calm, serene and breathtakingly beautiful. Enjoy the waves kissing the shore with chilled beer.

Had a day at the beach in Mirissa. The beach itself is very nice, the sand is perfect and the water nice. We had big waves which was fun. Just right next to the beach there is tons of garbage and this makes the experience a bit less joyful than it could have been. Why don't they hire a couple of guys to pick it up??

We came to Mirissa a few days over our stay in Sri Lanka. A good pretty safe beach with lots of beach bars/restaurants- which seem to also have a great nightlife (not that we enjoyed due to young children!). Worth the stop/stay whilst in Sri Lanka!

We visited a few beaches at the southern part of Sri Lanka having in mind that we read Unawatana is the most beautiful one. Well, I don't agree, I think that Mirissa beach is the best. Yes, it is little bit crowded with tourists but still that cannot change its attractiveness. A lot of nice restaurants and bars that you can visit at night time. If weather is with you, as whole it is a pure joy :)

It's a beautiful beach with clear blue green water. Go in the evening time for sure and you will see all resturant providing candle light tables for a beautiful relaxing evening  at the beach. Food and liquor offers are at very reasonable prices. Do note that post 10 pm most of the outlets play loud music for a party scene.

Skip Mirissa if you are looking for true hidden paradise, peace and tranquility to unwind in an authentic beach in SL! Awful place! It's a first time I went to Mirissa beach only for an afternoon walk.. to check for a place.. Such a disappointment! It wouldn't suit me much to waste my time and money for spending a night close by. I've heard it's one of the best beach in SL but it's not true! Far to be called a piece of heaven and untouched paradise! I didn't even find it has some charm.. maybe a hippie style, yes! Set in a very small bay, it's not a serene, unspoilt and cleanest beach but overcrowded and overbuilt touristic place. Mirissa remains to be massively popular among the tourists who like to be mixed with a lot of others tourists looking for lots of bars and parties with loud music every evening.

Perhaps one of the most touristy beaches in Sri Lanka but fortunately no beach vendors approaching you all day long (which happens in unawatuna). Water is often quite rough so not the best beach for small children although it is shallow for a good little stretch.  Restaurants on the beach are okay. Yet to find one truly outstanding.

The beaches in the south of mirissa vary in nature. However mirissa beach offers a place where everyone cab relax and swim in peace. It is not really a surf beach. The waves are small making it perfect and safe for children and families.
Had a very romantic candlelit meal on the beach in Mirissa with the surf lapping our ankles and the full moon rising. Stunning.
Spent 6 days here, was not too crowded, very nice beach, happy hour cheap beer, great selection of fish for dinner, nice big waves
Mirissa is an excellent beach, good for both swimming and surfing, with many restaurants and bars right on the beach.
Mirissa is quite beach area with waves for sup surfers and wave bords. Great food and beer , you can rent bords to surf .
Tourist place - it looks like a funfair. 5 years ago it was a special magical place. But now it is just full of restaurants and the magic is gone. :(

A really popular beach among tourists, which means a lot of restaurants and people selling whale watching tours.. The sun chairs are free which is nice. It's a big beach so it's possible to get away. If you get bored on sunbathing you can watch the surfers in the bay or rent a body board. We had two nice days at the beach!

My husband and I surf but we also have an 18 month old. We were worried that Mirissa wouldnt work for out little one but in fact there is a calm spot just down from Number One Mirissa that is fantastic.

Marissa Beach is a typical sandy beach lined with many bars, eateries and resorts.  So if you are going to eat or drink you will have a wide choice of price ranges.  There are also a number of different massage offerings. The beach itself is clean and reportedly safe.

We are come to mirissa for swimming and take a lunch. Long bay beach and nice small resturent on the beach.good relaxing on the beach. Mirissa is Paradise for surfing people. Spend your enjoy  holiday with mirissa beach...
Mirissa beach is a great place to get away from it all and relax, eat good food, snorkel, surf and meet fellow travellers and lovely locals.
Absolutely gorgeous. We had such a lovely time here and then went on to whale watching. Spectacular.

First of all, there were waves as high as 4 meters, crashing just a few meters from the shore. Swimming was impossible. I had fun, I won't deny it, playing like a kid with the waves... but it wasn't ideal to relax in the water, and I would certainly not trust children to be left by themselves in the water. Apparently this is not always the case, and in December and January the sea is calmer, but during our stay this is what we found. The real problem, however, is that the beach is quite overcrowded, with bars and stands leaving not much space. Finding a seabed is nearly impossible, and a lot of the bars aren't even nice. Last, the main road runs just behind the beach and is always, constantly trafficked. It's maybe worth spending a couple of days, but that's it. Certainly, I'd recommend whale watching (with the proper service... some are tourist traps: don't trust the cheaper offers). But in terms of beach and sea, I enjoyed ways more Unawatuna and Bentota.

Don't believe the guide books that describe Mirissa as unspoilt or only starting to develop. This is an overbuilt, busy beach which is great of you want lots of bars and parties. Awful if you want peace and quiet. The quality of food served at the beach cafes is generally dreadful.

Mirissa Beach is very calm and beautifull beach with minimum of turists. Lots of restaurants with tasty and cheap food. Close to beach is many little shops with fruits and the other snacks. On the other hand, it is not good place for swimming, because the ocean is wild with big waves, but we enjoy a lot of funny there.

We based ourselves in Hikkaduwa and decided to spend the day in Mirissa Beach, sleep over and book a whale watching excursion. All three of us felt the same way. Mirissa Beach was more dirty in terms of trash everywhere. We also saw more mosquitos. We would recommend Bara Beach, Weligama beaches or Hikkaduwa if you plan to stay for a week. Mirissa Beach is something I'd recommend to visit for a day just to check out the mini island and whale watching. This is three Canadians opinion to each there own. The water is def calmer here, great for young children.

To be honest when I read comments on Trip advisor about Mirissa I was hesitating to go there because everybody was complaning about crowded beach. We were there at February it was a very sunny and clear day (32 degree no rain, no clouds), we had sun bath at the very end of the beach (Papa Mango), swimmed there and as lunch we had fish. I would recommend this place.
Waves were large again tomes, great for surfers.  We snorkeled with turtles and fish. We ate our dinner with the sea lapping our feet

Mirissa has a really nice beach. Enough soft sand to lay on with both sunny and shady spots. Altough there can be some big waves, the water is clear and clean. Good to have a swim. Some nice beach cafés with sometimes live Music in the evening. We really loved Mirissa!
The beach here excellent but the waves are big and powerful with a strong undertow, great for surfing though.
The beach is broad and sandy, lost of fish near the beach, good for snorkeling, surfing. Lots of restaurants with fresh fish, young people. You can see the sunrise and the sunset!
Another beautiful beach and Sri Lanka, however during the day are bit over run by tourism. I guess this is something that you can expect from such a popular destination

Maybe this seems too harsh but this is not Mirissa as it used to be! Stunningly beautiful, secluded, clean and untouched. I've rated it very good mostly because I remember Mirissa as it used to be some 4 or 5 years before. At that time I preferred Mirissa to many fancy places as Maldives, Seychelles or Brazil beaches. Coming again was a mistake. It was quite painful to see what has my once favorite beach turn to: overcrowded, polluted, dirty ... I better stick to nice memories I have about this beach and start searching somewhere on the East coast ...
Great, clean beach good for surfers and for people to relax. Good restaurants along beachfront as well. Highly recommended
On return from our 1 night whale watching boat trip,we stayed 3 nights at lovely/friendly AussieSwiss Resort on Mirissa Beach.

One of very beautiful beach in Sri Lanka 🇱🇰. Very beautiful around Giragala small island 🌴. You can see sunset in Giragala Island you can walk through the beach to island. But the bad thing is fake whales watching groups in the beach there are some people trying you to sell whales watching tickets but I can recommend their boats and services if you are travel with you guide take a help from him and if you want book you selves visit Mirissa Harbor and do it. ( Just 5 km )

The beach is definitely beautiful and if you want to be surrounded by other people, bars and restaurants, it is ideal. However, if you are looking for true paradise, peace and tranquillity, you just need to travel 4 km away to find another beautiful beach. There are signs everywhere in Mirissa stating 'foreigners only' which may contribute to the coldness of the local people towards tourists which is not evident everywhere else in Sri Lanka. Everything is also overpriced including food, excursions and souvenirs.
Very beautiful beach, warm ocean, big waves. We ranted a bodyboard for 400rs. and had a great time at the beach.

Mirissa Beach is a happening place in the small town of Mirissa where people come to go on whale watching safaris. The beach is very clean. It is dotted with eateries of all kinds. The sea food on offer is phenomenal. The crowd is a decent bunch..many are families with kids in tow which seemed to indicate (to me) that this is a family friendly town and beach. We walked along the beach for a while as the tide came in and teh waves wet out feet. It was a very relaxing experience.

Very nice beach wirh lots of space. Not too crowded for the main beach and almost no "beach boys". We had huge waves and lots of fun. Only problem, no shade. In the evening its very nice for dinner. Great time here
Dirty,Overcrowded, Polluted, Noisy. If you have time go further East   and North from Tangale where you will find some nice stretches of Sand.

Situated in a bay, beach not too wide and fairly empty being mainly used by tourists. A few bars and eating places. Water can be tricky. Beach shelves very quickly and children should be looked after carefully. Surfing towards harbour end.
Crowded and noisy beach.high waves so difficult to swim but sand,long beach. If you like party beach you can go there for Peace and quiet should go somewhere else.
The rumors are true. Many establishments ( bars, restaurants and even hotels) outright refuse service to locals here. Pity that a beautiful beach is shadowed by this culture.

The beach is long and wide, packed with tourists but the crowd is laid back. There is none of the rowdiness or tackiness associated with say Patong or Kuta. The sea water is also clear and clean! Go but please don't ruin the vibe!

Very beautiful and clean beach with big waves and lots of good restaurants, san beds in the restran are free of charge but you will regularly ask you to remove from them because if about 5 o'clock in the afternoon sun beds replace tables for dining in front of them will stand freshly caught fish that will prepare you in the restaurant for dinner at very reasonable prices

First time ever coming to Mirissa Beach, and I wish I had come before. This is just the perfect combination of beach, ocean and some great little places along the beach where you can enjoy a delicious meal and refreshing drink. The beach itself is clean and not too overcrowded. I will definitely be coming back.
Came here with my boyfriend for 2 days. Loved it! Good bars and restaurants all the way along the beach. Beautiful golden sand and blue water
Superb beach area clean and with plenty of restaurants from one end to the other. Good for surfing and for water sports.
A 2 day weekend on probably the best beach in Sri Lanka!! Clear waters, soft sand, whale & dolphin watching.....
It became some self full-filling prophecy. The beach hosts simple places, bars, hotels.... yet not to busy but tourists will find alike people
The most beautiful beach! Incredible views each way you looked! Great restaurants all along the beach, could have spent ages here!

We went to 3 beaches in Sri Lanka, hikkadua, unawatuna and Mirissa. This was my least favourite when i was expecting it to be the best? It's majorly over crowded. Which I understand it was high season but una and hikka were no where near as busy. But most of all it was the food situation! I'm a massive foodie and apart from one place on the beach there was no decent food at all!!! There's loads in hikka and una. Unawatuna over Mirissa any day or night for that matter!

After having booked in advance accommodation in this area, we decided to leave as soon as possible. The place is overcrowded, noisy, dirty and full of tourist traps. Possibly one of the worst spots I've suffered during my travels in Asia. Be also aware of the waiters and several places that live exclusively from tourists, as they will try to take advantage from you in any situation.
Bright, Sunny Beach for the perfect tan.. Surrounded by shacks & restaurants serving local beer & yum srilankan food
The beach can get a little rough but their are warning flags to help you understand the danger level of the sea if your swimming.

You can definitely have a great time in Mirissa, it has the long stretch of beach, heaps of restaurants on the beach, surf, safe swimming areas and a safe vibe. It also is located right next to a busy stretch of road, has more than its fair share of rubbish both in the water and on the side of the road, and has heaps of tourist. I believe if you do your research, you will find a nicer beach either south or north of Mirissa.
Great beach to both stroll and stay at, go there when you are in town! Its nice for surfing, sunbathing and swimming.

Loved the atmosphere- we went around 6 pm to the Mirissa beach and was surprised to see the number of  seafood cafes along the beach. Service was a bit slow as the place was full of tourists and almost every cafe was full. Thoroughly enjoyed the night and the food was excellent.
It was awesome, and even you can enjoy very well around the beach area. Suggestions best for Diving, Scuba Diving etc.

There are two breaks at extreme ends of the beach - a left and a right point. The right reminds me of Noosa. It doesn't take much of a crowd to make the right difficult, but a top wave. The left was great, but the second day a bunch of Euro surfer friends came out and conspired that they got all the decent waves.

Quite busy little village. Lots of tourist and food are quite expensive in the restaurant but if you look around, there are little cafe/mini resto serves good food. Dewmini restaurant is the best place to go for food.

Horrible overcrowded beach. Every last inch of sand covered with cheap plastic chairs and loungers. Tacky bars and shops selling tourist tat. Hundreds of people. Honestly terrible, noisy and dirty. 90's pop music blasting from the bars at 8 am. Tropical island paridise? I think not. Don't waste your time. Go to one of Sri Lanka's other much more beautiful and peaceful beach's where you can relax and enjoy the natural surroundings.
Nice beach & has lots of restaurants which grill fresh seafood food for you! Nice for surfing & swimming! I liked walking there during the sunset.

This was our last stop in Sri Lanka, we had visited so many other beaches but we certainly appreciated this one the most. It is very clean and all the facilities you can ask for. Great relaxing atmosphere during the day and a lovely romantic candle light dinners on the beach at night. Certainly great for music and dancing too. But that wasn't our scene. Our highlight was the whale watching tour. We saw 11 Blue whales and a Brydes whale. It was a perfect spot to spend 4 nights.

After the 2004 tsunami legislation was passed that all establishments need to be at least 100m back from the beach. This is evidently no where more in breach than Mirissa, where restaurants lay their chairs right up and actually over the waters edge. While pleasant for an afternoon drink, the restaurants threaten to remove the very essence and beauty of the beach. The water itself has waves, with a good break for surfers at the western end and an interesting little island to be climbed at the northern end. All in all not a bad beach, but better can be found further east.
Lovely and guaranteed to see whales and swim and surf safely, we stayed in January and no rip tide???!!

Fine beach with plenty of opportunities for all kinds of activities. Wide and long stretch of nice, white sand and a nice sea to cool down in. In some of the parts you need to watch your feet in the water, it can get rocky. Also, the sea can be quite wavy, with a bit of an undercurrent, making it less suitable for lazily floating around  (which is what I like to do :-)). Beach is quite clean and loads of bars and restaurants are available for the inner beach bum. Close proximity of the main road is mostly not an issue.

My kids were pulled out to sea in a rip tide and had to be rescued by lifeguards as well as another teenager. I do not think it is safe for swimming. When I said there should be warning signs to a local bar owner he said that would be bad for business. The experience was terrifying and the lifeguards reported it happens every day.
beautiful place although not a sunny day, sand & overall environment is great. love the little island you could walk across the sea & getting another view of beach. night time also hilarious. good

Im disapointed  with most of places in Sri Lanka i stayed, except Mirrissa. Over all sri Lanka is beautiful. But the culture of taking money of the tourist makes the trip really bad. Prices the charge for rooms with no quality. Tuk tuk, even the parks have prices for tourist and locals....if the goverment alows this,of course the rest of the people makes the same. The only place i didnt feel this was in Mirissa. Super beautiful,calm and smiling people. I end up stayed there more time because i didnt feel rip off  and i feel at home. The beachea im Mirissa and around are the best in Sri Lanka and the town is small...just loved....
The beach is clean and small hardly 1km, Water is clean , big rock to climb but not for every1 as it can be dangerous. Food is not expensive , nice place to relax , swim n surf

What was once a lovely little bay is now crammed full of bars,resteraunts, whale tour / surfing paraphernalia, it's just not a pleasant place to be. Prices are high and standards are low. It's all about fleecing the tourist. Couldn't get out of there quick enough.
Very cosy, beautifull beach for a great day of relaxing. In the night good party,s in the beach bars

Very clean beach, nice big waves to keep our 6-year-old entertained all day, boogies boards to rent for cheap (Rs 300/hour), restaurants on the beach for a bite or a beer, and a liberal offering of beach chairs to lay on. Very friendly environment where one will find strictly other tourists frolicking in the waves. All the locals are staffing the eateries. A bit trashy to get to it from the road where trash literally piles up and into the street. But the beach itself was pristine and held plenty of great views. This is a must-see!
Hello everyone! You should visit on Mirissa Beach! There You can buy fresh fish from ocean. The mail reason is a beautifull view.

Every restaurant and bar we visited had appalling service. Lots and lots of male waiters sitting around, never acknowledging your existence as a customer and not caring that you want to spend money in their establishment. In one I waited over 30 minutes for a gin and tonic whilst they tried to bring me prawns and various other items I didn't order and then tried to make me pay for them at the end anyway. The food is pretty good on the beach but service is apathetic and that really ruins a mood in a lovely location.
Cool beach with nice people. In my opinion too many tourists. But nice restaurants directly on the sea side

Mirissa is crowded and dirty. Very narrow and busy highway splits between the beach and most accommodations. Any restaurant or grocery has to be accessed by walking, or taking a tuk tuk. We started here but quickly found Kogalla Beach about 40 minutes north. Mirissa has a hippie vibe, which is fine, but not for us. Also lots of Chinese tourists. Curious mix. But dirty--just dirty.

The beach is packed full of bars and restaurants but has plenty of room for sun baking and swimming. There's lots of surfing on the back waves. Climbing up the little rock to see all the beaches is the highlight and it's a pretty amazing spot to watch the sunset!! Plenty of activities to offer such as learning to surf, snorkelling and jet skiing.
Wonderful beach and waves; relaxing holiday and valuable fresh fruit juice. Calm place to stay and very cleaning beach.
Mirissa beach very fermus for the (whale whacing and dolphin ) ........ and beach side restaurant ,fresh sheafood, ........ very good beach clean and relax........ my custemers are very happy ......
The waves are fun to jump in and over. Also more quiet place to swim. Not the best beach for children - you have to keep an eye on them all the time, because it gets deep quickly.

We were in a Guesthouse away from beach, near the quiet (north) end of the bay which was nice, no party noise at night, restaurants to choose from in the day when on the beach near us and many restaurants farther away for supper but still a short walk. The younger backpacker crew seemed to hang out more on the other end which was fine with us, quiet at night.  The beach is a nice firm sand and the water can be rough with an undertow which can sweep a person out to sea, if not a strong swimmer beware and stay in waist deep water at most.
Nice and quiet and nice walks available and very good for swimming we really enjoyed every moment spent there!

The Mirissa Beach is nice and clean. The waves are good (even if sometimes are quite big, but not that big like in Hikka). But take care (as usually) because sometimes you can catch a big wave and as I saw, there is no lifeguard. And wasn't crowded, that was good too.
This was amazing and a mix of travelers, local cafes and road side restaurants very friendly, this beach is comfortable for surfing and swim also

Some of my friends were raving about Mirissa, so I figured it would be a good idea to spend New Year's eve there. Big mistake. The beach is overcrowded with restaurants and their cheap plastic chairs, tables and beach beds. Allegedly, this was a nice beach about five years ago, but now you better avoid it.

Mirissa is a pretty busy with tourists in high season,pricy ,but still good place to surf having 2 reef breaks good for both begginers and advanced surfers,nice Parrot rock -best place to meet sunrise and finish your day watching sunsets.Plenty of restaurants, night parties 7 days a week(November-April).Possible to snorkel on a calm day. Nice beach for children.
Some areas are clean. Whale watching and sight seeing are promoted in the area. Restaurants offer lot of fresh seafood. 4 star hotels are nearby. Bus and tuck tuck  services are good.
I was expecting a calm, beautiful beach, similar to Unawatuna, was I mistaken, it was chaotic full of young people lounging about on scruffy beach furniture yuk
Good safety beach for sea bathing. and good waves for surfing. I swam to far on the sea. some lifeguard are there. but keep your safety first

The beach is one of the most delightful that I have come across in Sri Lanka. It is in a Bay with headlands at either end and so is very scenic. The sand is perfect being very fine and clean and soft enough for children to build sandcastles. The sea is not too rough and is gorgeous for swimming. There are also lifeguards on duty all day.
One of the nicest beaches we have seen in Sri Lanka. There is still some litter at the entrance to the beach next to the road, hopefully it will be removed in the future.

Fantastic Beach - many bars to the far side of the beach closer to where it bends offer free chairs, you can also negotiate with other vendors if you eat there. Waves are great, no peddlers selling you stuff and really chilled out.

A mostly clean beach with turquise water, powder-like sand and narrow sea. The waves offer a playground but should not be underestimated (as a non-surfer). Amazing sunset - don't miss it. At night it turns to a party location for tourists.

Clean golden sand though the waves can be very strong. Popular with surfers and bodyboarders, with equipment or lessons being  freely available. A section of the beach has lifeguard station. Entire beach is lined with bars, restuarnts and sightseeing stalls but all low key and no pressure sales or hawkers. All in all a good place to hang out

This has been our favourite beach so far of Sri Lanka - you can walk the whole of the beach in about 15 minutes, so it's quite small, but there are lots of restaurants, bars, and surf shops. Plenty to do. Our favourite part of the beach was the tiny island that you have to walk in the sea to get to. You can get some amazing views from it and watch the surfers wipeout!
Bars, restaurants, loungers, surf to bodysurf in.  Close to road and no litter bins so leave only footprints

good beach .... the best we visited is the one on the way to unawathuna.... pleasant  clear water ... for best experince of all the activities  Unawatuna specializes in surfing.. hikkaduwa for snorkeling... etc

We only stayed 1 day in Mirissa and regret that most of our time was booked for Unawatuna.  In comparison Unawatuna is full of tourists and there is rubbish on the sand because of the restaurants on the beach.  In comparison Mirssa beach is flat and clean and absolutely stunning.
My friend and I visited Mirissa, Unawatuna and Hikkaduwa and Mirissa was our pick for a mixture of relaxing and happening atmosphere.
Nice beach. Especially for surfing. Mirissa in a good for combination with experience the  hole sound coast .

A nice stretch of white sand edged with palmtrees. with plenty of sunbeds and eateries it's perfect for a day's rest. The waves were good for bodysurfing and if you wanna take a ride on a jetski that's possible too. During the evenings all  restaurants put out candles and it looks very cosy and welcoming.
The sand of the beach is marvelous! So fine and the see clear and gentle! The beach restaurants offer a great range of good food!

Mirissa Beach is a lovely curved bay lined with palm trees, small beach bars and restaurants and a couple of medium sized hotels. A lovely spot for bodyboarding or just playing in the sea on the main beach. A good reef break righthander at the west end of the beach. Mirissa is getting busier and busier. It won't be long before the big chain hotels move in as is happening at Weligama just up the coast. Visit soon.

You will find this beach on the way to Galle. I guess, it is the southern most tip of the island. It is one of the most serene and cleanest beaches I have ever watched. It is the best place to finish your day. Watch the splendid sunset here and have a cool beer to chill with your friends to unwind. Must visit place!
Fantastic beach here. Solid waves, solid restaurants, beautiful hotels and even a smaller tide pool area that is perfect for swimming, especially with young kids. Will definitely visit again.
Comparing to Tangalle, this beach is less wawy, you can even snorkel here. Many bars and restaurant on the beach, vut everything rather in small or hippie štýle, no big hotels.
There are a lot of people here. Beach is very clean (on the sand near the water). Waves are small, so it's good for swimming and children. Only few places in the shadow. Too much bars/restaurants.

Beach: clean, good sea and waves; Parrot Rock a good place for a brief explore or sunset Catering: varied.  Some good places, some much of a muchness and pretty uninspiring. Lots of seafood on sale in the early evening.

Average beach, just due to its business, however a short walk east an there are some nicer quieter beaches, which are great for snorkeling, saw a green turtle and a variety of fish every time we went out. On the main beach there are plenty of over priced beach restaurants and places to hired snorkels and surfboards, how ever the surf breaks at least 100 meters out on a reef not so good for beginers. ( the next main beach west, about 10 min drive is much better for beginners). The beach is a cool place to base your self but rent a scooter and take some day trips up and down the coast to see more Sri Lankan beauty than an over populated tourist hotspot.
mirissa beach was excellent.mirissa beach can surfing and we can had rest in mirissa beach.i highly reccomend mirissa beach.

Mirissa beach is a beautiful stretch of clean pristine beach. There are a lot of surfing and other water sports options that one can use. In addition to that the beach side eateries have great food and host parties every night.

Best fun is playing in the waves. If your a surfer it looks great and is a reputable place for the sport. We are not surfers but enjoyed playing in the waves close to the beach. Lots of restaurants directly on the beach.

If all the hotels and bars stuck to the law and stayed 100m back from the tide line this beach would be great. At night it is lit up like a Christmas tree complete with lights and spotlights. The saddest thing is turtles lay eggs on this beach. We saw baby turtles emerging from under a deck at the Zephyr bar and due to all the lights heading into the bar or along the beach rather than into the ocean. It is beaches like this that will cause sea turtles to go extinct. The beach is clean except for the few public entrances that aren't through hotels which are like garbage dumps. Nice sand and fun waves to play in.
Saw Blue Whales as well as dolphins. Also enjoyed sea fishing and catching Red Snapper. Chose local beach grill to cook it with chips and salad

Mirissa and its breathtaking sandy beach pretty much transforms your dreams and visions of a tropical paradise into an everyday reality. Located close to the Southern tip of the Island of Sri Lanka and only about 200 km from the Equator, this secluded crescent shaped beach is the perfect place to sit back, relax and forget about all the hussle and bussle of your other life that’s a million miles away. This small sandy tropical beach boasts some of Sri Lanka’s best and most stunning sunsets and sunrises. All the Guest Houses in Mirissa are set back from the actual beach giving you the impression that you are on a deserted palm fringed island. Every now and again the silence is broken by the sound of a coconut falling on the sand or a chilled beer being opened by someone further up the beach. Mirissa Beach Sri Lanka

It's pretty sad what's been done with this beach. It could be a gorgeous place, but its been completely ruined by tourism. The beach is full of restaurants with the music terribly loud and sunbeds (or tables at night) covering all the sand. The beach is crowded and there are even water scooters in the water, which is not too clean. If you like quiet paradise beaches, go to Tangalle and the nearby beaches.

Mirissa beach is a perfect place - lot of restaurants with sunbeds for rent, yellow sand.. The sea is perfectly clean and warm but is not very suitable for swimming, it is shallow and there are big wawes - but that is why it is so good for surfing.

Not my sort of beach. Too busy - tourists wall to wall. No idea what time you'd need to get there to grab a beach lounge so if you want any shade that leaves the alternative of sitting under the trees at the back of the beach - not a great idea if they're coconut trees! A place called Secret Beach was recommended. We didn't get there but it might be worth checking out if you want some where a little quieter.
This is a really nice beach and we wouldn't have gone to any of the more popular ones. Not many kids, no old people, enough room for your towel to lay down. I hope it stays the same.
I have never seen a beach in Asia this busy but it was around New Years. Good swimming. Waves but still fun. Many surfers.
Safe beach, no hawkers. Clean with plenty of places to eat "Paradise" take time to choose your place, we always stop by for a drink first and if food looks okay we return.
theres not much beach left when the tide comes in, but its sorta part of the fun to watch the beach chairs almost get taken away! good surf and boogey sport spots. pretty beach
The beaches are beautiful. However the peacefulness is disturbed by a big road just behind. Environnement seems not respected (rubbish and wild constructions).
Top notch spot. Beautiful beach. Lots of places to eat. Friendly people and all you need for a beach holiday
We went at 8am before the sun hot too hot! It was lovely and clean and had its own personality! Absolutely lovely!

When we first arrived we were a little shocked by how busy the beach was. It was New Year's so our visit may have been the exception. Once we got over the initial shock that it wasn't a quiet, secluded beach and that we would need to share, we really enjoyed our stay. The waves were great, there is a lifeguard so we felt safer and access to good food was just a matter of walking up the beach. If you do want a quieter beach then you can head a little bit north to Welligama. It's a short bus trip away and you can enjoy amazing seafood straight from the ocean.

It's a sight to behold. The beach is great and has beautiful surroundings. You can lay on sunbeds, climb the amazing rock to view the sunset and enjoy your time there. In the morning people are running across the beach. The waves may be big though, so be careful. Extra point for cleaninness: because the whole beach is covered with restaraunts, they clean the area every day. A pleasure to be there.

After spending some time in other parts of Sri Lanka it was a little shocking at first to see women in bikinis and men without shirts on here, but it quickly became normal again and was very nice to feel free on the beach.  A gorgeous beach it is too - sweeping around the bay with fine white sand and palm trees.  The restaurants serve delicious fresh seafood at reasonable prices, and since they're all only 2 storeys high they make a pretty backdrop rather than a monstrous eyesore.

Coming from Australia the beach itself is nothing special. About 2 km of brownish sand and average waves. But. The beach is lined right to the waterfront with so many restaurants and cafes. Sunbeds and snorkel vendors. We went in peak season. While it was busy we could still find a shady spot to sit and a free spot to swim. The people watching is great as there are folks here from all walks of life. There are also a few other beaches within 30 mins that are much quite should you desire. One of the best places we have visited in Sri Lanka. Loads of fun.

Restaurants line the waterfront and tourists are absolutely everywhere. We were here for new years and Xmas though so maybe it was busier than usual. Great for more western type food options and to go out at night. We don't like partying but still found the atmosphere nice. Definitely more pricey for everything than some other places in Sri Lanka. The beach has nice big and safe waves to play it and both ends of the beach are great for surfing so would definitely recommend if you like to have fun in the water rather than just swim in calm water. Overall I'd recommend staying here if you are happy to be where everyone else is :)

Finally i shorten my stay to only 1 day in Mirissa. Generally Mirissa is busy, loud and dirty (garbage visible everywhere). Nothing to compare to Unawatuna or super nice Goyambokka beach. Going to beach via paths between houses, is like thought garbage place. If you look for nightlife i would choose Unawatuna beach or if you look for nice looking quiet beach i would go to my favourite Goyambokka beach in Tangalle.

I stayed at a hotel near the beach. This being an open beach attracts a lot of crowd. But there are a lot of restaurants and you can take a long walk on the sand. If you are in Mirissa, don't miss this place (unless you are staying at a hotel which has a private beach).
Really nice beach, with big waves. The beach is clean and has a good selection of bars and restaurants.

Mirissa beach is one of the best beaches in Sri Lanka. And it's a top tourist destination in the country. There are activities available like surfing, whale watching and diving.. Beach is clean and has a breathtaking view. There are plenty of hotels and guest houses to stay and nice beach restaurants to eat or have a drink. Usually Mirissa gets really crowded with local and foreign visitors in December and there is a lot of beach parties going on in 31st of December.
Its a clean nice Beach. The Water is perfect and clear :) Some tourists and almost no Sri Lankans .. :)

We were amazed to find a family friendly beach that was not only clean but free of vendors with good beach shack food and plenty of walking space, a volleyball net, surfboard rentals and decent waves!!!

This is a very nice beach with a chill vibe. I've been to beaches all over the world and this rates in my top 3. If you don't like waves, maybe choose another but my tween-aged kids loved the waves and the wave boarding. Many chairs to choose from early in  the day with umbrellas, free if you buy a drink or two. Happy hour starts at 4! The bars on the beach do stay open late so if you are a light sleeper or have kids, maybe you want to stay off the beach. Most hotels are just a short walk from the main drag but the noise is better.

People rave about this beach and I cannot understand why ? !! If you like advertising signs and rubbish , piles at the entrance , building sites , large western beach style overpriced crappy food restaurants then by all means go .
This was probably a gorgeous place until massive new tourism developments, right on the edge of the water, were built. It had an unpleasant atmosphere, because of the masses of people.

We have read many good things about Mirissa beach in Lonely planet. The version was from Jan 2015.  It described Mirissa as a lovely beach without too many people. When we arrived it was packed! The beach was filled with sun beds, umbrellas, whale trip signs. Too much of everything! We have been to many different towns in Sri Lanka and have only meet smiling, nice and welcoming people. Here it seemed like they were very tired off tourists, understandable! The main road is noisy and many of the guests houses and hotels are placed on both sides off the road. We cancelled our booking and left after one day. I would choose some of the other beaches further east.
Surf is up from dawn to dusk. Never got tired of watching varying levels of surfers. Felt as though we were getting free lessons!

The beach is a half moon shape caught between a peninsula in the west and a rock connected by a sandbank to the beach at it's eastern edge. The beach is lined with attractive, non intruseive beach shacks serving food and drinks. A heavenly place for families, youghts and solo travellers like myself. The food is a bit pricier then in town but not at all exagerrated. You can still have a fish plate or seafood special for less then 1000 LKR. Great place

Mirissa is a lovely beach and we preferred it to Unawatuna (saw it later and our decision was right) and Hikkaduwa. Clean place, not very crowded and no large beach front hotels here. Option for whale watching and surfing.

Yep, they have ruined it! Over crowded. Polluted. Noisy. Smelly. Only a matter of time before something goes badly wrong here. And from what I can see the locals can only blame themselves, it is truly a mess. Such a shame, I'm sure it really was beautiful not so long ago.

Based on everything I had read previously about Mirissa I had anticipated it being a lot quieter and less developed than it actually is. We came here primarily for the whale watching but as we were spending a few days it was a positive that there are plenty of bars and restaurants, however if we had come for a Tranquil time we would probably have been disappointed. The beach itself is lovely and relatively clean, although the beach restaurants do need to be more vigilant about preventing litter and more bins need to be provided. The crowd is mostly young people in their 20s and 30s, lots of surfers, but there are also plenty of families and it seems to be a nice beach for kids although the waves are strong in places. All of the restaurants on the beach sell pretty much the exact same food and much of it is fairly uninspiring - we didn't experience any really good meals while we were in Mirissa although none of them were terrible either. Expect to wait a very long time for service wherever you eat as there seems to be no urgency or desire to provide good customer service anywhere.

Nice beach, beautiful blue sea, very relaxed atmosphere. Very high waves. 1 took me by surprise and after 10 tumbles I submerged,so be careful! Nice food and small town which had a very laid back atmosphere.

Mirissa is to Sri Lanka what Marbella is to Spain, occasionally sublime but often ridiculous. Mirissa's only reason for being is the beach and sea which are still, just, acceptable. But the developments along and on the beach are relentless and in parts it is totally overdeveloped in a poor way. It seems to have learned nothing from the disastrous over-development of nearby Unawatuna. Greed is the order of the day and brash and crass tourists are feeding this, resulting in over priced sub standard accommodation. If you are looking for affordable tropical winter sun in a busy, no frills town with a decent beach then you will not be disappointed. If you are expecting a tropical paradise, don't go.

Lovely beach to sunbathe on... range of bars/ restaurants/ hotels with sunbeds available for use. Great sand for sand castles!! Watch out for lots of rocks in and around the sea... great for a 'wee paddle' though. Biggest downside is the beach is right off a busy road... noise from which can be heard, even over the noise from the sea, making it a little less that completely idyllic... easy access though via tuk tuks!  Would definitely recommend at least a day chilling out here.... horizontally 😃

It's a great beach. A little small though so it can get crowded. Good for soaking in the sun and surfing and whale watching (though did not do it myself as it was supposed to be a 8 hour event).  No snorkeling. It's one of the cheaper beaches you can stay at.
The beach was a great time. There is plenty to do and a lot of places to eat and drink along the beach. There are people trying to sell you diving tours, whale watching, etc. Lots of fun.

Great clean beaches, good for body boarding in September, no touts great to relax and unwind, local lads & bar staff happy to play volleyball with anyone who wants to join in great views and local sites something for everyone.
Very nice beach with plenty of cool beach bars / restaurants where you can have a drink or a grilled fish

Absolutely stunning! White soft sand crystal clear water. Nobody trying to sell you anything. Plenty of places to eat and drink. At night along the beach front is a relaxed chilled vibe. We made a mistake leaving here for Unawatuna. Follow our journey on Instagram @twolostllamas
We thought this would be the ideal Christmas chill out it turned out not to be mainly due to our villa but Mirissa its self was pretty limited. However the beach is excellent and good for swimming.
Amazing beach, beautiful sand and great waves. Unfortunately the overpriced beach bars really let the place down.
Great beach with lovely sand, waves are very strong though so be careful! Lots of bars and restaurants on the beach to choose from. Only down side is can't always get a sunbed.

Mirissa beach is a small beach but it's the happening place with full of life. Whole lot of shacks and restaurants serving delicious food are lined up along the beach. This place is known for whale watching. We took nearly 3hr long boat ride for whale watching which was very exciting and worth the time and money. There are only three whales in this  area. The local boat men know them well and follow them even if they are inside the water. After noticing the fountain of water jets from a disaster all the bits speed up to reg the spot before the whale disappears again. This hide and seek game was exhilarating and we had a great time.

It's the perfect place too relax after travelling through the rest of Sri Lanka. The beach is clean and not overcrowded as we heard about other places in the area. You can use beach chairs from many of the places for free. The service at many of the restaurant can be really slow though

Mirissa was a fantastic experience. I was initially wrong in underestimating Mirissa. But when I visited the place, my experience was different. It is a very happening place. If one visits Sri Lanka, then I think a trip to Mirissa should be done along with the Whale watching. Its a lifetime experience.

The beach is incredible, but food here is very poor. In comparison to the beach restaurants in goa and Kerala where food is always tasty. The restaurants here serve very average cuisine. Even if you order local food it arrives cold. I've spoken to many people over the last few days on the beach and they say the same. Food and service isn't good. Good luck finding a tasty meal, I'm still searching....
Mirissa beach is an excellent beach of lanka. Peaceful and clean. Good sea food restaurants. It is nice thinking place with sunset.

I can see how some will enjoy mirissa beach as a place where you enjoy the fact that you're in an exotic, warm spot sipping a cold one while your country is snowed under. If you don't mind any of the following,  mirissa beach may be to your liking: - techno beats (or their bass frequencies) following you everywhere - Sunbeds and seats crowding the water front - Hard to find shade since people occupy the seats in the morning and won't let them go for a large part of the day - Garbage in between the cafes and restaurants - many tour advertisements in strategic locations Mirissa beach is in a beautiful natural setting and the water has something to offer for surfers, snorkelers, children and others alike. The above however distracts from the natural beauty and it is our impression that this beach is turning into a loud, crowded party place that draws mass tourism.
Nice beach with a lot of restaurants with big waves, good place for dinner or relax on the beach. The best restaurant is actually Zephyr, there makes a famous Pasta food!
I was really fascinated when I first git to Mirissa Beach that I forgot everything.  The specious beach with golden sand and the blue ocean really took me to a new world.
A beach is a beach is a beach is a beach. Embrace it. Golden sand. Warm water. Amazing sunsets. Friendly people from all over. Lots of eateries and happy hours and more!

Mirissa beach was one of the best beaches that we have visited not just in SriLanka, but all over. It is a clean strip of white sand with clear turquoise waters with a few good beach shacks on the other side. The water is swimmable and there is a coastguard present. A walk to the end of the beach which has the parrot rock is highly recommended.

After visiting empty long breathing east cost beaches and Tangalle beaches we came to Mirissa... because everyone is talking about it.. And I felt like in "Croatia" overcrowded with many sunbeds, many restaurants and whales promotion bilboards.
Very nice beach with big waves clear water. Several bars and restaurant where you can have drink and enjoy sea food.

The beach is outstanding I loved everything about it, there are also lovely beach restaurants to choose from day or night, it seems very unspoiled by cheep tat, absolutely loved my days here. if you want to relax and unwind this is a great place to be.
amazingly beautiful beach during day time... and by night - amazing beach restaurant.... highly recommended.
Lovely beach to chill out on. Lots of bars and restaurants, but not too crowded. Water is a good temperature for swimming. Cool waves as well!

Mirissa is a very nice beach town in Southern Sri lanka. It is best known for Dolphin and whale watching. If both arent on the list, then you may as well avoid this beach. Like most small beach towns, this too has a charm of its own and is full of tourists.

I have read lots about this beach and it's really very nice: clean water, middle sized waves, lots of beach bars. Almost every night is party in another bar. You can spot where by light and louder music. Crowd is mostly international, young and well fitted. But the place is turning into tourist spot, so sometimes you can see some package tours people. Also some of the bars got rooms to rent and if you are lycky enough, you can find room with private bathroom and view to the see for 20$ a night for 2.

This is a good beach as one can get into the water till quite far, but is also small and crowded. We liked tangalle better. But if you are looking for activity and many beach shacks dotting the beach then this is a good option. Wellagama is a quieter and a bigger beach and close by to Mirissa.

Me and my boyfriend stayed at this beach for a day and we couldn't be happier. The ocean temperature was perfect, many great resturants, and AMAZING sunset! Also there is many Great hotels nearby this beach.
I loved Mirissa beach very much. Was nice to sunbathe there and good to swim. There is a quiet swimming area for children also where are no waves.

Beautiful beach with lots of chairs to chill on which didn't cost. Restaurants dotted along which were great for food in the evening. Sea was rough when we were there so didn't go in for too long as quite exhausting but the beach is so white and very chilled!
Best beach in Sri Lanka so far. Nice restaurants on the beach, freshly fished fishes and seafood. Lots of waves fun to jump into. You won't get pestered by beach vendors.

Having been disappointed by other beaches so far on our trip we fell in love with Mirissa - lovely beach for swimming and chilling in the sun, great vibe with good mix of tourists and locals. We loved it here so much we extended our stay to enjoy more time by the beach!
Amaizing beach and ocean. Sand is sensitive and very clean, water is clean and warm. There are many bars, pubs and restaurant

The only thing I was thinking when I got to the beach is that finally a beach that looks like the ultra reality videos I used to see about beaches. Having the rich palm woods on the mountains and surrounding the beach is breathtaking. The sand, the rocks, the waves and everything is AMAZING!

Very clean, safe. lots of cafes & restaurants serving excellent food. feeling of standing on the edge of the world since there is no land mass directly south till the antarctic!! watched amazing sunsets as well as a moon set!

Me and my friend went here in the end of low season, had a couple of days with a lot of rain but after that the weather was amazing and the beach was really nice. The waves were quite high and the current was strong but perfect for surfing. They told us Mirissa would be better for swimming in December during high season.
Really awesome beach with plenty of waves if you are in to surfing. Be wary of the beach boys around. They will rip you off at any chance they get.

Good place to stay for couple of nights, beach is close, where you can even surf, or at least try 🙂 Dorm is alright, it is not warm inside, comfortable to sleep. A lot of parties going on the beach, so Mirissa is nice party place in general.

Stop here on our way back to Negombo and I absolutely love the view, the beach was so nice and inviting. Many tourist having fun in the water. I can see how people are drawn to this place. It is one beach that everyone should stop and just relax and enjoy the warm weather and the spectacular view.
Most beautiful beach we've seen so far the waves are perfect for surfing beginners, lots of pretty bars and restaurants along the beach front. Definitely worth a visit.
Such a gourgeus beach on south of Sri Lanka woth great selection of restaurants and bar. Will be back here for sure!

Nice and clean beach with lots of restaurants near it. In the evening the beach changes into a big long restaurant with sea food. You just pick your fish or other sea food and they cook it for you. Very nice, we were there every night.
Very lovely and lively beach.  Lovely soft sand and very clean which we loved. We love sitting on the beach watching the sun go down.

This is indeed not the secluded paradise beach of travel brochures, for you alone. But it is a nice beach anyway, clean sand, clean sea, and it's touristic, essentially targeting under 40's, but the older ones (like me!) can perfectly feel at ease. Strong waves (can be fun if you like them), so be careful, but water is shallow enough and there are lifeguards on duty, which makes the difference with most other places in the area where it is really too dangerous. Accommodation is essentially simple bungalows or guest houses, obviously appreciated by the above mentioned target. For upper level, you may consider the series of Lantern boutique hotels 4km east, with direct access to the beach (but too rough sea to swim, use the swimming pool). From there, get a cheap 5mn tuk-tuk ride to Mirissa. Many small restaurants/bars on the beach (some say too many, it is true that at high tide, they do not leave a wide strip of sand) with free sunbeds if you drink/eat (from them obviously), just bring your towel. At night, the tables are on the beach, and fresh fish is on the display for you to pick and have grilled. Rock or reggae music is unavoidable, found it not too invading for dinner, might be for the ones staying in the bungalows, as music is reported to be heard late in the night. All in all a nice touristic beach, not a remote atoll.
A genuinely perfect tropical beach and bay.  A good selection of rustic beach bars that dont rip you off, clean white sand & beautiful clear water.  I wish I was there now!

Nice beach with a lot of restaurants and bars. The sea was quite rough when we were there but once you get outside the break you can just swim and relax. In and out past the break could be a little tough. But the waves are smaller on the sides of the beach.

Beautiful sandy beach with lovely trees providing shade in some parts, but I found it very touristy. There are a number of restaurants with tables and Sun loungers down to the water, and many holidaymakers both in the restaurants and sunbathing along the whole beach. Mirissa is no longer an undiscovered paradise beach.

We went here for the afternoon and had a beer on the beach. The atmosphere was lovely I wish we had stayed in one of the guesthouses for the night. Lots of little places to sit out on the beach and relax. Definitely recommend to visit this beautiful beach!
Good beach for waves and relaxation. Beautifully curved beach with good opportunities for a morning jog.

Great place to stay. Stayed on two occassions, having left Marissa to travel in the mountains I returned to Hangover hostel to sample Mirissa's nightlife again. There was nowhere else in Mirissa that I wanted to stay. Nice and comfortable rooms. Extremely clean and tidy. Air conditioned. Nice common areas. Attracts a nice mix of people, from those who want to chill out a little more to those who want to party a little more. Had a really great stay here!

This is a very nice beach to visit, also during off-season. In contrast to Arugam Bay or Bentota Beach, there are bars available to drink and relax. And if you want to have some peace there are also parts available on the beach where it is very calm. All in all I like our stay at Mirissa very much!
Clean beach with strong current, and walk in to sea bed about 10 meters. Many good restaurants near by.

This beach from a distance looked the most beautiful and we only saw a small part after stopping for a drink at a restaurant. We saw the stilt fishermen and was gutted to find out it was only a hobby now and more of a tourist attraction. Absolutely stunning. The real Indian Ocean beauty. I love Mirissa! I will return one day. Brochure worthy photos can be taken here!

Mirissa beach is lovely and has fun nightlife but PLEASE BE WARNED: these beaches are NOT suitable for weak swimmers! Today, a man who was trying to snorkel these waves drowned and died, with his friend barely escaping death himself. My friend (who is a doctor) and some tourists, who were also trained, tried their best to revive him via CPR. I ran to get help but the help is not there. The beach is NOT EQUIPPED with proper medical equipment (AED, intubation kit, ambulance) making chances of survival minimal at best. We were only able to obtain a bag mask after multiple rounds of CPR. So please, please, advise the utmost caution when swimming.
we had a good time ... wave jumping and relaxing at the beach ... and good restaurants near the beach
Just a laid back place for chilli crab, beer and resting . Local surf, yoga and safe swimming of reef break surfing
The most gorgeous beach in Sri Lanka. We were only supposed to stay in Mirissa 4 days but ended up staying a week because it's so beautiful here. Nice soft sand and lovely clear blue sea.
Restaurants galore, rolling waves and lovely scenery. Can't argue with that. Great for surfing and body boarding but also as good just to relax.

Mirissa beach is clean and the water is warm and clear. There are lots of waves, so it's ideal for surfers and wakeboarders. It's not great for casual swimming and snorkeling, though. There's very little actual beach space to spread a towel on. Most of it is either occupied by bars and restaurants, or the waves come up too far. The sand is soft and white, and there are no sharp rocks underfoot except at either end. The beach bars are good for a beer and a nice view but not much else. The beach is not overly crowded, I was always able to find a spot to swim and sunbathe without much trouble.

Mirissa Beach is a beautiful beach with lots of surfers but is still interesting for those just wanting to relax and enjoy hanging out. The big waves are consistent so it's a great place if you surf or if you like to watch them (or like to play in big waves). There is enough variety of beach restaurants that you can get what you want to eat and drink.
Not right place to surf for beginners, you can instead visit Welligama to surf. However, its a great place to swim, enjoy the sun and chill at the bars and restaurants at the sea-front!
Lot of tourist are there.very clear water.not like weligama beach.this beach is not good for the people who can't swim.

I have been to many beaches all over the world and a few a very select few are something special and better than the others. Mirissa beach is one that will stick in my memory for sure. Golden sands, refreshing water not a piece of litter in sight top it off with some shady trees makes one lovely place to enjoy Sri Lanka. If you go to the beach have look from the rocky outcrop in between the beaches you willing spot the (free!!!) shady trees that are just past all the beach restaurants. Take a book and and surfboard and set up for the day!
Beach has nice restaurants and clubs. Really clean beach with soft sand. No shells which make it really comfortable. Nice waves to go for a little swim and have fun!
Sea can be a bit rough but the beach holiday itself is very nice. Can be difficult to get a good spot as there is a lot of bars/restaurants encroaching on to the beach

Brilliant beach unique hotels, surfing, bodyboarding, snorkelling, great food, every night there is a party in a restaurant with laser light show. We both loved it, as it's about 2.5 hours from Katunayake airport using the motorway, great place to unwind and start the island holiday.
This hotel needs major makeover, wifi is too weak and basically the place needs a big cleanup. Need to provide clean towels and descent bedlinen and blanket with covers.

Totally don't get the positive reviews. Mirissa it's nothing more than a very, very, small strip of yellow sand with mainly (except one, Zephyr) low class bars and 'restaurants', full of tourists, mainly backpackers. Not a local to be seen. Except those selling tours. There are some beach chairs in front of most restaurants which you get for free when your drink and/or eat something there. The town itself is nothing much to look at: there's a busy main road splitting the beach side from the 'town' area. You'll find a few shops, including souvenirs next to the beach road. Hotels and the thousand and one rent a rooms are on both sides. Mirissa is probably nice if you are looking for cheap accommodation and cheap eateries and do not mind about an overly touristic (and ugly) town. If you decide for whatever reason to come to Mirissa, take the side at the beach. It will save you unpleasant walks next to a busy and dark road at night. There are many nicer beaches in Sri Lanka, with Hiriketiya being a pearl not that far away. And even Tangalle being 100 times nicer.
very clean and white sand beach, lots of activity around the beach. good night life as well. great seafood.

Mirissa Beach is a narrow and busy beach with many good restaurants along the beach that come alive at night with strobe lights, fireworks and fire dancing. Great cocktails and delicious seafood. The water was pretty rough and you need to be careful where you swim but I am told out of monsoon season the water is calm and the beach is wider. I was told Sri Lanka is very cheap - but coming from Hong Kong, I found that it wasn't really - unlike South East Asia.
Holidays for unpretentious traveler. It dominates the positive atmosphere combined with beautiful nature and the Indian Ocean.

We've travelled a lot and definitely seen more stunning and cleaner beaches than this one, however I particularly like this beach for the stairs leading to the rock in the ocean. It really does look fascinating when the sun goes down.
The town itself isn't interesting, stay at a property at the beach (i.e. Number One Mirissa). The beach is great, and has some nice beach cafe's.
Very beautiful beach in mirissa. good spot for surfing with kids, a lot of good restaurant with a sea food.
We have been here several times, and we live this places. The locals here are super friendly and go out of their way to make your visit unforgettable.
Couple good restaurants and good place for surfers :-) Very clean water, sand as gold - we not meet any beach boys. And y can enjoy spa & massage.

Nice beach good atmosphere def a place for younger crowd ...sorry to say . Many bars and restaurants offering fresh fish and happy hour cocktails.loved sitting on the beach eating with the waves under our feet .

Mirissa beach is very beautiful and the water is clean. In the off sesson waves can be quite rough and it is difficult for children to swim in the sea. In the off season the tide is quite High and therefor the beach is also narrow. I recommend ti Book a hotel with a pool if you bring children.
Best beach in the country. Mostly calm and not so many shops. No place for party, but for sunbathing, ocean activities and whale watching.
