I thought the beach would full of rubbish and tourists... turned out I was wrong. Instead it was pristine with clear blue waters, the kind of beach most people dream of going. A number of restaurants are available there if you would like to have a fantastic seafood dinner after the watching the sunset. I enjoyed myself thoroughly
We were here off season, but it worth every penny! Ocean is great, food is great, people are great. Strongly recommended for visit!

A short beach with clean waters, with much peace and quiet time. No one would bat an eye for your stupidity and fun. Awesome waves and good to watch some slick moves from surfers. Love the View from the Rock Island, a must-visit location to relax.

Mirissa beach is once of the cleanest beach in Sri Lanka, surfing is possible even in the off-season. Beach is safe for the beginners as well and life-guard is available during the day time. The The view from the beach during the sunset is awesome. You rarely see the locals in the beach. A must visit beach is Sri Lanka
Although it is narrow the beach is stunning! The water is a little rough for swimming properly but we still had fun. Lots of fab places to eat and drink. Excellent vibe and lovely people!

This beach is a surfer's paradise but you need to be careful as there are rocky edges on one side. Even if you are not interested in surfing this is still a great travel destination as the water is pristine and the setting amazingly calm and offers a relaxed ambience. Sea food is readily available in the shacks situated on the beach. We visited from Galle and it took us 1 hr to drive down. On the way you can stopover at Unawatuna beach and the turtle hatchery. Overall highly recommended!!
Really nice beach for families and close to everything you might need for a toddler to enjoy themselves
Mirissa beach is still fairly untouched. The nights are cool and the mornings divine. The docks offer great views of the boats.

We spent 4 nights in Mirissa and we absolutely loved the chilled atmosphere (please note we were there in October which is low season). Some of the beach clubs play nice music during the day and there are good spots for sunbathing. It is a nice area to sleep as well as at night the beach becomes a beautifully romantic way full of candlelit restaurants on the sand. During the day it is very easy to go to Welligama for some surf. I would not recommend this beach for families with little children or even for people who want to do any kind of swimming/snorkling/etc. The waves are way too strong and the currents make it very difficult to even stand in the water.
Very nice beach with restaurants with seafood. Swimming and surfing possible, with few places to rent a surfboards.
Very nice beach but water very rough with big waves. Plenty of deck chairs available to lie out. Few stray dogs but friendly
Damn good beach.. We had a excellent time out on this beach for our anniversary that we spent here for two days.. Full of fun and activities around this area.. True comeback out here!'

We spent one week in Mirissa and it was beautiful vacation. During day you can take sunbed, drink fruit smoothie and enjoy Sri lankan food. In the evening beach turns into charming place with more than 20 restaurants. One bad thing are big waves.

I spent two afternoons at Mirissa because and enjoyed every second of it! The waves were perfect for playing in and lots of people were using body boards which looked awesome! It is very clean and there are lifeguards constantly watching the water so it is safe for swimmers of all abilities. Best beach I have been to in Sri Lanka! I definitely recommend it to all!

We are in mirissa right now, September 29. Yesterday went to the beach. The waves here are so high as it's still not a season. Good we did snorkelling in Nilaveli cause here I doubt we can see anything clearly. The water is very sandy cause of waves. Although they are still promoting Wales and dolphin watching. However, we enjoy playing with waves and grabbing the drinks at the beach bars. There plenty. Plus, the spa is great here.

Mirissa beach is simply beautiful - the stuff of dreams. Palm trees, golden sand, sunshine, a gentle breeze and sea calm enough to swim in. What more could you want? The peaceful beach was quiet and clean with a few lovely beach bars and restaurants serving drinks straight to your sunbed. Heaven...
Palm trees, white sand, clean water. When I was there (September) it had a strong current but you can swim.

What to say about Mirissa beach. On one henad, we've had a great time, enjoying on the waves, as the sea was too rough to swim when we were there. The food in the restaurants was good, the coctails were perfect. It is a great place if you just want to enjoy the beach, and don't really care in which country you are. And then comes the but. There are ONLY tourists at the beach (allegedly the locals are not allowed to the beach??). It doesn't feel like Sri Lanka, it is just another sandy beach on some coast. And it is too filled with restaurants, bars, hotels, guesthouses,... It's tourism gone wild in a transition country. We've visited Nilaveli at the east later during travels and I liked it more. But it is completely different, no wild parties there, no noise, only water, sand and fishermen (locals!).
This one of the fascinating places in coastal line of southern Sri Lanka.  Famous among foreigners , specially Europeans.

We only spent a day and a half here but the beach is nice although a bit narrow when the tide comes in. There are plenty of eating and drinking options and the sea is safe to swim in even during late monsoon....we were there in August. It's a relatively touristy place compared to places further east but a very pleasant place to chill out for a  couple of days.
Good place to be if in Mirrissa.  Good for surfers and just anyone who would like to chill at the beach.

My boyfriend and I went there in September. The weather was great and we really loved that is place. The waves are quite big which is a lot of fun if you like playing in the water. We could use the beach beds for free in any bars and all the bars/restaurants are not overpriced. Really romantic by night and some chill atmosphere in some of the cafe. The beach is quiet made to relax. Definitely worth to stay one night or two !

Plenty of nice beach bars and lovely beach to enjoy swimming and walking! Very easy access from the road. No beach sellers in site to annoy your relaxation! Life guards on duty is a bonus. Body boards/snorkelling/jet ski facilities avaliable on beach a bonus.
Beautiful beach spot which has the perfect about of tourist and local culture. Stayed there for three days and wish we had longer. It seems as if it is very family friendly location.

Mirissa beach has a good range of beach restaurants etc. We were there in September and the tide did cover the whole beach at high tide. The waves were good for surfers but you need to be a confident swimmer at this time of year.

Great clean beach with plenty of small quirky bars. There are various coves some quieter than the main beach; Zephyr although when we went in September there were not an unbearable number of people! Amazing waves for surfing - really enjoyable beach.
Lovely clean beach with cool bars and  a mix of restaurants. Seems a lot more chilled than other beaches we've visited. Plenty of activities to do during the day, suffering, snorkelling etc
mirissa beach one of best beach.very wide beach..lot of bars and restaurant with ftresh sea food.nigh you can enjoy some beach parties but not everyday.
One of Sri Lanka's nicer beaches. Great for relaxing and swimming. Good restaurants  and friendly locals.
Nice beach, but the tourist industry has come down hard in here, so now there's hundreds of European or occidental types here, so...the charm has gone from the place I knew five years ago. Pity
Fantastic beach with great bars and restaurants, been twice and it gets better, lovely golden sand warm sea, a beach everyone should visit once in their lifetime
Is a nice beach to relax and read, at night there at some good places to eat and have a drink, good vibe
Amazing place to stop by or have bath when you are travelling along the coast side. Love the sea breeze with amazing sea view.

The waves are big and you cant actually swim in there. You can just have fun jumping into them. Because of the waves, the space beetwen water and bars/restaurants is pretty small but you can find a shadow almost every time of the day! Bars are cute, cheap cocktails (300rupies), great atmosphere and amazing sunset (around 18.30)!

We had a lot of fun on this beach,jumping in such as big waves! Perfect for surfing. In september not many people.,clean and quiet,good services provided. But there are much more beautiful beaches in Srí Lanka.

When we first arrived and saw how big the waves where we were really worried, took us a bit to understand the situation and how to make advantage of it. We rented paddle boards and started riding the waves, it was really a fun experience with a lot of lovely photos. We ordered food and it was really nice. Absolutely nothing to complain about. I totally recommend this place.

dirty and there is hardly anywhere to sit and relax that isn't a loud beach bar. I can see this being fun if you're under 25, but as someone in my mid 30s, I found the place pretty gross. skip Mirissa and head to the east coast.

The sea here is crazy and the beach is so small. Everything has been built so close to the sea that when a big wave comes in (often) you get soaked when you are sitting in a cafe (well your legs and feet get soaked). The waves are also dangerously strong at times and wipe you off your feet. The pull back of the waves is SCARY. Be very careful and stay near the beach. No one goes out to see and the lifeguards prevent anyone doing so. We saw the lifeguards go out twice to go and help people who had been sucked out by the tide.

I stumbled upon the quiet end of the beach during a walk from the busy, tourist end of Mirissa Beach.  It was so nice to escape the crowds, pumping music and business and settle back on the white sands amongst the palm trees.
Quite relaxing place! Find a good bar and lay black ! The prices are quite reasonable (one can find coconut for 50 slr)!

Mirissa beach ....my custemers really enjoy .....specialy  seafood resturants in evining fresh fish can buy there .....many kind of fish ....... they very happy to eat ............ whale whaching  and dolphin it was amazing experiance good place to visit tourist
A lovely beach with plenty of restaurants and bars along. A place you would love to spend with family and kids
Its an OK beach if bars and music are your scene. Lots of ramshackle restaurants and bars trying to be trendy. If you like reggae then this your place

The beach is really narrow and there is not much room to sunbathe. During off season sea is also very rough and beach is a bit dirty with trash. Surf breaks are basically unsurfable due winds and rough seas. Some restaurants on the beach are nice, like zephyr.

The beach is nice and clean, however there are too many bars/restaurants/cafes, with lounge music all day round, happy hours etc... In less than 5 years this will become like the beaches in Marbella, Lloret, Salou or similar places, with an exceeding number of hotels, guesthouses, bars and restaurants, noise, pollution and plastic everywhere (by the way, plastic will be/is one of the plagues of our century, polluting entire beaches, parks, lakes, rivers....). Tourism can become a good way to improve economy, but it should be controlled in some way, otherwise it will be also a way to destroy the beauty of the country (I'm from Catalonia, and it is a pity what has become of our beaches so I know what I'm talking about)
The beach is quite clean and has some good restaurants. The sea was very rough and we could see huge tides coming our way. A good place for surfing.

When visiting Mirissa, don't expect a pristine beach anymore. As a hotel owner said: it used to be like Talalla close by but those days are gone. If you like a small beach with bars along the entire stretch all trying to get your attention by means of the international mix of happy hours, beats and fish presentation: you will love it. If your looking for a beautiful Sri Lankan beach, just pass it by

The beach is not too big and has about 10 restaurants clubs with some of the best fishcurry. The looks are bounty and the waves are high. The waves are not te be underestimated tough, cause they really are rough sometimes.

We wanted a little down time from travelling so much so we decided to have a week doing some beaches along the southern coast with Mirissa being our first stop! Beach is beautiful! Laden with palm trees and white-ish sand! We bought a towel from over the road as assumed you needed to pay for the beds! Not a lot to do apart from the rock and a few bars/pubs on the front but nice for a day of sunbathing!
We have been there for couple of days and I must say I love it. It's long and clean beach, not so crowded restaurants are nice and the waves are amazing. Best beach on sri lanka !

Mirissa is a beautiful seaside resort village with many little cafes lining the sandy beachfront - take your pick, they're all fabulous!  At night, they put out the day's seafood catch, so pick your own fish, crab or crayfish and have it cooked to your liking while the surf laps your feet as you sip a cocktail!  And if you like to surf, the point has a great break (just beware the reef, but it's marked well)!  And the water's fine - clear and warm!
Lovely, golden beach to spend some time, even off-season. Nice to take a stroll and there are several restaurants.

This beach has the wow factor... Great fun in the day. Hire boogie boards and spend a couple of hours riding the waves. The bars along the front rent them. The board quality varies do check them out. In the evening the beach looks great with all the candles. Fire work displays also take place on the beach. Shame about the lack of quality places to eat. We were warned about the kitchens as most places are not hygienic . Walk round to Turtle beach at the far end near the small island. We were lucky and spotted a Turtle.
Even in August this is a great place to relax and have sun bath. There are nice bars and restaurants to eat looking at the Ocean. It's fantastic! Even for dinner!

We had the most awful weather during our visit and this did spoil it. The whale watching boats did not go out but it meant we spent more time in the number 1 roti shop so it was not all bad. The beach is lovely and we watched the life guards being schooled by Aussies so you know they are good.
Great beach. Nice atmosphere and good food. Waves are great for bodyboarding with kids. Evenings are quiet.

This is by far my favourite beach in Sri Lanka. It can be a bit choppy for a swim, so unless you are a strong swimmer it would be best stay close to the shore. The beach has such a relaxed and chilled vibe. The palm trees at the back rake outward across the sand which can provide shade when the sun is too intense. The beach is backed by a number of bars that offer good price happy hour drinks(happy hour seems to run for about 5 hours). A great place to spend a few days of your holiday

Go in Mirissa you wont regret ! You have nice bars and restaurants on the magical beach and a lot of activities in Mirissa ( excellent massages snark farm kayaking...) One of the best beach I have seen during my trip
Lovely body waves, snorkelling, indulgent restaurants comfortable relaxing residences. From dawn to dusk with sandy feet, warm water floating and happy tummies!

A beach absolutely prepared for tourism. You maybe won't learn anything about Sri Lanka people or culture (except sea food recipes...) but it's a good place to relax yourself and prepare (or finalize) your trip throughout the country.

It' a nice beach with plenty to do. You have restaurants and bars on the beach so you can chill. It is also clean. You have surfing lessons in the next bay going to the city next to Mirissa. It was a good stay here.

The beach is quite big and offers everything from restaurants, bars, surfing schools, shade under the trees... There were a lot of families, couples and also friends (my case). We had a lovely afternoon, listening to the ocean, jumping around in waves.

We stayed twice a few days in mirissa. We liked it so much we came back before leavin sri lamka. Small village on the beach: beautiful beach with a lot of nice restaurants where you can eat fresh seafood for a very reasonable price. Easy to go to Galle from here, only 1 hour by bus. It was low season but quite busy. Beautiful wheather and less hot than the east coast. The waves are terrific! You have to be careful where to pick your hotel: not too close to the road because of the noise in the early morning, not too close to some beach reataurants because they can have loud music until early morning. We stayed in the center in a little street with lots of guest houses (Extreme host guesthouse,  Amarsinghe etc) a bit farther from the road but only a few minutes from the beach. Not the perfect ocean view as the guest houses on the beach but quute all right, clean, confortable and not expensive.
Nice beach with a lot of people and restaurants. But I am sure Sri Lanka offer better places than Mirissa Beach

Mirissa is a very Nice beach. We really enjoyed our stay here. There are Nice cafe's on the beach and good waves to go bodyboarding. You can rent them at the beach. Too bad we lost our Go Pro camera (with a headband) in the waves at mirissa beach. If you find it at the beach please contact leave a message.

We have visited all of the most popular/recommended beaches in Sri Lanka during our trip and Mirissa was the most beautiful beach! Really nice restaurants and bars on the beach, great atmosphere and vibe. Fresh sea food being served every evening on the beach in many nice restaurants. You can enjoy a nice dinner while sitting on the beach with sand in between your toes! Sunbeds available beside every bar during the day. Very clean beach, excellent to swim, no boats, and no people trying to sell you anything. Very relaxing but yet busy and lively. Great food, good prices, happy hour during the day and in the evenings in many bars. Real chill!!! Highly recommended!!!

Mirissa is a very nice beach town. There are lots of restaurants and bars on the beach, They give the place a good vibe. The beach is beautiful and the Indian Ocean is magnificent. We visited Mirissa in August and the ocean can be very rough at that time of the year, but there were lifeguards and we could have a swim, that was fun!

Along the beachside there's a real lined up restaurants or cocktailbars with a calm breeze, nice OceanView. The competition of around 20 bars with terraces in the sand makes it more interesting  for the Western Tourist. An example: 2 to 5 bars are having "Happy Hour" from 5 pm till 10 pm. Fantastic !!!

The beach is rough this time of year, but it is a very nice beach. It is most for young people,msurfing, doing watersport, and listning to loude reagge music. The resturants is fine but i expected better.

This is my friends and my 1st time came to this plame. We take train from colombo port, it is took 3.30hours to reached the station closed to mirissa continue took tuk tuk about 10 to 15mins. Once the tuk tuk driver drop us, we are a bit scared, because we didn't see the beach or other people, until we open our google map to proved that he not send us to the wrong place 😂😂 I can say, mirissa is just open on that time, coz is less of tourist, just nature as it it. Mirissa is good for surf lover. Few restaurant are available, reasonable price n good quality of food.. we r in love for this place..😍😍
High waves, good beach clubs, save guards, relaxing chairs, palm trees... What more can you want from a beach?

Really nice sized beach with lots of restaurants to choose from and sun beds to lay on. There is a strong current with big waves which you only really notice when you go out quite deep and get pulled out with the receding wave so be careful! Good for body boarding if you stay very close to the shore.

The beach is divided into three parts, which significantly differ from each other. The main part the largest with many cafes and hotels right on the beach. More beautiful and clear water in the next section, here you can watch the fish, sea urchins and sometimes turtles. Between them a small island-rock, from which you can watch beautiful sunsets.

This is my favorite beach in Sri Lanka so far.  Be aware that there some very big waves, at least during monsoon season, and the tide tends to pull you down the coastline, so it may not be appropriate for small children.  If you're looking for something calmer and quieter, maybe check out Tengalle.

Stayed in Mirissa early this month and we had a great time. However, there wasn't much happening around. Having read about reverse discrimination I was a bit skeptical cos we are from India and many a times we had folks coming up to us and speaking in Sinhalese. Though we got some odd treatment in some restaurants most of our stay was pretty pleasant. We were coming in from Arugam bay and felt that people were much more friendlier and forthcoming there than anywhere else in SL.  But we loved the beach and the hotel we stayed at was very well located. Will definitely come to Mirissa again.
Really nice and clean beach with lot of places to walk around and enjoy the nature - hangout, swim, surf, outdoor-reading.
Very beautiful beach, great for playing in the surf, renting boogie boards and having fun. Enough restaurants along the beach to choose from.

Not like Unawatuna: smaller, cheaper and not crowded. We had a cheap hotel in the back. Really nice and quiet beach although the current was in off season very strong, you just could get in to the hips. But with doing some body surfing it was really fun. Good food although some restaurants were annoying with their music. A friend was with his family in a hotel at the beach and one of their rooms was full of cockroaches. Anyway our place was clean but outside on the road there is a lot of rubbish and they told us to shut the windows at night for our security. Well.. anyone could break in there quite easy.
it is the best beach in Sri Lanka i highly recommended it to all people whose want clearly water in the see

Had a great few days here. Loads of cafes on the beach for a cold beer. Good place to go body boarding although there is a bit of a current that runs so just watch out with small children. With a bit more of a tidy up and a lick of fresh paint it would be amazing. The fear is that the tourists will find this place and then it will get over crowded.
Our favourite stay of our trip was in Mirissa. Cozy, calm and lovely beach with lots of nice restaurant / bars dotted along. A must visit place.

We saw our first whale final after 2,5 hours. After chasing it with several boot we where back after 6 hours. It was nice to see a whale but it was a chicken chase with little else. Lots of people had see sickness problems further out sea. We had for more fun and enjoyment on river safaris, land safari or simple waterfall treks.

What a delightful beach. Admittedly a tourist spot but still with charm. A little neglected but with it's own charm. Attentive waiters encoring the use of their tables for drinks and eats. A lively spit to relax and unwind. Would be very busy in high season. A fascinating walk is to the neighbouring harbour where there is heaps if action early morning as boats unload their catches. A lively sunset from one end if the beach.

Lovely beach even patrolled with flags! A little bumpy due to solid wind but still a refreshing dip. Be careful of touts in the bars, apparently all are illegally selling alcohol which is very cheap. Nice to see some clean sand.

The beach might have been nice at some time, but now it's overbuilt and ramshackle buildings are way too close to the shoreline. Also the busy road is very close to the beach. No real town centre either in Mirissa.
Nice beach spot with relaxed atmosphere. A few good bars and restaurants along the beach front. Looks to be developing for higher capacity to attract more tourists

Our stay at Maison d'Hotes could NOT have been more enjoyable!! The BnB is primary run by the two most lovely Sri Lankans we met in our entire trip, a mother and a son. They were amazingly kind, helpful with anything we could have ever needed, and were always checking on any needs we could have, yet not to a point where they were overbearing. They offered to arrange our airport transportation, they arranged our transportation to the next destination and I'm sure would've done anything we asked which required a local in the area. Even stayed up necessarily to provide us with a meal when we arrived in the middle of the night. For never having hosted anyone at their BnB before (the place is new) they were naturals. The rooms themselves were nice, nothing luxurious but the beds were large and comfortable and the air conditioning worked great which is a big one in hot Sri Lanka. The family made home cooked meals (and had fresh juice) any time we asked, and made recommendations of places we might like in the area when we did not. Mirissa itself was perhaps the most scenic place we saw during our 8 day trip. The most popular (seemingly) beach area is a short walk away, and the picture of the point you see in the listing is right outside the front door! The beach has plenty of restaurants and bars to check out, a couple of close islands or disconnected peninsulas which made for great sunset viewing spots, and the beach and water itself was warm, with great waves to play or surf in. These hosts are exceedingly polite and we had an awesome stay at a very much affordable cost for five students!! Highly highly recommended for any type of trip really!

It is a really nice place where we can enjoy with friends and family. I went with my family  few times since it is really fun out there. Sea bathing is a must there & there are plenty of night restaurants and so much night life there !! Must visit attraction in Down-South Sri Lanka. Cheers !!!
A lovely place to spend time during the day and enjoy Sri Lankan cuisine during the night!! A very clean and quite place. And also very near to the city center..
The best place to do surfing and to have a swim in the sea. Plenty of beach side restaurants and hotels.

Stayed at the Paradise Beach Club right in the centre of Marissa beach with stunning views over the ocean. Loved the little beach bars for drinks and fresh seafood. One of the cleanest, white sanded beaches we got to see in Sri Lanka - just beautiful!

To be honest, this Aussie beach snob was mildly surprised by Mirissa Beach. It was clean, with soft sand, not too crowded or commercialised, and had a good vibe. There's not a lot of sand to laze on at high tide, but typically you'd be staying at a nearby hotel anyway. There's only a handful of shops along the main road and most of the nightlife is centred around the chilled out beach bars. Happy hour lasts until around 10pm, which is handy. It's a nice spot to land for a few nights, but not sure what you would do for any further length of time.

Beautiful beach, not overly commercialized. There was a stretch where the beach extends into the sea in 20 meters or more. Lovely to play with the wave safely. I heard from locals that the beach in the other nearby places may have jelly fish so be careful.
Mirissa beach is famous for surfing. You can get surfing lessons here. Also you get many budget  hotels along the beach.

A beach not as populated or popular as Bentota. Its a common sight to see the local fishermen around fishing, they charge you to have photographs clicked with them or for a closer view of their Chinese Fishing nets

Mirissa has a lovely soft sandy beach. There are a few too many restaurants now, but there are some quieter shady spots if you search. Sometimes have to wonder how fresh all the fish is that is on display in all the restaurants as there is always so much left there late each night, often in the open without ice. Beware.

Three days was too long for me. I personally wouldn't want to visit a second time, not my cup of tea. Beaches are good, not a lot to do apart from lying on the beach drinking all day, if like that sort of thing it's great.  Whale watching trips, be vary about the claim that the boats are of good quality. I dreaded the trip, with diesel fumes in close space, can't escape you're in a boat which is over crowded. Nothing positive about the trip.

A very nice place! Very clean beach with fine sand. There is a part with the waves and the part without waves. There is a few people on the beach. For the people from Europe: if someone says it's crowded there, it does not mean that on the beach is so many people, like on the beaches in Croatia or in northern Italy.
Very clean and nice beach i have ever seen. Good beach for surf and dive.very stunning view at night. found happy hour restaurents to have beer and bites.
At Mirissa we can choose from more beaches - two bigger and a smaller one. At the biggest beach there is good possibility for learning surf, at the smaller ones you can rest more quietly.

Water was gorgeous and the sand was perfect. Beach was spotlessly clean and the many bars and restaurants on the beach with reasonable prices made it worth our while to stay there almost all day. It does not have much shade but you can always grab a drink in the bar. Wadiya has particularly good cocktails and staff (don't be put off by the hard sell at the beginning). You should be also able to rent a bodyboard for about 300-500 LKR for the day which is great fun on the waves. Be advised though, if the waves are strong, you should only venture swimming out if you are a confident swimmer. Every day we saw someone who needed rescuing... ;)

Mirissa was our favorite beach on our trip to Sri Lanka. Definitely better than Unawatuna. Pristine water, clean beach and lots of sun beds. U can walk to the southern end of the beach which has a bay like area good for swimming if u wanna avoid high waves. Come evening and the beach just transforms itself. All beach shacks arrange tables and chairs on the beach along with fresh produce of the day. Pick what u wanna eat. U can even bargain..!! Special mention for sunshine beach inn for lovely music and ambience.
A pretty coooool beach with lot of acitivity. Theres surfboards which can be rented and some really good hotels on the beach.
Mirissa beach offers amazing views ... The water is so blue and the beach is adorned by palm trees and the best part about Mirissa is that it's not very touristy .

Lovely beach and very doable to walk the entire thing. The waves get really big! You can go out to Peacock Rock from the beach, climb up and see the beach from up above in the ocean, great views. Restaurants and bars loaded up and down the beach!

Be it swimming or surfing or a little bit of snorkeling Mirissa is an absolutely stunning beach. Towards the two ends of the bays there is relative safety in doing some sea bathing. The rocks around the parrot islands is great to observe the rich marine habitat. But its best not to get in the water during the off season as the currents can be pretty strong
If you visit mirissa please do wait till the sunset and you may get the best moments of your sri lanka .

We stayed in Marissa three days at the end of our trip in Sri Lanka. It was a great relaxing time. Just a few tourist around, the weather wasn't so bad at all and we found good prices in accommodation and restaurants.
lovely beach! weather, sand, people everything was great! i recommend couples, friends and all types of groups to visit this place

Last month we visited the Down south Sri lanka, Mirissa Beach with my friends. It was Beautiful place, Good place for surfing and Whale watching & Dolphin. So Whenever you traveled to down south, You should visit Mirissa Beach.
Went here very briefly on the way to Galle from Tissa. The part of the beach we went to was not busy, there was restaurant near the beach front.
Great whale watching opportunity. Blue whales live in this ocean. You can also see migratory sperm whales and dolphins.
We went there early in the morning at six o  clock we get boat and sailing to deep sea we see the dolphins and whales that is fantastic .yes, that is first time in my life we enjoyed very well

Small - clean - not so crowded beach. Beach has severe under current. However has an interesting feature - there is an island which enables you to walk in the ocean to reach there ( as water gets really shallow there ). Overall good experience
With family we love beach breaks for swimming and bodysurfing. This beach is perfect for this. Water very clean, people nice. Surfing is also ok.

What a great find in our trip to Sri Lanka. Reminder-ed me of Bali 30 years ago. No 5 star only 3 star. Has a great surfing break and plenty of activity on the beach after 4 with happy hour everywhere. Plenty of choices to eat from along the beach with reasonable prices. The water is the beautiful blue that you would expect and looks inviting. It can be a little dangerous with a big crunching wave consistently coming in but on the northern end a great pool forms between the beach and the rock formation with the waves gently coming into the area. For those of you that want to have a little bit of a challenging walk, ask the locals how to go to Secret Bay. It's up over the hill on the northern end. Well worth the effort but not straight forward to get to

Even in the low season Mirissa Beach was very nice. Liked to climb the Mirissa Rock and loved the high waves although not really too rough as they can be as I was told. From the Mirissa Rock you can sometimes see the Sea turtles in the clear water.

I travelled here after spending some time in Unawatuna and I quickly realised this beach is very different. Unlike Unawatuna, where there are loungers on nearly every inch of the beach, Mirissa is much more of a 'bring your towel and enjoy the sea' type of place and is a lot less commercial. There are still a number of resturants on offer and all the ones I ate at were good. In the evening some of the restaurants have displays of fish where you can choose you own and get it grilled in this tasty garlic butter. The sea is also different from Unawatuna and instead of having a big drop and dumpy waves the sea  is much more enjoyable to swim in. The beach itself makes a good walk especially in the evening as there is no loud nightclub music just chilled bars with Relaxing music and tables  lit by candlelight. I definitely recommend this place, just make sure you bring mosquito spray!

The sunsets here are stunning, a beauty to take in as you wander along the beach with the waves of the Indian Ocean crashing around your feet. Mirissa Beach is a fairly small stretch of coastline with bars and restaurants lining the shore, illuminated at night to create quite a picture. Plenty of choice for food (fresh fish!) and drinks and a very safe place to relax and unwind.

Small beach good for swimming. There is a lot of greenery surrounding the beach. The beach has many bars alongside however there can be too many sellers which might prevent you from enjoying the peace. Whale watching happens at Mirissa so makes sense to spend time at the beach too.

Very nice place to walk and Leisure. bad experience was beach boys. they came to promote there boat safari, gem shops, took tooks and more. we going there to take a relax. but that people are the problem.
If you are aroumd just dont miss to see. Nice view, lots of restaurants.  We havent been but heard thar parties at nights in the high season
Another clean, blue & beautiful beach in Sri Lanka. This is popular for surfing. I don't do surfing but I have seen people surfing in this beach.
Crack open a coconut, slip into a hammock and rock gently in the breeze, allowing the hours, days and even weeks to slip calmly by.

We really loved Mirissa beach, it is small, compact and actually has a decent beach, unlike some other Sri Lankan beaches. We enjoyed swimming in the ocean, it was pretty decent, not too rough. There is decent surf also as there is a small reef. Plenty of bars and restaurants along the beach. Well worth visiting.

The Mirissa Beach is a long arch shaped stretch of beautiful sand. The water is warm and beautiful but the surf is rough and there is very strong under tough.  One must be very careful while bathing. The beach is lined with many beach shack style restaurants where you can have meals and rent a lounge chair. There is a small island at the east side of the beach. it can be limed and visited. At high tide the beach becomes a bit small. But at low tide it is a dream. Also - lots of shady places to sit.

Seeing pictures of what this beach was like in 2003 really makes me sad. The beach is highly rated by TA and guidebooks but in reality it is a very dirty run down looking place. Cheap restaurants and bars are too close to the water leaving no actual beach space. Too many beach boys here harassing tourists and very slow service from the staff who looked very stoned. We heard from some people that locals aren't even allowed on this beach so that kind of made it feel like a non authentic place. No local families etc just local beach boys. We found the beaches further south like Tangalle and East like nilaveli much nicer so don't waste your time here...
Saw 2 Blue Whales and tonnes of Dolphins.  Caught nothing fishing (run from th edive centre 5-10mins west of mirissa beach) which was overpriced and the equipment was pretty awful

A small cove beach suitable for swimming and a nice walking beach, a small high island you can walk over and up to.  Lovely greenery surrounding the beach.  Many little beach bars/all pretty average..happy hours..pick your fish etc..
It's the most beautiful beach we have been to yet in Sri Lanka. Love the bars and restaurants on the beach. Great atmosphere at night.
Beautiful.beach. you can visit everywhere in South while you are staying in Mirissa. Better restaurants than Weligama where I stayed.
Mirissa is very famous with locals and foreigners for it's nice beach and the activities like whale watching. One of the great place that you won't missed when you visit Sri Lanka for a vacation.

I felt like I was swimming in a Bounty bar advert. Such a beautiful beach. It helped our hotel was directly on the beach so we could really make the most of it. We did some snorkelling and saw some tropical fish in shallow water. A great place!

The firstt night we arrived in Mirissa we went staright for the famous fresh fish we had read about and left feeling a bit let down as what we found was large terraces filled with loud drunken tourists served by not overly enthusiastic muscle bound waiters who over charged us after leaving not just us sitting for along time wondering if we would actually be served after the said muscle bound wating staff finished trying to impress the before mentioned drunken tourist girls Now all that said we got to the beach early (7amish) the next morning and went for an explore to find some of the most outstanding beach and islands on the sea shore. To then happen on a beach front cafe (Mirissa Beach WADIYA Guest House) for a very authentic Sri Lankan breakfast searved by one of the most charming resteraunters ive ever  had the pleasure to meet called Desmond we went back every morning after this. Then an hour or so before sun set decided to walk along the beach to where we spotted some surfers at the far end where the coral reef is and headed there only to discover the laid back, chilled out fresh fish serving beach bar we had read about called SURF BAR Mirisssa where once again ended up going back to for the freindly excellent service we where delighted to find on first getting there. The guys knew just how to keep the good service and freindlyness on a superb level Please dont change :  )
Mirissa beach is nice, but you should try to get our of town, because  the main beach is overcrowded with restaurants putting the terraces literally on water

The whale watch experience was very good and we organised it through the hotel, I suggest this is a very good idea. There were a couple of serious surfers staying in our hotel who told me that the waves could be very good. The Fish in the evening on the beach with waves running around your feet and the table is an experience. I suggest one of the restaurant bars at the end near the main surfing area!

Beautiful Sandy Beach, Big waves, it can be hard with a baby to swim but lots of fun together, we enjoyed every moment,   The restaurant on the beach offer a great spot to watch the sunset with a drink and also fresh daily fish for dinner.

Very touristy and similiar to a beach in Thailand with bars down on the water. Was pretty relaxing, but the water was just so so warm. Head up to Weligama for a more relaxed vibe if that's what you're after.
I spent an evening at the beach. It has quite a few shacks to chill at. Was a little crowded though.
Gorgeous beach. Fresh fish for sale - choose your fave and they'll cook it for you in the restaurants. Really nice beach. Chilled. Great dinner places.
Mirrisa is famous for taking boat to see whales and dolphins. However beach is ok and what i love is the color of sea. Lot of budget hotels at the side of beach   and fully occupied by foreigners

A nice beach also for walking,there is a big rock,at the end of the biggest part of the beach,one side of the rock the sea is verry quite,nice for swimming Late afternoon,for dinner,,a lot of restaurants on the beach
This was a one of best place to relax. With the time it got lot of crowded. Mirissa beach has gold sand blue water. Of couse Surfing Point. One of beautyfull beach in south.
Such beautiful beach! great vibes.. The big rock is unbelievably beautiful. kind of a steep climb. but the view from up there is totally worth it! really enjoyed it.

The beach is beautiful, really it is, but is too busy to enjoy. We went swimming there only early morning or late evening otherwise it was too crowded. The line of bars, restaurants and hotels is never-ending, they are spread all along the beach, each one with its own favorite party music playlist, impossible to hear the sound of waves here. Fortunately it seems that the hotels are ll build after the first line of coconut-palm-trees so you have the impression of a beautiful scenario, but it is easy to see how it will get more and more busy with constructions in the future...

Riding the waves here board or no board is fantastic BUT only do so if you are a strong swimmer and not afraid to go under. The return current from the eaves is very strong and can make it hard to get back into shore. Fantastic bars and restaurants too.

There are two sides to Mirissa beach. We definitely preferred the more quiet bay. There are a couple of bars close by where you can buy food and drink. There are plenty of sun beds on the busier beach but only a few on the bay side.
Huge waves all day - good fun and perfect for bodyboarding. This was a welcome change from the barren Tangalle beaches. Please note however - the food here is universally awful.
Excellent beach for  children and adults for both swimming and snorkeling. There is also plenty of surfing  going on.We spend 2 weeks on this beach and loved every minute of it.

went to a number of beaches in the south and west. Mirissa easily topped all the others. the waters are a beautiful combination of emerald and sapphire. there are plenty of waves yet the water isnt turbulent. plenty of sandy beach around and there is just the right amount of crowd-not too empty not too crowded. there were a number of restauraunts doting the beach-although none of them looked particularly inviting and most were rather empty. but overall, easily the best beach we went to
Awesome beach. The only negative point is the waves are big and strong so a bit hard if you are with kids. The restaurant on the beach offer a great spot to watch the sunset with a drink

Having been to a few other Sri Lankan beaches, this one is really great for independent travelers who like to walk to restaurants, etc. We found that lacking at other areas we tried like Tangalle and Rekawa. I wouldn't want to stay on Mirissa beach for a week, but 1-2 nights is perfect. The beach is swimmable with large waves, and you can access no less than 15 restaurants/bars right from the beach. The inland side of town offers even more options. Come night time, there is a "scene" but it never felt overly crowded to me. Compared to Thailand or Brazil, this is a VERY chill place to do the beach town thing. But if you're looking for isolation, deserted beaches to yourself, and total peace and quiet, Mirissa is not the place. If you're looking for a laid-back beach town vibe with some music coming from bars and interesting people-watching, Mirissa is for you. Appeals to all kinds of travelers in my opinion -- we saw singles, couples and families.

Nice view from the top of the rock, the day i went the water was a bit murky but some told me it was crystal clear the day before, good place for snorkeling if the water is not murky. Got to see those fishes! Couldnt catch any good waves for boogie boarding though!
Great beach for swimming and sunbathing. There's plenty of restaurants nearby and surf breaks at either end too!
Nice place. Good beach. Nice food. Not much else to do. Don't stay at Mirissa beach club hotel as this is the one disappointing thing. The staff are the worst hotel staff I have seen.

Mirissa beach is perfect for everyone they are always something to do. Such as body boarding or surfing or just relaxing in the Jamaican bar. The sunsets/sunrises are perfect over the horizon. I'll definitely go back

We spent 2 nights at a beachside hotel.  Mirissa beach was clean and unspoilt and great to walk along.  The sea was too rough for me with big breakers and an undercurrent.  I enjoyed a good paddle though!  You can walk to the little 'island' view point. At dusk the sunset is amazing and the beach turns into a restaurant mecca, as all the bars put out tables with lanterns and display their fresh fish.  A great atmosphere with (often loud) music to draw people in.
Best beach in southern province.  Nice and clean beach, several places to eat, good surf, free wifi in every restaurant.

This quite nice beach. Though private, secluded beaches are probably nicer, than this, but you need to rent a scooter or take a tuk-tuk to get to those. This beach has big waves, specially towards the evening. A lot of restaurants to choose from. There's always surfers at the right  (west) side of the beach.
Nice beach with pretty big waves to play in. Snorkelling was ok with decent visibility and there are few restaurants on the beach.
Mirissa Beach is a perfect place where to lie back and relax. The beach is quite nice, there's plenty of shops, guest houses, and restaurants. Good spot for surfers.

the beach is beautiful, with trees growing toward the wawes and some small beach bars offering drinks, sunbeds and excellent dinners with fresh fish. animated, with local and foreign people walking up and down. I would like to go back, really liked the sense of peace and life of this place

Unlike most tourist locations, Mirissa beach doesn't have lots of locals trying to sell you useless trinkets. The beach for the most part is pristine, not overly busy and is set in a very dramatic location. A great place for surfing/body boarding; and there is no shortage of places to eat or drink which also blend in with the surroundings, and the food that you get in most of them is excellent. Highly recommend the Zephyr restaurant, excellent food and great ambiance.

Very popular beach so it is full of tourists but it doesn't feel overcrowded. The western end is pretty much empty and offers a lot of shade so that was my favourite spot. There are plenty of cafes along the beach where you can cool down away from the sun and have a meal/drink. Nice place where to spend a whole day in relax!

beautiful sunrise and sunset point. many activities can be done in mirissa like Snorkeling / scuba diving / Surfing/ whale watching etc. what i personally loved was just sitting and relaxing on the beach :).
Turquoise water, rolling waves, golden sands. Beach bars.Shade if needed. Safe for children. Walks delightful.
I would recommend this beach to all tourists in Sri Lanka. It is the perfect combination of wild beach, big waves, nice parties on the beach during the night.

A very pleasant beach with plenty going on around it, particularly in the evening.  It wasn't too busy when we went.  The beach is sandy and whilst we didn't swim it didn't appear particularly rough.  In all a nice place to sit and while away some spare time during the day.
Very nice beach with excellent view. It was not very crowdy, though there are many restaraunts and parties every night at different places.

Just back from a South of Sri Lanka holiday. Mirissa by far felt like the best beach of the lot that we stopped at. The sand is fine and soft, the water was amazing to swim in and there were a lot of surfers but the beach is segregated naturally into a surfing zone and a swimming zone. There is a little rocky cropping half way down the beach which is super nice to climb and view the sunsets, which are beautiful in themselves and a lot of shacks to grab beer and grub at.
Mirissa beach offers white sand and clear blue sea; the waves are very strong and can push and pull at you. At this time of year I didn't find the beach overly busy.
Beautiful, active beach by day which turned into party central at night. Not sure if it's like that throughout the year, however we visited at Christmas time.

Whilst this beach is kinda beautiful, its surroundings including rubbish, scummy cafes, divey accommodation and peddlers, makes it seriously a sub-standard beach! Highly recommend NOT doing more than quick dip and leave. Sadly the Sri Lankans are major polluters and the beach is ruined in a big way by this - slightly unhygienic. You'd also struggle to find a bar/cafe clean or appealing enough to sit at.
The beach wasn't too crowded and the sand sloped gently into the sea rather than a steep shelf. Sufficient activity to be interesting (people watching) and a few restaurant/bars to explore.
really nice beach, clean, big waves (not for swim or kids), variety of restaurants, friendly people.

Mostly empty of tourists, this is a beautiful sandy beach lined with cafes. Sunbeds are not expensive but you need to get one with a parasol. The sea is beautifully warm but we could feel very strong currents pullin at our legs and would not go more than chest deep despite being strong swimmers. The waves were very powerful and the biggest ones were impossible to jump, they would pick you up and smash you into the sand, we got a few bumps and grazes that way, but for the hardy fool it was fun :-)

Beach cafes, on a very soft sanded beach. Wavy seas, and a lot of accommodation choices. Very touristy but not yet overwhelming. Great seafood at pretty much every restaurant. One beach over gives great views on to some wave surfers in deep waters. Better vibe than in Unawatuna Beach, Mirissa seemed to have a better mix of tourist from different countries.

We were positively surprised about Mirissa because i had read that it was dirty and was not what it used to be.We found it beautiful with very clean sand and water,plenty of bars and restaurants with sun beds, nice atmosphere with many surfers.A pity that i can not say the same about the surroundings which were very dirty.Our small,nice hotel was a few minutes walk inland,the nature along the way is fantastic if only would not be tons of rubbish spread around and also the river way quite contaminated.It is incredible !!!! how it can that be? somebody in a restaurant explain us that the rubbish collectors do not come if people do not pay them,as many are poor they prefer to though the rubbish anywhere ! what a pity.The government should do something to preserve these concern areas of this beautiful country !!

Yes, I know it's just a beach but it's the only place in Sri Lanka where I couldn't wait to get away. I was expecting a tranquil beach with a few bars, the reality is a smaller version of Tenerife. Accommodation is overpriced, service everywhere is awful as everyone is stoned, all the bars play solely Bob Marley (not sure what reggae has to do with an island in the Indian Ocean), lots of travellers with acoustic guitars all playing redemption song and western tourists generally wondering around in very little, which is obviously not in keeping with the countries primarily Buddhist, Hindu and Muslim population. Haven't been to any other beach resorts in Sri Lanka but save your time and go and visit anywhere else on the island, it's sure to be better than this stray dog haven.

If you want to surf...bring your own board from home...the rentals have crappy ones and the rates are about 500 R for 1-3 hours 1500 R for 24 Hr. Night life and some dancing available tue-friday .. Food is ok... Beware of cheap alcohol...

Good restaurants and sun beds directly at the beach. Also nice by night with all the lights. It's nice for partying but also just for meeting some friends in a calmer location. There are also live bands playing in some of the restaurants which is really enjoyable.

Good Beach for swimming, pretty calm but enough waves to attempt some body surfing! Plenty of options for food and drinks, long happy hours and seems to be a party at one of the bars each night. Not a lot of options for shade though, we couldn't get any sunloungers in the shade so spent the day under cover at one of the restaurants.
At last a nice and cosy beach, not to many of them in Sri Lanka. A bit expensive at least compared with India, but not more than any other Sri Lankean beach.
This beach is so nice! With the nice green surroundings, this feels like paradise. The beach has a lot of different restaurants, and all of them have sun beds. The sun beds are free.

Had a great time here! The waves were perfect for boogie boarding.  Beach is lined with shops/hotels. Found one with unreserved beach chairs and an umbrella - to our surprise it was free to use! Bought some drinks and rented a boogie board.

The Beach is Full with Bars & Restaurants but still has a chilling Ambience. At Night Most places serve Fish. But although it looks scenic the quality does not meet expectations. Better take the sun downer at the Beach and the Food in town.
Its a good beach, clean and warm water however the water can be a bit wavy always try to swim in the less wavy parts.

I really like this place! The view is fantastic and when I went there in the early morning there were sometimes cows on the beach which I found funny! In the evening it turns to a beautiful restaurant. Yes the prices are higher than in other parts of the country but I think we shouldn't complain about that because they are still cheaper than in Europe and other places ;-) i would not agree that it is too noisy there as long as you don't stay directly at the beach because there is a main road and the beach bars are playing music in the evening. I had a three minute walk to the beach and at night it wasn't noisy at all but very silent :)
The water was calm and clear, could see the bottom, there is a few rocks around so need to be careful

Really good, was here for a week, after that went to Unawatuna, and we realized Mirissa is so perfect! Clean and not crowded, you can rent bed&umbrella, or just find a place where you can lie on the sand. Next to the cost guard station there are concrete seats and table. If you have luck, there will be turtle nest as well! :) We loved it very much!
I'm not a surfer but our kids loved playing in the waves, but you do need to be careful, nice restaurants for lunch and dinner on the beach.
Beach is nice with white sand, blue water, waves and a lot of restaurants. Beach and water are clean. In one part you can also surf a little bit. Definitely one of the best beaches in Sri Lanka.

Its a small beach (not too small) with the finest sand i found so far and the water is pristine clear. Perfect for bodyboarding and wave jumping, also can swim a bit further in as there seems to be no undercurrent as far as i know. The beachfront is dotted with small restaurants with the usual seafood and rice and curries, some unlicensed but they advertise the bring your own drink so basically you can just buy your beer from next door, walk over and drink it there, very laid back. It is all outdoors, some tables in the sand, some on platforms, prices are almost the same too. No vendors wondering around on the beach(not a single one) so its relaxing. Dotted with tons of palm trees and sun loungers that you just take, no need to pay for them - if its there and noone is sitting on it, its yours! There is an area that is full of whale watching tours so you can sort that too. Also every evening a different restaurant hosts the evening disco - some dance/house music, i recon it is the same DJ as the music is the same and you know from the big strobe lights in the night in front of the place. It is casual, we did not wear shoes or flipflops at all. Be aware of the strength of the sun - sounds a bit obvious but nonetheless we managed to get burnt by lunchtime on day one, especially as the water is so clear, you can burn badly. Beautiful beach, highly recommended, very relaxed. We spent 5 days here and were not bored(the waves and people trying to dodge the bigger ones gives excellent entertainment).

Such a beautiful beach, fun swimming as there's some waves but not too much which gives the option of body boarding. At night time it comes alive with all the pretty lights and selection of around 10 places for dinner which all serve fresh fish amongst a great selection of other dishes. Highly recommended for either a day or night visit.
One of the most beautiful beaches in south of Sri Lanka. There are some hotels and restaurants around. The beach is suitable for surfing as well.

Mirissa Beach - popular with foreign tourists provides opportunities for water sports - especially surfing. In the nearby area are many shops, restaurants, bars and other amenities. The beach is very close to the A2 Galle to Matara main road and traffic can b very busy and noisy at times
Just my fave place on the coast! Not far from Weligama (5 km), which is famous surf place. So amazing sand and clean water.. I recommend to visit it!

This a beach to have a stroll on and also have fun with the surf where there are great waves rolling in with many body boarding or just swimming into them: but be careful they are strong and one woman ended up with a bloody nose as a result of one wave. We were at the Paradise Club so could enjoy the beach right outside the hotel. It's great place to soak the sun after a morning whale watching.

We were staying up the road at the Lantern Hotel which was approx. 5 minutes away. Mirissa Beach was heaps more crowded & very touristy. Although it did look safer for swimming than at our beach at Kamburugamuwa . A good place to for dining as there are heaps of restaurants along the beachfront.

This is a tourist beach with good choice of service in it. There is evidentially so much people that you can lay off even a Sri Lankan style of service. This means that you have to wait everything quite long and if you don't show you want service they won't offer it... It's good beach for relaxing and swimming. Eat somewhere at the city though (better food).

Pretty quiet. Not too busy, with many korean and russian tourists. Really fun for a swim, with shallow water quite far out. Completely sand covered bottom, with a reef break surf spot naturally enclosed at the west end.

By far the cleanest beach I have seen this trio, beautiful golden sand with great surf.  The beach is backed by palm tress has some great places to eat and drink along.  Not bothered by people selling their wares.  The beach loungers and umbrellas are all free. Lovely walk to the end of the. Each and onto s little island. Absolutely perfect.

After travelling around some of the off the beaten track parts of Sri Lanka for a few weeks it's very pleasant to arrive in a place that seems to welcome tourists warmly. Mirissa beach is beautiful and there is lots to do: the surf is great, the beachside bars are quaint, there are massages on offer and there is variety in food - a blessing if you've been living on Sri Lankan curry and fried rice for any length of time. Prices are a little elevated, and there are a lot more of the annoying tourist types, but that's the price you pay I guess.
If you want a relaxing stay do not go to Mirissa! Especially at night!! Europeans and some Asians allowed only

Mirissa Beach has the soft fine sand and if you are a beach walker, this is the best. The waves can get high but swimming is fun and the water is clean and warm. Restaurants line the beach, all serving fresh caught fish and seafood of the day, grilled to your liking. Lounge chairs are available free infront of the restaurants in the hope that you buy food and drink from them but they don't bother you for business. It's a great chill beach with a good vibe.

Great sandy beach. Surf spots at either end. Great shore break to body surf or take yhe kids in on bodyboards. Great turtle watching vantage point at eastern end of the beach! Great cocktail bars and sunsets. Only slight issue - the bar owners are not great at cleaning the beach for litter - especially after the tides are at their biggest. There isn't loads or anything, but I found myself collecting bits of rubbish on returning to my hotel after surfing between 6-9am. A little more respect for the environment wouldn't go a miss by all beach users though frankly.
Nice place to sweam in rather calm sea and relax on the sand, a lot of cafes where you can eat sea food and other tasty meals.

The beach has beautiful, fine sand, but there are restaurants and businesses all over the beach.  There is a little hill to climb for more views of the water.  It's a beautiful place and popular with many tourists.

It's a nice stretch of beach but the waves can be fairly big. There are rocky areas at either end -- great for finding small fish and crabs-- though we came across a small sea snake so be careful. There are lots of bar shacks along the beach and most do food. The place in the evening becomes a sea food/ fish eaters delight, just make your choice and have it cooked to order. When we were there it never got very busy, there are some sun beds but some have seen better days.
Stunning golden sandy beach with an abundance of good eateries and ample space to find a secluded spot to lie and soak up the sun. Safe swimming too !

The beach was a nice beach. We walked all along and up the rock that juts out of the sea. A nice viewing point. From the rock we could see the snorkelling areas and spotted a long eel and lots of those horrible Black Sea urchins. Nasty if you stand on one. These sea urchins were clinging to rocks near where people are swimming so be very careful. There was also jelly fish here, a couple washed up and some people got small stings. Not sure what type of jellyfish they were but assume they not to bad or they,surely, would warn people of the dangers. The current was extremely rough with a very strong under current and huge waves that make it difficult to get in to the sea. Several restaurants line the beach with all choices of food. Very expensive though. So if on a budget, bring your own food. A couple of bars banged out tunes, if you like that sort of thing. One was packed with people so a popular place to party. They have evening parties here too, so again, a great place to go for a party. (Beer is 500 rupees though!)

This was one of the most beautiful beaches I've ever been. Just a few bars right on top, many good surf spots, relaxed habitants, every night a party in just one bar. As we came to Sri Lanka, we wanted to stay here for a few days... But we extended our stay for the complete trip (as you can reach any point of interest in the surrounding area by a day trip). Loved this place so hard!

In February  it was hot enough  to require  recliner  seats  and a parasol . Good thing  was that there is no charge  for use. We spent  6 hours lounging  at no cost. There os no hassle  to buy anything ,  it is actually  sometimes  challenging  to fing someone  to get a beer from.  Beach itself is a little  dirty.lots and lots of fag butts near the seating  areas. waves a little  rough. sometimes  2 meter swell or more ,  and lots of sand churned  up. great place  for sunset and evening  meal ( that is a little  more expensive  than the main street)

We spent a few days in Mirissa and while I know it is now high season the beach was packed with tourists. There are so many other beaches within walking distance or down the coast that are better and less crowded.
this was one of our nicest stays in Sri Lanka. There is a variety of things to do around, such as the Whale Watching.
Good place for relax, surf and explore. Visit some restaurants along the beach and enjoy a breakfasts around 400rupies.

I'm going to rate this beach five star even though it has one or two issues. Pros: Tropical paradise - most tropical beach I have ever seen Extremely photogenic Beautiful grainy sand Not too crowded (although not extremely quiet either) A great beach to chill out on for a few days Negatives: Restaurants playing loud music at certain points along the beach!! Can't really swim here - waves are very big and strong Can't snorkel in most areas as a result of the waves but there are some coves.

I visited Mirissa in last week of December, 2015. Mirissa beach is perfect place for those seeking quiet place next to beach. It is small place but has its own charm. Nice local restaurants on the beach offer tasty sea food, local food and drinks. Great place to relax and chill!!
great location and beach...whale watching tours are good bit of a chase amongst the boats for best view
A beautiful long sandy beach with plenty of activity, safe bathing areas and some excellent surfing and many restaurants & bars to choose from

I was here at evening after long trip. I visited the Mirissa Eye restaurant at sunset, and it was very relaxed: waves, sun, beer. During the day there a lot of places to hide from the sun under palms. But be aware, in less than 100 meters is a main road, and on the dark time it's a bit fearfully to go along the road. Better try to find the apartments close to the beach.

The best  beach  in Sri Lanka. Very safe for swimming,  there are waves,  but not big and dangerous .on the beach the sand is almost white, very clean, not far from city center. There are lots of shacks and restaurants. Many sunbeds  (blue colour ) and umbrellas are for free.

This is truly one of the best beaches in Sri Lanka "OVERALL". Its great to swim, great to enjoy dinners and meals by the sea, It has one of the best atmospheres for beaches in Sri Lanka. There is good food & drinks by the beach. Whale watching is available on season. It is also one of the most popular destinations of tourists coming to Sri Lanka. Accommodation could improve as only a few start class hotels available at the moment.

Mirissa Beach is absolutely beautiful but we must have been there during the change of seasons as the waves were huge, leaving almost no beach. Because of the surf, we decided to eat at one of the beach-side restaurants and continue up the coast a bit to our next stop.
Probably the best beach in Sri Lanka. Very scenic and safe for swimming. lots of restaurants and shacks on the beach for shade and food.
This is a lovely place to be both day or night. Love the views. Waves are fun but you need to be careful of the current. Managed a bit of snorkeling too. Lovely in the evening for a drink.

The beach is average though it is clean but crowded in the evening. Nice place to hangout but traveling all the way to see this place seems waste of time and money specially locals are seen as unwanted here. The beach is good for Swimming and surfing but the food joints are local unfriendly they directly or indirectly say we don't serve locals
The beach is very neat, has nice views. One can climb up the view point and relax on the rocks near the beach. It is a nice experience

For me the best beach in Sri Lanka. It is little crowdy but the sand is really soft and wawes are great fun! You can see the real beauty of this beach after the sunset - it is full of restaurants and nice music.
We were suprised that this beach was so magical even if there were so many people. The dinner on the beach was the best on Sri Lanka.
Best place to chill, learn surfing, do some scuba diving, rent a scooter  and travel around passing by all beautiful beaches in the south of Sri Lanka.
This once beautiful beach is now spoiled. Too many tourists and ugly buildings. You might be better off looking elsewhere.
This is the best beach to cover on West coast, the water is clean, sand is not coarse, not commercial, hence neat n clean.Variety of eating options available as well.

great beach, in january the sea was calm with some waves, really great for swimming, a lot of bars and restaurants down the beach for chilling during the day and night, on the road there are some small shops for souvenirs and mini markets, it is perfect for people who want to stay on a nice beach but still dont want to be board on their holiday
Popular among tourists and with lots of restaurants and hotels this is a nice beach for swimming, surfing and eating. A beautiful bay with sand to lay down on or for the kids to play on.

One of those beaches that really gets under your skin. It has progressively become busier over the years but still holds on to its niche status. Go now before it becomes to over run and loses that charm that many beaches do when they become over run with traffic.
Nice beach, while it does have many people for a swim or surf. After taking a dip, you can stop by Zephyrs for lunch or a drink.
Mirissa beach is beautiful! The sand is gorgeous and soft, the sea is warm and the atmosphere is relaxed. It really was a little paradise!

This beach was great for lounging in the sun throughout the day. Plenty of bars and restaurants. The sea was nice although maybe not the best for surfers. The sunset here is beautiful from the rock in the sea.

We caught the number 350 bus from Galle, bought the ticket on the bus which was 50 SL Rupees and took the hours ride to Mirissa. The bus journey was quite an experience with loud reggae type music blaring all the way. Anyway, we made it and the journey was well worth it, such a beautiful, peaceful beach. Whale watching trips were advertised. The sand was lovely and the palms swayed in the light breeze. Well worth a visit.
Recommended. Big waves. Fun for playing, but not recommended for smaller children. Lots of great resturants along the beach
Plenty of activities to do... Whale watching trips, good food and great weather. I stayed at Mandara report on my trip to Mirissa.It's an exceptional hotel.
Well, a week before I was in South Goa, so I expected something similar...but actually there isn't too much to see or do at Mirissa beach unfortunately.
A very clean white sandy beach. Sea can be very rough , with large waves   Very dangerous with jet skiers weaving in and around swimmers  no safety lanes or designated markers.
I love this place! I want to stay for ever. Great for walks, bars, restaurants, SURFING! Hotels and apartments. The people are sooooooo friendly!

Decided to do a day trip here. Lovely beach with a few eating houses to choose from - service at these  a bit hap hazard. Please be careful in water - my wife chose the wrong wave to body surf in and was thrust to the seabed - result was injury to her neck, a broken nose and a large cut- a trip by ambulance to Matara general hospital and an overnight staywas the result - an experience in itself. We wanted to see the bay at night as we had read how beautiful it was - never mind, maybe next time
There are plenty of places to eat and beach side guest rooms. The beach has areas to suit all age groups with a really big wave area for surfing and a flatter area towards the east side of the beach.

Lovely beach with a lively bar and restaurant scene in the evenings especially. There are sun beds and umbrellas available but not enough and some had seen better days. Shade is a must at mid-day so I would say get to the beach early if you intend to stay all day and that way you may be able to bag a shade! Beach is clean, the waves can be rough but the water remains quite shallow for a good distance out.
We been to Mirrissa beach, unawatu na and hikkaduwa, my favourite was this one, you can do body boarding little wavey to swin but lots of fun, you can find sunbeds availible

A back packers paradise. Lovely clean beach, though some parts are rocky. Sat sipping my pineapple juice watching two little boys running in and out of the waves as their mother stood watching. The body boarders were not just youngsters but older folks like me too, the brave and the young at heart ones. The waves didn't look that high for surfing, but can be deceiving. Was concerned to see no life guards present. Many cafes and restaurants along the beach, offering food, drinks and rooms. A lovely beach to just chill and watch the young ones having fun.

Lovely sand, superb water quality, restaurants along the Beach- however the one we picked was over priced and very poor quality food... others may be better.  We asked for a discount which didnt go down very smoothly. Waiter kept telling us that service is not included... in the end the Manager came up to our table and was quite agressive.... shame

One of the best beaches I have visited and it was very crowded with more tourists than the locals. Plenty of restaurants around to have food but was a disappointed with some of them as we found better places to eat outside the beach.
It's scenic, not so crowded and it has its own personality. Enjoyed an evening there, not so many waves but it's better to take care swimming at the rocky part.

Mirissa beach is near-perfect, with its gentle waves and sun-kissed shore line. It also serves as the perfect point from which to do a day trip to Galle (the fort area) and return to this quiet little paradise. The more secluded parts of Mirissa beach (walk through and past the main beach) are simply amazing - you have the beautiful ocean, which is shared with 4-5 other people. Careful of getting in too deep, the currents can be strong.

The beach is very accessible, warm water & a nice blue turquoise colour, plenty of restaurants on the beach too. Great for learning how to surf on the left side of the beach. the waves arnt too big on the main section.. Great sunset views too

So many beach restaurants along the beach front - pick which ever one you fancy and park up for the day/night. If you have a drink in the day at one you are able to use the sun loungers out the front. Good swimming but waves can be rougher than they look. Most restaurants are also hotels so can grab a cheap room beach front and enjoy hiring body boards for very little cash.
You won't be alone, but it's a beautiful stretch of sandy beach with water that is just the right temperature.

I nearly met my maker on Mirissa Beach! I tried Belly Boarding, only this kindly Aussie chap swam up beside me and my mate and said, "Do you mind if I give you some tips?" We were all ears for the next few minutes. Only then he says, "Actually guys, we ought to head into shore a bit." We had been so engrossed that we had started to drift out and a bit too close for comfort to a big rock in the sea, and the waves were coming in, and I have a bit of a 'dodgy shoulder' - hence I had the very first 'panic attack' I have ever suffered in my entire life and I just couldn't get my breath. If it hadn't have been for that kindly Aussie I'm not sure I'd have made it back to shore....but it's still a good beach, but not as exceptional as my favourite beach in south Phuket whose name defeats me.

Love how Mirissa was just one beach and not a big tourist place. Here it is relatively easy to meet other travelers and the restaurants were mostly great and fare priced. Quite a lot of backpackers which made it easy to meet people and gave the whole beach a relaxed, but ongoing feeling.
Very nice. There are so many restaurants and bars on about half km range of the beach. I went in evening. It was amazing..!
Its a good beach for a swim and surfing. And in the evenings had time for trying some fishing by a rocky cliff by the beach.
Nice and not crowded beach. Few restaurants and backpackers hostels. On the left side (next to fisherman village) few spots for snorkelling

The beach from Mirissa is very clean and perfect for enjoying the sun or walking. The waves are very different depending where on the beach you are but can be quet high what makes the beach also perfect for learning to surf or more experienced surfers.

Mirissa is a very touristy place, packed with guesthouses, hotels and bars on the beach. You see hardly any locals and some restaurants even say 'locals are not allowed'. The waves are great and the whale watching trip is worth doing. But if you prefer a quieter place then book your hotel/guesthouse a bit further from Mirissa where the beach is beautiful as well.
rather touristic place to be, crowded but friendly. Wonderful, real Tropical view beach like you see at pictures. enough to do and to experience.

A lovely beach for the daytime and evening. Lots of waves in the sea and each to find a spot to relax during the day. Restaurants and bars located along the beach front. In the evening you can choose fresh fish to be cooked from one of the many stalls along the beach.

The beach is very beautiful and the vibe of that place is amazing.There are also two surf spots,for intermediate surfers.Plenty of restaurants,but  most of them are overpricing the seafood..And the thing we did not liked is that there was not a single beach bar,where you can have a drink or two in the evening.
Nice swimming beach with many places to stay and eat but quite a busy beach. We only walked through and had a drink on the beach but nice ambience. A fair number of families too.
Excellent place for peaceful holiday. It is an enjoyable place for people of all ages especially who are interested in swimming and water sports. Plenty of tasteful sea food is available.

This is one of the tourist places hence is a very busy beach with many shacks around playing live music or records. They display fresh fishes caught during the day which you can choose and they will prepare and serve you. There are plenty of resorts and hotels to stay around this beach. Most famous activity is whale watching.

Very nice beach with some restaurants and cool bars. But not too much. Only one big hotel on one side. And with our kids (7 and 9 years old), we had especially appreciated the area watched by the life guards. A surf lesson (around 1 hour and half) costs 3000 LKR (around 20 dollars).

Great bay of golden sand. Nice waves to catch on a body board - even the 5 and 6 year old were in there. Probably one of the only places on the south coast I would put the kids in as the rip is really strong around that part of the island.
