The bars start to ramp up the music at around 7pm and go till very late (sometime till 4am) If you've had an exhausting day in the surf and chasing kids on the beach and in the pool then you won't hear the music. If you are a light sleeper then you may be annoyed.
By relaxing beach, great for a surf or. Swim. Lots of little restaurants along the sea, especially great at night when all the little restaurants have lamps on the tables.

Went in Jan'16. Place is full of foreigners. 40% of people I met were from Amsterdam. It is a very nice beach. Crystal clear water, white sand. You can go sunbathing. There are few good resorts beach side like Marina Bay sands etc. In the evening the sunbathing and swimming stops and it becomes a candle light dinner place with lovers frnds and families. You can see stalls of Sea food outside every restaurant and pick the fish you want after negotiating prices with vendor. Though the restaurants get closed at max by 11 PM. Try to reach there early.

Probably the best beach we've visited so far. There's are lots of bars and restaurants along the beach but many of them are quiet and chilled out. Some play loud music. Beware of the current and huge waves that appear from nowhere on the main beach! We found the sea much calmer when you walk five mins up the beach, past Mirissa rock to Papa Mangos bar. It's also a great spot to enjoy a beer and watch the sunset. On the main beach there are plenty of sun beds to relax on. We recommend the Mirissa Eye restaurant for fantastic seafood. Enjoy!
Mirissa Beach is definitively better than overpriced Unawatuna Beach, next to Galle. Mirissa Beach is far more natural and natural, less aggressive in tourist facilities.
We loved mirissa. Very chilled out but with some great restaurant/bars with sun beds and umbrellas. Good waves but can swim as well and good whale watching tours from the harbour
Awesome beach with big waves which were great fun! Quite a few options for food, especially at night when the restaurants spread out onto the beach and present all there fresh fish!
Best and cleanest beach in Sri Lanka , also stunning to eat under The Stars at night, lots of restaurants with candlelight dinners along The beach
The mirissa beach is overall very beautiful and offers a lot of restaurants and bars with a nice view. The beach is relatively crowded though (for Sri Lanka) and therw is some trash lying around.
The beaches are still not very clean. There are people always wanting their next meal ticket and taking photos will cost you money.

Sea very warm and pleasant. Restaurants on beach expensive but beach environment great for eating and drinking. Choose the restaurants with more people in. Be careful of the sea urchin spines hidden in the surf and on the rocks.
Great beach for swimming, body surfing, people watching, smoothie drinking, exercise and sunbathing!
Yes, its right, I can't stop thinking about this place and will come back in a few months cz its paradise in the middle of the ocean and everyone has to come here at least once

The beac is really nice, with palm trees and a lovely sunset spot. Unfortunately, we founded too crowdy, with loud Bob Marley music ( was'nt he from Jamaica??). If you lime crowded beaches this is definately for you.

Mirissa is another good place to visit on the way down. The waves are not worth surfing if your there for surf. Get a tut tut to jungle beach area or Madiha. Good beach parties in mirissa as well. Not as wild as hikkaduwa but still good. Good beach for family's and inexperienced surfers

Mirissa Beach remains one of the most beautiful beaches of the South of Sri Lanka, despite it being more and more touristic. I particularly enjoyed the less visited part, further from the main beach, as you stroll along the shore towards Bandaramulla. The beach is not that wide and there are very few cafes compared to the main part, where the beach is wide and the restaurants abound. Suitable for young children.

A lovely huge clean beach with plenty of scope to be on your own or in the thick of it... We found a lovely spot to the eastern side which was much quieter & less beach bars. To the western side you can hire the dreaded jet ski's (another good reason to head to the eastern side for the peace). Many of the bars also hire surfboards & body boards. Most places have beach beds which are free & there was no pressure on you to use their facilities, but one does as a courtesy! Of an evening all the bars put tables on the sand & the place is strewn with twinkling fairy lights...quite magical.  A great spot to watch the sun go down too... They all serve fresh fish, which is displayed for you to choose.  Most bars stop serving food around 9.30-10pm. The sand was soft & lovely to take a stroll along. The sea was very clean but can be a bit rough with lovely waves lashing the beach...so be weary with small children or if you are a less confident swimmer. Remember....only leave footprints in the sand
Beautiful  beach with safe swimming. Many choices of eats sits, drinks. Great place to watch the su set over the palm trees.
One of the most stunning beaches in Sri Lanka with lots of activities to do or just relax and soak in the views

The sand is white and tender, the locals say it is the best beach in sri-lanka. Lots of cafes and restaurants with fresh fish, beach activities such as volleyball, surfing, jet-ski, dolphins/whales watching. There are guards ready to save you from water, although there is only one strong wave you have to get over (I lost my sunglasses there) and you can enjoy undisturbed water. No wind. Beautiful jogging in the morning, almost no dogs - there are some but they are really friendly.

Beautiful, relaxing beach, but be careful of the undercurrent, its very easy to get knocked over during high tide, or strong currents, even for experienced swimmers. The stretch of beach we were on didn't have a lifeguard that we saw, but we were at a bar/hotel, and made sure we kept sight of our friends!!! The water is gloriously clear, with ample opportunities for watersports, snorkeling, surfboarding etc, and was one of my favourite beaches of Sri Lanka!!

Mirissa Beach is more quiet than Unawatuna, and we were told that sellers were banned from the beach. The water and the beach is clean and warm, and there's a lot of restaurants along the beach. Apparently a nice place to surf, and the seafood is quite allright. Would recommend to go if you want a bit more quiet place, nice for families.

Got the bus from Unawatuna, & spent a few hours there, walking the beach, having lunch & a few beer.  Much better for walking along, than the beach at Unawatuna Its getting busier & busier every time I go.  Nice to see the small hill at the east end of the beach open to the public again, its been at least 3 years since the last time you could go up it, pictures very nice from the top
The beach is nice an clean. But there are quite no trees because the beach is very narrow. So there is also no shadow....
Nice beach with some relaxed bars and restaurants. Surfing, snorkeling, jet ski possible. Really enjoyed the place and would recommend it.

I'd read reviews of how beautiful Mirissa was. Was is the operative word. Techno music blasting out At midnight and restaurants offering chips with everything. Seven months of waiting for a relaxing beach holiday and then this! My idea of hell. Oh dear, I so wish I'd gone somewhere else. Don't go. Sri Lanka can be lovely; why do the cheap and tacky, noisy and tasteless get to spoil it for everyone else?
Very nice beach, many bars, music and fun to morning. Clean sand and wather. All day is god waves :)

A less more touristy than unawatuna but much more touristy than tangalle. Always a lot of waves. Good for surfers. There's sun chairs with parasol along the beach but you need to be out around 9 am to get one. A lot of restaurants. Food at the beach are in general expensive and nothing special.
A very crowded beach, a bit like Costa del sol... but nice for swimming. A lot of options for food. ---------------------------

A lovely sweeping beach with plenty of places to eat and drink. We asked for the rental fee for some sun beds outside a bar at the west end of the bay and they were free. The beach slopes fairly gently into the sea, so despite the fairly big waves it is pretty easy to stay within your depth. At the west end of the bay there are some flat rocky outcrops in the shallows which I walked past without paying attention. As I swam back in with the waves over these rocks I found to my discomfort they were covered in very sharp sea urchins. I was buffeted by the waves and was lanced many times, but other than that I would definitely recommend.
Party beach, many people but not too much. Some nice bars with good music. We have been there for New Year's Eve and it was nice.
One of the better beaches in SL but the music is pretty annoying turn it down a bit guys or put on something A bit more chilled out

Yes it's a nice beach, great for families etc and lots of places to eat. Couple of surf spots but locals were all dropping in, maybe they don't know the rules. Also most of the young locals serving you couldnt be half Assed you were there, not all but many. If you dont like package holiday places with happy hour bars on the beach then just go to visit. Apparently in the evening are evil sand flies.

This is one of the best beaches we have been to in the world. There are 3 beaches, 1 for snorkelling however the actual beach is very small. 1 for surfing and the other for chilling. Crystal blue sea, huge waves and lots of bars. Who couldn't love this place. The thing we liked was it was much more chilled than Hikkaduwa. Well worth a visit.
Great beach, great beach life, good for people watching, surfing and lounging food is a little behind the rest of SL, need more variety and quality

Very clean beach, water was blue there and tides are enjoyable... so many tourists from all over the world... a lovely sunset and great evening with lion beer at shacks over the shore....one of the most beautiful beach from sri lanka..

big problem in mirissa now rooms are not in roupies but in $ & € so expensive for  not very good accommodation  they build too many hotels quickly  sometimes dangerous buildings they dont respect the norms of security hotel  sunbeam  please dont go on the balcony they can fall  anyway the beach is so nice   too much noise in the night
Clean water with some good waves. Spoiled a bit by the development on the beach front and the restaurants playing crappy music.

The road is closed to the beach but with the sound of the waves you do not hear the traffic. The beach is perfect, a small island, perfect waves and no rocks (compared with Tangalle). There is also an area with lifeguards so the beach is very safe. At night, the beach becomes a huge restaurant and you do not recognise it. The sand is very sticky...I needed 3 showers to remove the sand on hairs, neck...
The end of Mirissa beach closest to the harbour is by far the nicest.There are plenty of beach restaurants and the rocks and surf make it great for ambience
The best part of Marissa was the Whales. What a stunning sight. They are so big and amazing. To also see the dolphins and turtles was a treat.

The beach surely was a paradise once. Now it's full of overpriced low quality restaurants. You better eat somewhere else. But it's nice to have a drink there, listen to music and watch the waves. The beach is so crowded with tourists that you sometimes cannot find a place to  lay down on the small sandstripe which doesn't get overflooded.

As an expat living in Sri Lanka, I'd heard a lot of good things about Mirissa beach so went there the other day and it is horrid. Far too many cafes and tourists that have now taken up all the space on the beach meaning there is nowhere to sit unless at a cafe. We planned to stay the night there, walked down it then had second thoughts. We went to Matara beach instead which is quiet, no tourists around and is real unspoilt paradise, away from tacky touristy crap. I'd recommend Bentota beach for anyone that wants a much less touristy beach with only a smattering of cafes that don't encroach on the nature. It's also much more beautiful, too.
Probably one of the best beaches in Southern Sri Lanka to visit with family for a good swim. The food around the restaurants are quite expensive though.

Mirissa is an awesome place for those interested in beach holiday with special interest in whale watching. There are many accommodation along the beach. The beaches are full of corals rather than sea shells. You can go for snorkelling if you wish to. Go for Whale watching with Geeth.

Relatively nice beach with the core set of features you'd expect: sand, waves, palm trees,  and overpriced bars. Other reviews set high paradise-esque expectations of this beach but my girlfriend and I found the beach to be rather average and reminiscent of any beaches in the mediterranean. If you're in the area you might as well have a stroll down the beach but don't bank on any profound experiences!

Mirissa Beach is by no means a laid back destination. Nevertheless it is very picturesque. The crowds consist of backpackers and flashpackers and contribute to a certain vibe. In the evening you can sit at candlelit tables directly by the water and listen to house or reggae. For me this is rather a cool than an idyllic place.

Reading the reviews for Mirissa beach I had higher expectations. But this narrow beach reminds more of the packed charter beaches in Thailand more than anything else. There are much better options in Sri Lanka if you want nice beaches!
Quite good beach with great waves to jump into. Restaurants + rentals are there. What prevents it from Excellent rating is that there is no shade there. You can buy an umbrella though...
great sand, beautiful water, strong waves, great cafes and very clean. Most favourite beach in the area.
Wide white sand, fairly rough surf, but with some good breaks at the south end.  Good food and drinks.
Not as crowded and very clean.  Beautiful.  There are places to eat and relax.  Great way to enjoy some sun and ocean.
Its average compared to many other top spots in Srilanka. Its not very secluded and busy due to sheer numbers of tourists

Mirissa is a beautiful beach. Clean sand, warm waster. The waves are a bit rough but were a plus for us. The beach has lots of restaurants but during the day they don't impact your enjoyment. It's touristy but not too tacky. You can even grab a lounge bed with an umbrella and due to the weirdly slow and inattentive service you likely won't need to order from that restaurant. The restaurants on the beach offer some of the best and worst food we had in Sri Lanka. It's worth being picky if you're eating. The service at the beach restaurants is, strangely, consistently slow and inattentive. The service was really confusing. A well coordinated joke, but for no understandable benefit. I wouldn't normally be so harsh or disappointed and I understand the lack of sophistication in their systems and staff. But because the restaurants exist only to cater for tourists, it's pretty disappointing. And so inconsistent with our experiences in smaller towns, touristy places like Ella and restaurants in Colombo that cater more for local patrons. We haven't been to other beach towns yet. But this is something to be mindful of in choosing your beach destination.
Paradise Beach in Mirissa has beautiful sand and great waves.  Lots of good places to eat and drink.  Great place to be!

The beach is sizeable with a good long stretch of sand that is quite wide too. The beach face is a little steep,and so the breakers can catch you unawares when they hit the shore. But the water is delightful. It is not jarringly cold and is both warm and refreshing at the same time. It is fairly calm only a few meters away from shore. If you time it right, it is easy to get past the wash of the breaking waves. Good to swim at, very family friendly. Enough seating and sun beds along the length of the beach (particularly if you get there early) as most Cafes have something on offer. Highly recommended.

The Mirissa beach is beautiful. It's a lot smaller compared to Unawatuna, but still big enough and the waves are endless. The east side of the beach (near to the big rock) is the best. The restaurants are better here (still far from perfect but OK). Great to see the waves crashing into the beach. And lots of fun to dive in and play. The days fly by here in a very relaxing manner. Restaurants on the west side to be avoided, they were poor in terms of food and service

It was a lovely experience riding a small fishing boat and indulge into the corals in this very clean Mirissa beach. People loves sand bathing and snorkeling as well. I met a lovely family nearby and we went fishing and have a simple picnic along the beach. It was a memorable experience.

Great balance between calm and social. There are no salesmen harassing you and you can lend a sunbed free of charge if you just buy something at the restaurant (a beer for example). At night the restaurants serves fresh seafood (catch of the day) that is just delicious!

The restaurants on the beach (every single one I visited had horrible service and average food) take over the beach with their tables and chairs...there are few shaded areas but lot of people fight for those...the beach itself is nice with soft sand...not the place you'll find peace and quiet though...
A Beach to enjoy both for swimmers and surfers. Lot of samll and bigger cafes and resorts to chill out when not in water.

A beautiful beach. Not a big beach but very relaxing with plenty of food and beverage options. The water is warm and the waves not too big, so easy swimming. I did notice at the western end there was some surfers. When I come to Sri Lanka again I would definitely come back for a few days.

Restaurants - but  yet to find good service restaurant as they take  own time so order Very early ,,, beautiful for light surfing & sun & wally ball & location is amazing , 1 hour from Capital Colombo & 1.5 hra from Airport on the Express way

We were in the area since we had been whale watching. Beautiful, soft, light coloured sand. Broad expanse of beautiful beech with no litter. The ocean is crystal clear - I could see my shadow in the sand from the pristine waters above. Calm waters with gentle waves. This is one of the best beaches I have been blessed to experience. Plenty of chairs and umbrellas to hire. Not at all commercially busy which is a huge bonus. Loved my time there.
This area is famous for whale watching,Bathing,Surfing and fishing.peoples are coming here enjoy their vacation

Having stayed at Mirissa for 1 week over New Years period - We noticed it to be very busy around New Years eve and the days leading up to it. However is was nice and quiet in the days following New Years. The beach is beautiful, soft sand and very clean in comparison to Unawatuna, The beach bars are all very similar, expect long waits for your food, and pretty laid back service! But this is all part of the beach culture in my opinion. If you are looking for excellent food and service - probably best to avoid this place. The music can be a bit annoying, at least if it was good techno some punters would be happy! The vibe at Zepher on NYE was excellent. Water is beautiful - waves are great fun and there is a sheltered cove at one end of the beach for kids to enjoy without getting smashed by waves! Away from the main beach there are some great family run restaurants which I would highly recommend. The Golden Gate restaurant is a 5min tuk tuk from Mirissa beach towards Matara. The food is delicious and it is very reasonably priced! Sadeep is the young waiter who is very friendly and I went surfing with him a few days along the amazing coastline with very few other surfers :)

Mirissa has, or probably had, the potential for being an interesting beach. It has the surf, it has rocks that break the waves for possibilities to avoid the waves, it has a good located for different excusions However, Mirissa Beach is packed with restaurants trying to get as close to the water as possible and competing to play music as loud and long as possible as the night turn into dawn. Plastic chairs, tables, sunbeds and party tents are placed all over the beach front giving the whole place a tacky feeling. The tide floats everywhere around you using these facilities. (Reading the Lonely Planet guide 2015 edition about Hikkaduwa is actually more of a description of Mirissa, whereas Hikkaduwa is a relaxed beach). Finally this rather short stretch of sand is packed with tourist. If I got it right Mirissa is really great if you want the all night party and one or two smokes. It is also a good place for excursions and surfing beyond beginner's level. If you want to relax at the beach, maybe in the sade of a palm tre, be able to get some sleep - Go somewhere else!
Beach is too busy and not good for surfing due to rocks in the bay. Also there are jet skis and some bars play techno music, so you feel like on a cheap tourist beach.

We planned a week here to relax after trekking around the rest of the country. In my opinion, the beach is not nice enough to spend so much time. Pros: soft sand, walking distance from hotels, clean water, pretty view. Cons: this is a small strip of beach so it gets very crowded, almost no shade unless you want to pay to lounge at a restaurant, waves can be rough, getting a hard sell from every restaurant as you walk the beach. It's not the worst beach in the world, but it's not a good place to relax and you will be ready to leave after a day or two.
A nice sand beach with some surf idea for body boarding with younger children.  A selection of restaurants but get there early to get a table for sunset.

Go for smaller beaches in the area arround mirissa. Mirissa might be the most beautiful Beach, but it is crowded and expensive. There are beautiful smaller beaches in the area, where you can relax better and save some bucks too

The beach is nice - wide with a soft sand and beautiful sea which can get rough when it is windy but it is all very pleasant for chilling out, running or just walking. One of the terrible things is that foreigners leave their rubbish on the beach. it happened over Christmas and New Year's period and nobody is bothered to clean it. We were told the police is corrupted and there is no control over it and if the locals clean the beach a little, they just shuffle the rubbish further away from the beach and later during the day you can smell it. There are dogs on the beach which seem to be nobody doing their "whatever they have to" and nobody seems to be bothered. The most annoying thing is extremely noisy tecno music coming from every bar starting from 10pm until 3.30 am. We had only 1 night a good sleep from 11 when is was raining and the bars closed earlier. We complained as many others and we were told there is nothing can be done as the police doesn't care. We are not coming back and not going to recommend this beach to anyone who wants the relaxing holiday!
The Mirissa beach is a lovely beach.. On new year eve it was fabulous and the vibe was a very positive one

Clean and lively Mirissa Beach. Everyone's happy to soak in the sun when we visited earlier.  It seemed clean compared to other polluted beaches in Asia. A bit crowded but manageable to swim with not having elbows to elbows with strangers. A must try in Mirissa.

Vrry crowded, waves don't make it really nice to swim, lots of sand washing up. But if you like to jump around in the waves, then you're fine here. Don't expect nice clear water. Beach is very clean. Nice island specially to watch the sunset.
Good Beach and good seafood. enjoyed watching the whales. I aso enjoyed the seafood. there were choices of lobsters, calamari, jumbo prawns etc. Hotel is also priced with decent budget.

Definitely a beach to chill out. First place I see in Sri Lanka which is not dirty because you won't see any locals (sorry to say). The waves are huge and fun to play with. Mostly couples and families to see. Bars and restaurants with bad service included (except Zephyr restaurant) - just bring a lot of patience. The only thing I missed is a Kiosk or a place where you can simply buy a bottle of water. No public toilets. Safe guards. Great scenery and the water is clear and warm. Enjoy!
Favourite beach - clean, incredible waves, wonderful people, cute little bars. Best part of Sri Lanka for me!
Mirissa beach is beautiful with nice white sand, good for surfers but also non-surfers. In the evening the beach bars offers cocktails and sea food (although avoid buying rare species...).
Too Many restaurants from my point of view, but still, it was nice. The beach on the left was nice for surfing.main beach is clean and quier
Mirissa Beach has all you need for a great holiday by the sea. Several good restaurants, big wawes and easy going atmosphere.
Long and clean beach with all necessary service! Friendly people and a lot of sun beds. Waves vary from day to day. A place I never want to leave.

A nice beach to relax and have a drink or two in the evening. There just one or two points of public entry to the beach. All other entry points are through the restaurants by the ocean. This is a very narrow beach with almost no space between the restaurant seating are and the ocean.
Gorgeous beach with stunning views - lots to do, and at night all the restaurants serve fresh seafood BBQed in front of you.

Probably the best beach in Sri Lanka. Quite touristy and lots of beach bars around. I can not understand what people always have with the East Coast - the beaches in Trincomalee are dirty for the most part.

Mirissa beach is very inviting. It's A unique  beach of very clean water. An great place to unwind oneself in the breeze coming from blue water. I spent more than two weeks there in last October and November. It's a great experience !
The beach is excellent. I stayed there for three days and can't complain about anything. It isn't crowded nor deserted. Night life on the beach is wonderful too.

We came to Mirissa for whale watching but also enjoyed the nice beach during our short stay. The beach is nice but with quite high waves, i.e. perfect for playing with the waves close to shore, but not really for swimming as there are strong currents (the next bay has much calmer water for swimming and is only a short walk away). The beach has unfortunately lost a lot of charm as it is very developed with accommodation, bars etc along its stretch and only 50m from shore. It is therefore not the place for a quiet holiday but nice enough for a short stay.

Great beach - clean sand and a good choice of beach bars/restaurants (albeit a bit samey in each of them) The sea is fun if a little powerful for younger children as the waves can be quite high and strong. We enjoyed our 5 night break there... Just don't stay at Central Beach Inn - eat there instead!
Stunning beach with a lovely little snorkelling area by the rock groyne. Super cute changing area and great bar. Truly beautiful.

A fairly busy beach with a selection of beach bars and restaurants, there are also a number of places to rent a surfboard and ticket touts for whale watching and day trips. It was clean, I didn't see any rubbish. I give this average as I've seen better beaches in Thailand.
There are lovely little bays, and the slightly longer main bay. Every beach down here seems good for Swimmingpool.

Lots of activities available and a fantastic environment! You can rent surfboards, water scooters, go diving or whale watching. Good restaurants and many hotels/hostels and such. Not so much party, so I guess better for couples or family's.

I really enjoyed Mirissa Beach, especially Secret Beach. For starters, it's a really clean stretch of beach and not teeming with people. There were hardly any vendors, just a great big golden puppy who was super friendly and jumped me in the water. Waves were a bit high when I went.

I've been to best beaches and worst beaches in Sri Lanka but mirissa beach is good one but suffering from local food suppliers. The huge open sand area is covered with tables of so called "restaurants". If you are not rave party person don't think about enjoying this beach especially at night. It is very hard to enjoy tranquility as these restaurants pumping electronic music at you making whole beach noisy.

Excellent sandy beach – thought it was the perfect size and has everything you want without being over developed or over commercialised. Manages to maintain some charm and chilled out feeling, which is great.  Some really nice beach bars / restaurants along the beach where you can use sunbeds and parasols without charge if you drink or eat something from the restaurant. Our favourite was the Mirissa Eye as it was mid-way along the beach and in a fairly decent spot for body boarding and playing around in the surf. Only downside is that the main beach is not much great for swimming unless you are a strong swimmer and get beyond the surf – but if you walk east and into the next bay (a couple of minutes walk), then this bay is more sheltered and suitable for swimming. The surf is quite strong along the main beach – the biggest waves are in the corner at the west end of the bay.  Would be great for surfing, but not good for swimming. There are plenty of bar / restaurants along the beach and quite a few of them hire out boggie boards at reasonable prices. Plenty of tuk-tuks available to get to other places as well – seems to have a set 200 rupee fare for anywhere within Mirissa itself. If you don’t want to be disturbed by music playing until the early hours of the morning (especially at the weekends) then do not stay right on the beach – you’d be better staying somewhere a little bit inland and either walking in or taking a tuk-tuk.
Nice beach, clean, clear water. Many different cafes on the beach. During the day good for lunch and drinks, at night for cocktails and dinner.

hotel was under construction and the services were poor.took so long time to serve the breakfast.most terrible thing was that some of our family members did not received what they have ordered, even after informing them for several times.

We've been fortunate enough to travel the world extensively and in our opinion Mirissa is not a world class beach. It is spoilt by too many buildings directly on the beach (so that you can rarely see the beach from the road); a horrendously busy road with drivers who are constantly using their horns; and discarded plastic bottles / cans on the beach (including on what should be a lovely rocky outcrop) and even worse on the roadside. We came here to do a whale watching trip and then quickly moved on.

Mirissa Beach is a lovely place to hang out and swimm... really lovely  beach... but the food isn't even close to be sri lankan and it's usually 3 - 4times higher then it should be... try the main road food stales :)

We came to Mirissa and were shocked at how small this beach is.  You can walk it in less than 2 minutes... The better beaches are outside Mirissa in either direction.  Go to Kogalla Beach - amazing!  And skip Mirissa Beach (unless you want surfing and whale watching trips to the deep sea).

This may get busy with tourists from time to time but it's simply a stunning arc of sand with two small islands either end. There's a lovely quieter bay just east of the main beach where there is also some decent beginners surf on a decent swell. The other surf point is the right hander at the west end of the beach. Great sand and good body surfing and swimming.

Mirissa beach is a younger crowd beach with many surfers. Ithas some shade under the trees where you can relax. There's many restaurant on the beach serving good seafood. The sand was nicer here than Unawatuna. We only had booked one night but would have loved to stay longer.

A piece of heavenly scenery of ocean and white rolling waves with yellow sand and many eateries. from this beach you can book a whale watching trip or snorkeling in a glass bottomed boat. Just off the beach there are stores of all kinds with real bargains.A must visit area.

We stayed 8 nights in Mirissa (7 - 15 December). The first three nights in beautiful villa Siri Wedimadura, behind the bay in the direction of the harbour and a 5 minutes walk from the beach. Staying here, I really liked Mirissa: nice beach, perfect swimming area, nice restaurants, candles on the table at night etc. The other five nights we stayed at hotel Palace Mirissa, closer to the beach but tucked away at the hill on the west side of the bay. A very nice hotel, but here I started to hate Mirissa because of the ludicrous noise the beach parties produce every single night until at least 4 pm. Such a shame...
The beach has some good shacks but watch your bill, tried to be ripped off in a few of them
👌 👍 very beautiful beach, good water, nice sand 😊, and big 🌊 waves. Good place for 🏄 surf, relaxing. Nice restaurant on the beach.

Pretty busy, lots of beach shack restaurants serving cold drinks and variable quality food. Most offer the local catch to be cooked as requested. Despite the popularity of the beach it's kept very clean and tidy. Excellent atmosphere as the sun goes down.

Absolutely stunning beach. You can go in quite deep into the water, away from where the waves break. It is very calm. I must say far superior to unawatuna. Try to stay at Club paradise its slap bang on the beach. Lovely restaurents on the beach serving all manner of food, quite reasonable pricing. For the night owls they have parties in some of the restaurents which go on till dawn.

After spending time at both Unawatuna and Mirissa beach,  i must say the beach at Mirissa is so much better. The sand there are smoother and also the beach is around 1km or longer. Perfect for sunbathing,  swim or surf. There are plenty of choices for food on the beach in the evening.

The Mirissa beach is my favorite place in Sri Lanka. There is lots of different kind of restaurants and hotel on the beach. A lot of young people and surfers. The atmosphere is really relaxed and all the people were really nice.

We loved Mirissa Beach already 12 years ago, when we've been here last time (before the tsunami), and we still love it, although it went through a tremendous change in the last few years. There are so many places to stay and even more Restaurants along this beach. At night, there is going on something over here!
Great beach, you can walk the full length with lots of beach bars! Watch out for tide it comes in quick :)

There´s some good cafés, bars, and restaurants right at this lovely beach. View is great, and you can chill at the beach or take a swim (note: only in designated area as currents are quite strong). There´s also some surf (point break) at one end of the beach which is no beginner spot. Mostly solid right handers, a few left handers. Café: Try the Sea Breeze Café. They also have great sandwiches and a yummy curry (freshly made). Restaurant: We really liked the Zephyr (more international kitchen, but also fresh fish), and the burger was/is great.
The Indian Ocean looks awesome. A walk along beach is a great stress buster. A must visit for a quiet beach time

we came 10 years ago and Mirissa is no longer what is was. many sunbeds everywhere, many bars, too many people, horrible concreted hotels, go away there are some nice unspoiled beaches a bit more far in down south. we came to make discover the place to our friends but we didn't like to stay
Clean beach, good for swimming and relaxing. There are a lot of restaurants on the beach that serve all the day

the beach is ok but pretty busy, lots of whale trips etc there are plenty bars with sun loungers if this is what your after,the better bars were at the surf side of the beach,swimming was easier here than tTangalle area.
It is very touristic, but that makes it have more offers and it was the only beach where you had the restaurant tables on the sand. Totally worth it!

We stayed in Mirissa for 5 days after a busy week beforehand exploring Sri Lanka. The beach is beautiful, with lots of restaurants and places to have drinks whilst watching the sunset. There are also lots of free sun loungers which is useful. Busier than some other beaches along the coast but lovely nonetheless.

Mirissa Beach is amazing.The unpredictable behavior of the waves scare and generate interest at the same time,you just wanna dive more and more.It's hard just to swim there,but if you visit a small bay on the other side of the beach,you'll find the ocean in a deep stillness.Very good place to swim.

Lots of great bars and restaurants - some with great music, some horrible depending on your taste.  Good digging sand for those with children.  Entertainment sitting with a beer watching surfers at sea and hermit crabs scuttling about on the sand.  No hawkers.  Utterly relaxing.  Lifeguards.
Great beach for surfers with humongous waves. There's a small natural pool created by Coral Reefs at the end of the beach what is a sanctuary.
Great beach with plenty of restaurants, cafe's and a nightlife and fine waterfront dining
There is plenty to do and see. Whale watching was great and saw a number of whales. The beach is lovely and great swimming. Better in December though when the surf is up....
I just loved jumping into threse amazing and powerful waves all day long. Hiding in the shadows of mangroves from the sun, and drinking a beer in the surfers club in the night.

Very nice and tidy beach with lot of options to have a good meal, especially on evenings, when fresh sea food is offered. We've been there on pre-season so it was not so busy, but you can expect lot of tourists during regular season.
Super chill beach, lovely sea and waves, nice huts with food, music and cocktails. All you need for a holiday :)

It has all the standard cliches of a perfect little beach.It is expanding rapidly though and it probably won't be long before it becomes over developed like so many other places. Lots of accommodation on the beach or in the quiet back blocks.

Great for learning to surfing, not so for sunbathing. Waves can get strong suddenly and difficult to find the calm spot for sunbathing. Wouldn't say it's the most beautiful beach in Sri Lanka although I have not seen enough of the rest. Had much better beach experiences in other countries though.

Beautiful clear water, huge sea turtles, whales and dolphins nearby. Nice for bodyboarding near the shore and many surf points on and around Mirissa beach. The village is small and there are a lot of Paddy fields inland a nice lake nearby for short boat rides on local boats. It was not too touristic like Unawatuna/Hikkaduwa but not boring like Tangalle. By far, our favorite beach in Sri Lanka!

It's a beautiful part of Sri Lanka...south of the country, facing the mighty Indian Ocean. A great place for surfing, snorkelling and whale watching. However, our whale watching trip was a disaster , a brief sighting with loads of retching and vomiting on the boat. Also, the quality of food leaves a lot to be desired.

The beach is not too big, but there are a lot of restaurants with free sunbeds, where you can chillout whole day. We visited the beach in November, when it was only few tourists, but I can imagine that it can get very crowded in high season. The sea has a waves, good for bodysurf, but you can swim as well after you overcome few waves. It is also very good for small children because the water is shallow for several meters before it goes deep.  In the evening there a great choice of fresh fish for good price. To compare a fish in Mirissa cost approx. 900 Rs. and for the same size fish we were charged 1500 Rs. in Unawatuna and it was  not the fresh catch.
Fun beach with tons of restaurants around to eat at. A little crowded at times but overall it's a good place to relax and chill.
Fantastic beach x quiet , clean and warm sea, bodyboarding good , food places great , friendly restaurants x

A place where you can go to the deep see and watch dolphins and whales. We were lucky to see both. The ship leaves around 7 in the morning and comes back around 11am. Charges per head per adult is 6,500 SLR.

It's a wide beach, with lots of places to eat, stay, chill, hang out and party. Beach break is close out, so only fun for swimmers and wannabe bodyboarders. Pointbreak, reef is good when the swell comes from the right direction. All righthanders, only if the swell changes there is a left (look out for the rocks) To stay... if you like quiet, go somewhere else (Polhena and take a tuktuk for 500rps) to Mirissa.

this was the best beach that we stayed in whilst in Lanka. The surf was good for learning to surf, the sea was warm and the san golden. it was clean and it has a beautiful landscape. there are enough restaurants to eat out in a diffrerent place every night but not too many that the beach is crowded. at night the palm trees llight up with fairy lights and its just beautiful
Really nice beach with a lot of places to sit, drink juices, eat rotti and relax. Waves aren't so high, so you can swim with kids here

We had stayed in Unawatuna , the drive from our place to the Mirissa beach is a worthy scenic. Mirissa is one of the most prettiest beach in the near vicinity. The water is extremely clear, turquoise blue...the sand is like butter..soft and soothing. A long walk along the beach with waves kissing yr feet is an experience, fall in love. There are loads of shacks, offering happy hour on booze accompanying the fresh catch of fish n sea food..they will grill it to perfection and to your choice... Its a very calm and relaxing beach, perfect for couples or family time....for us we were a group of frnds. This place was our place for solace after the whole day of sight seeing. Good spot for swimming and surfing. There is a small island aswell...gotta walk through the sea to reach it...lil adventure for oneself. Overall for us it was a place worth coming back for.
The beach is really nice. Great for swimming and maybe beginner surfing. There are a bunch of cafes and restaurants as well!

Mirissa is a little gem of a place that was one of the highlights of my trip.  I visited in October which was the end of the low season / shoulder season I guess.  I'm certain the beach gets a lot busier in December / January however we found that the swimming was great in late October and the beach wasn't crowded at all.  Nice chilled out atmosphere with some great seafood on offer in the evenings - there are plenty of bars and restaurants but I thought it was a good balance (not too built up) and still some quieter spots with not many people around.  Some of the bars down the far west end of the beach played stupidly loud music (with no customers) until the wee hours which was an annoyance down that end (stayed at Surf View for a couple of nights) but aside from that this is a wonderful beach to visit.  Staying off the beach is a good choice for value - everything is accessible and plenty of guesthouses 5 mins walk back off the beach.

Mirissa beach is a popular stopping place for many tourists for some beach time, perhaps during a busy travel itinerary around Sri Lanka or maybe for the surfing and the chance to go whale spotting from the nearby harbour. It's backed by the main road which runs close to the beach at it's east End giving rise to  claims in some quarters that the West end is better and quieter though it isn't the quiet, unspoilt and idyllic beach that I've seen it described as in some guides. There are times when it can be busy especially in the late afternoon and evening, though when we visited in April it seemed noticeably quieter in the mornings. It is backed by a string of beach bars, some quite reasonable, one or two quite poor and most of which offer food. Many display fresh fish in front of the bar lit by oil lamps to offer to passing visitors in the evenings with seating both under cover and in some cases at the head of the beach. Some of these start to close down by the second half of April ahead of worsening weather and before this the best time to eat in the evening is before 9pm. They don't stay open as long as many European bars to serve food. Watch where you sit when the tide comes in too and especially where you leave your bags because in some cases the water could reach your feet as you eat at which times a close look at the sand might reveal small crabs emerging to clear the holes that concealed them and to look for food. In fact one of the periodic evening attractions is the sight of baby turtles making their way down the beach, sometimes betrayed by groups of people with torches watching them pass. One night I heard a small knocking sound below me and looking down saw one baby turtle head butting the leg of my chair. The quality of the sand is pretty good. There was a little rubbish visible at the further part if the East end of the beach (on the left as you face the sea) and at each end the sand was a little coarser. Across much of the beach though my wife described it as 'memory foam' sand for the way it seemed to cushion each step. The sea isn't ideal for swimming, with good wave action and in some parts a noticeable undertow that could make it especially difficult for small children. At the West end is the HQ for the local coastguard with a lookout point for lifeguards. At the far West of the the beach, beyond some rocks, the waves are much more pronounced and this is a favoured spot for surfers, with boards available for rent at several points along the beach while at the East end is a small islet that can be reached on foot easily unless the tide is well in. There are steps, no longer in good condition but easily traversed that take you up to the top. Most people probably do this though the view isn't good enough to detain most people for very long. If the tide is low enough, take a few moments to watch the antics of the crabs that occupy the rocks below it as they jump from rock to rock or seem to skitter across the water to reach their next. If you want a beach bar, some surfing, a chance to go whale spotting and don't mind sharing the beach with others looking for the same then Mirissa makes a good place to stay. If you are looking for golden sand and solitude it might offer less than you hoped and there are alternatives.

Mirissa Beach is certainly beautiful.  The surf can be a bit rough at times, but we still found swimming to be an enjoyable if tiring experience.  Unfortunately, the businesses on the beach are ruining the beauty.  Yes, tourists like to dine in candlelight on the beach.  I admit that we did enjoy it, but when you start to think about the fact that this beach is a prime nesting ground for sea turtles, including leatherback sea turtles, you realize that by putting tables and chairs up to the water line, the turtles no longer have anywhere to nest.  We heard reports of many turtles attempting to come up onto the beach to lay eggs.  These turtles did not get very far before they were disturbed by the commercial presence.  I do hope that the community and future tourists can work together to fix this problem and help Mirissa Beach live up to its potential at the same time.

Mirissa Beach is an inigma. It is very much a destination sought after by young and old, surfer, diver or sunbather. However there are certain pitfalls that some may dislike whilst others probably are indifferent. The setting across the bay with long beaches, turquoise waters and palm trees is amazing especially at sunset. Beware of restaurant touts in the evening though as after eating in four establishments along the beach with enchanting fairy lights and inviting menu's, we were served meals that reflected little of what was touted to be a great special !! Fish is bought in 'fresh from the Maldives' straight to your table is supposedly what one is offered. Why then re-fried calamari and crabs with no meat served with shell off ??? Choose restaurants carefully as lights, ambience and offer of Happy hour drink specials disguise the food quality in some places. Surf is extremely dangerous for inexperienced swimmers, older folk and children. Backwash is very powerful even when the tide is coming in. Water temp is great though and the area is good for photographers. Be extremely careful when trying to cross the road from the beach into town (?) as Tuk tuks, buses, taxis and trucks have scant regard for the prescribed speed limit nor which side of the road is supposed to be used. Driving up one side against the traffic is normal here as is making U-turns directly into oncoming traffic, and it is a surprise that there have not been many more accidents. There are many very nice shopkeepers in the main road, but also very many who are so arrogant and are doing you a favour by serving you. Not sure we will return here again as there are many other equally good places to visit in this wonderful country.

However, Mirissa is a small and rather quiet city (village?) with no real party places or shopping street as we could see in Hikkaduwa for instance. But if you are just looking for a not so touristic, not so expensive (yet) place just to relax and take it easy for few days, then I would recommend Mirissa!
